speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank the Council of Presidential Advisers for their deliberations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On 18 February, just five weeks ago, I started my Budget 2020 speech setting out what we must do to combat the threats posed by the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At that time, there were 800 confirmed cases outside of China.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I said then that the Government was monitoring the situation closely, so that we can and are prepared to do more if the situation warrants it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak is a battle on many fronts – medical, economic and social.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, on the medical front, countries are taking extraordinary measures to contain the spread of the virus, so their healthcare systems are not overwhelmed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many countries have implemented lockdowns, while the US has declared a national emergency.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, we are doing everything we can to keep you and your families safe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the severity of the virus outbreak grew worldwide, we stepped up our measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These have, so far, helped to keep the number of cases at manageable levels during the first wave.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ministers Gan Kim Yong and Lawrence Wong gave comprehensive updates on the further measures that we have put in place and gave us vivid and moving accounts in their Ministerial Statements yesterday.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We thank Minister Gan and Minister Wong, and the members of the task force, for your leadership.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On behalf of all of us in the Government and in this House, let us express our deepest appreciation to our dedicated and professional healthcare workers, and all our frontline officers, for working courageously and tirelessly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, as much as we try, the Prime Minister and Senior Minister Teo have warned earlier that the COVID-19 pandemic is likely to take at least a year to be resolved, and the economic repercussions would last even longer.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The world is seeing successive waves of infection and importation of infections.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must be prepared to take further tougher measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yet measures on the medical front to contain the pandemic, both in Singapore and around the world, have made the second front of the battle – the economic front, even more difficult.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These public health measures have caused severe economic disruptions and uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As more countries implement their measures, the economic disruptions will be wider, deeper and more prolonged.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global economy is now facing both a supply and demand shock.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the supply side, supply chains have been disrupted as locked down workers are unable to work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With highly integrated global supply chains, a disruption in any one part of the chain or in any one country will have knock-on effects worldwide.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the demand side, aggregate demand has fallen as people stay home and curtail spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Consumer and business confidence is plunging in the face of growing uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Global growth forecasts for 2020 have fallen sharply compared to just a month ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has downgraded its 2020 global growth forecast three times since January 2019 and flagged that a further downgrade is imminent in April.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It added that it expects a recession at least as bad as during the 2008 global financial crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Global financial markets are being roiled by the mounting uncertainties and cutback in economic activity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Stock markets have come down from their peak some weeks ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The key volatility indices in Europe and the US, which some call the "fear index", briefly reached levels last seen during the global financial crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Credit has tightened across the world, and the US yield curve has fallen below 1% for the first time in history.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The disruptions around the world will significantly curtail global demand, disrupt supply chains and possibly lead to financial shocks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As an open economy that is highly integrated with the global economy, we will be deeply impacted by these global shocks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The outbreak has impacted broad swathes of our economy, with some more affected than others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The most badly affected sectors are our aviation and tourism sectors, as international visitor arrivals in Singapore have nearly ground to a halt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Consumer-facing sectors such as food services, retail trade and land transport have been significantly affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The outward-oriented sectors such as manufacturing and wholesale trade have also been affected as external demand falls and supply chains get disrupted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken on the medical and economic fronts of the battle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is a test of our social cohesion and our psychological resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While people are understandably fearful, we must not surrender to this fear or panic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will take all the social and economic measures we need to keep our people safe, keep our economy growing and prepare ourselves for the recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, more than ever, we need Singaporeans to be strong and ride through these challenges together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a public health crisis, an economic shock and a social test.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will challenge our resilience as individuals and as a society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In such extraordinary times, it is collective acts of kindness and courage that make a people extraordinary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How Singapore manages this, and whether we emerge stronger from this, will define us as a people and nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: My last Budget was called the Unity Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have decided to call this Supplementary Budget the Resilience Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It reflects our determination that Singapore and Singaporeans remain resilient in the face of these challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Come what may, no matter how daunting the challenge at hand, we will bounce back, stronger and more united than ever, as we weather this storm together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In economic terms alone, this will likely be the worst economic contraction since independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last month, I committed $6.4 billion in the Unity Budget towards the Stabilisation and Support Package, the Care and Support Package and to support our frontline agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is over seven times of the first tranche.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a landmark package and a necessary response to a unique situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Resilience Budget focuses on three key areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, save jobs, support workers and protect livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, strengthen economic and social resilience so that we can emerge intact and stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Before I get into the details, I thank NTUC, the Singapore Business Federation as well as many citizens and groups, who have given us valuable feedback.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Your views have shaped our responses to the challenges posed by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our immediate priority is to save jobs, support our workers and protect livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over one third of the Resilience Budget is dedicated to this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even then, we cannot prevent an economic recession as the external health and economic situation will evolve beyond our control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But it will help us mitigate the extent of the downturn and more importantly, help save jobs and protect livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For workers who are currently employed, our top priority is to help them stay employed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the Unity Budget, I introduced the Jobs Support Scheme and enhanced the Wage Credit Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Both are focused on preserving and enhancing jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The situation now calls for bolder and more aggressive moves to save jobs and keep workers in employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will significantly enhance and extend the Jobs Support Scheme to provide more impactful and sustained wage support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms in the food services sector will receive higher support at 50% of wages and firms in the aviation and tourism sectors, which are the most badly affected sectors, will be supported at 75% of wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will raise the monthly qualifying wage ceiling from $3,600 to $4,600, which is the median wage in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also extend the Jobs Support Scheme for another two quarters till the end of 2020, so employers will receive a total of three tranches of payouts in May, July and October this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is more than twice the level of support provided during the global financial crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With this support from the Government, I urge employers to do your part to hold on to your workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhancements to the Jobs Support Scheme and Wage Credit Scheme will support workers employed in our enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second group of individuals whom we seek to support is self-employed persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the last few weeks, I received feedback from the Labour Movement and many self-employed persons calling for stronger support for the self-employed, who have less income security and whose livelihoods may be worse affected during this period of economic uncertainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This group has been harder to reach as they work in diverse industries, many occupations, with varying working arrangements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They include taxi and private hire car drivers, real estate agents, media and art freelancers, and sport coaches.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the Unity Budget, we were able to support some of them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For taxi and private hire car drivers, we partnered with NTUC, the operators and LTA to deliver help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They comprise the largest group of self-employed persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also introduced the Self-Employed Person Training Support Scheme to provide a training allowance of $7.50 per hour to self-employed persons attending courses under the SkillsFuture Series or select training programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this Resilience Budget, we plan to provide direct cash assistance to more self-employed persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of them have less means and family support, and need help to tide over this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have discussed with the Minister for Manpower and NTUC Secretary-General on developing a Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme, or SIRS, for this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible self-employed persons will receive $1,000 a month for nine months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhanced training allowance is on top of the already generous training subsidies, which cover up to 90% of fees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, trainees will be able to tap on their SkillsFuture Credit to further offset the course fees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through these schemes, and with our many partners, we hope to provide a safety net for the self-employed during this outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Looking ahead, we will see how we can better support self-employed persons in strengthening their financial security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For lower income workers, including self-employed persons, we have been supplementing their incomes through the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme (WIS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this Unity Budget, I announced that Singaporeans on Workfare in 2019 would receive a one-off Workfare Special Payment amounting to 20% of their 2019 payout, with a minimum payout of $100.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Jobs Support Scheme, Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme and enhanced Workfare Special Payment will help to sustain the employment and salaries of our workers, with more financial support for workers who earn less.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from employees and self-employed, I will provide more help for jobseekers to find employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, first-time jobseekers may be concerned about the current job market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include our students who have just graduated or are graduating from ITE, Polytechnics and Universities this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will introduce the SGUnited Traineeships programme to provide our young people with opportunities to gain valuable work experience, while giving an added boost for employers to emerge stronger from this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our agencies have been planning our manpower needs early and there is a range of jobs which we need to fill in emerging areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will accelerate hiring plans to fill these roles, while giving our people meaningful employment opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will recruit for long-term roles in the public service and sectoral partner institutions, in areas such as social services, early childhood education, and ICT, so that we can enhance our provision of essential services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also offer short-term, temporary jobs to handle the increase in COVID-19 related operations, such as health declaration assistants, temporary management support officers and the Transport Ambassadors announced by the Minister for Transport earlier this week.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we are working with the Singapore Business Federation and Trade Associations and Chambers to identify private sector job opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These may come from businesses recruiting for the eventual recovery, or with short-term manpower needs due to disruptions in labour supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened to see that companies, such as Micron and SMRT, have already come on board the SGUnited Jobs initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: WSG will launch an SGUnited Jobs virtual career fair tomorrow with more than 2,200 job vacancies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will focus on short-term temporary jobs that are immediately available.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Jobseekers looking for longer term roles can consider the wider range of jobs advertised on my CareersFuture.sg.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The best way to safeguard the well-being of our people is by supporting them to stay employed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But as the impact of COVID-19 on our economy deepens, some workers will lose their jobs or see their incomes significantly reduced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, the ComCare scheme provides assistance to those who fall into financial hardships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will exercise more flexibility when considering applications for ComCare during this period, to ensure that affected Singaporeans can get help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some families may require help urgently, while waiting for the new help measures to kick in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will set up a Temporary Relief Fund in the month of April, to provide them with immediate financial assistance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be available at our Social Service Offices and Community Centres.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also introduce a COVID-19 Support Grant at our Social Service Offices from May to September this year, to help our workers who become unemployed due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Low- and middle income employees who lose their jobs can receive a grant of $800 per month for three months, to tide them over while they find new jobs or go for training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In total, I will set aside $145 million for the new schemes and increased flexibilities to ComCare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singaporeans are concerned about how they will pay their bills and household expenses if their livelihoods are affected during this uncertain period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will put more cash in the hands of all families to help them cope.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will provide additional help for families with young children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will triple the additional cash payout given to each Singaporean parent with at least one young Singaporean child, from $100 to $300.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For lower-wage workers, the enhanced Workfare Special Payment I mentioned earlier will provide them $3,000 in cash this year for their household needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further help needy Singaporeans with their daily expenses, and in particular, the cost of food, I will triple the Grocery Vouchers given to them this year from $100 to $300.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with the $100 which will be given to them next year, needy Singaporeans will receive $400 in Grocery Vouchers over 2020 and 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also provide the earlier-announced one-off PAssion Card top-up for Singaporeans aged 50 years and above in cash instead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is to avoid the need to queue at top-up stations during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, the Government will partner the community to strengthen the network of support around our workers and families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Self-Help Groups and Community Development Councils (CDCs) have stepped up their efforts to help families and vulnerable groups through their own assistance schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will support them to do more, and better meet the needs of their communities and residents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will double the grant given to Self-Help Groups to $20 million over two years and increase the additional grant given to CDCs from $20 million to $75 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Labour Movement is also doing its part to help our workers and self-employed persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last week, NTUC announced the $25 million NTUC Care Fund (COVID-19), which is jointly funded by NTUC, unions and the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fund will provide one-off relief of up to $300 to low and middle income union members.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yesterday, NTUC announced a $4 million top-up to the Self-Employed Person Training Support Scheme, to give union members an additional training allowance of up to $1 per hour.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be on top of the enhanced training allowance rates of $10 per hour which I announced earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our social service agencies also do good work supporting vulnerable groups in our community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will support them to adopt digital tools to continue to reach out and serve their clients during this period, through the existing VWOs-Charities Capability Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Social service agencies can reach out to the National Council of Social Service to apply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, the Government will exercise greater flexibility on its fees and loans during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will freeze all Government fees and charges for one year, from 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will apply to all fees for Government services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help graduates who are worried about having to pay off their student loans while finding jobs in this economic climate, I will suspend all loan repayment and interest charges for one year, from 1 June 2020 to 31 May 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will apply to all graduates who have taken a Government loan for their University and Polytechnic studies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also suspend all late payment charges on HDB mortgage arrears for three months, for those who are struggling with their mortgage payments during this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: HDB will continue to exercise flexibility when providing assistance during this period, through existing measures such as deferring payment of loan instalments for six months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To summarise, we will protect jobs, support our workers, and protect livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will do this by helping employees stay employed; stepping up support for the self-employed and lower-income; creating more opportunities for jobseekers; helping unemployed workers tide over this period; and helping our households with their expenses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation closely and are prepared to take swift action to do more if needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second thrust of the Resilience Budget is to help businesses overcome the immediate challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Resilience Budget will address the three Cs on the mind of every business owner now – cashflow, cost and credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For businesses, "cash is king" and many have called for more timely assistance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As some have told me in Mandarin, "远水救不了近火", or "distant water cannot put out a nearby fire", we are doing our best to flow the payouts under the wage support schemes quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By the end of this month, more than $600 million would have been disbursed to employers under the former Wage Credit Scheme parameters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By the end of May, a total of $5.6 billion would have been paid out under the Jobs Support Scheme and the Wage Credit Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The agencies are working hard to bring forward an additional $500 million of wage credits under the enhanced parameters, from September to end-June.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further ease cash flow for businesses in the immediate period, I will grant an automatic deferment of income tax payments for companies and self-employed persons, for three months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Instead, income tax payments will only be payable from July 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In other words, if you paid money last year and need to pay tax this year, you will delay paying for three months so you can use the cash to meet other urgent needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So income tax payments will only start from August 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Employees may approach IRAS, if they need help with their income tax payments and wish to avail themselves of this arrangement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Where the cost is within the Government’s control, we will do our best to help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will, therefore, enhance the Property Tax Rebate which I announced in the Unity Budget, by raising the amount and covering more types of properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a big enhancement, from the 15% to 30% Property Tax Rebate announced in the Unity Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses in other non-residential properties such as offices and industrial properties are also affected by the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will now grant a Property Tax Rebate of 30% for the year 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly urge landlords to fully pass on the rebate to tenants, by reducing rentals, to directly ease the cash flow and cost pressures faced by tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many businesses have pointed out that it will be a lose-lose situation if landlords do not support their tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After all, if tenants fail, the properties will be empty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So my message to landlords is: do your part, chip in, and give additional help to tenants who are more badly hit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will lead by example in supporting tenants by enhancing rental waivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other Government agencies, like HDB and the National Arts Council, will provide two months of rental waiver to eligible tenants, up from half a month announced in the Unity Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All other non-residential tenants will receive half a month of rental waiver.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, as mentioned earlier, I will freeze all Government fees and charges by one year, from 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will further enhance our financing schemes so that even the hardest-hit businesses can continue to have access to credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I earlier enhanced the Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS) – SME Working Capital Loan to alleviate SMEs' cash flow concerns, and introduced the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme (TBLP) for enterprises in the tourism sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support businesses’ trade financing needs, I will enhance the EFS – Trade Loan, by increasing the maximum quantum from $5 million to $10 million, and increasing the Government’s risk-share from up to 70%, to 80%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also announce subsidies to businesses for loan insurance premiums under the Loan Insurance Scheme, from 50% to 80%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will expand the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme (TBLP) to all enterprises, and increase the maximum supported loan from $1 million to $5 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SMEs that require support beyond the TBLP can continue to tap on the EFS – SME Working Capital Loan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The maximum loan quantum for this will be further enhanced, from $600,000 to $1 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we will work with Participating Financial Institutions to defer capital payments for one year on the EFS-Working Capital Loan and the TBLP loans if requested by businesses, subject to assessment by Participating Financial Institutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help to support good companies with strong capabilities, and catalyse private sector loan capital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the situation is fluid, we will seek to provide help where the credit needs are more acute.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Concurrently, MAS is working with banks and insurers to see how best to help businesses and individuals facing cash flow challenges with their loan obligations and insurance premium payments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Details of these measures will be announced by MAS and the industry later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All these measures deal with helping people financially.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But there is also an important and complementary part – giving people relief from legal obligations that have arisen because of the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is no fault of theirs that they cannot perform these obligations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, people may have paid deposits for a big gathering that now cannot go ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is not their fault that the gathering cannot go ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government is studying the issue, and the Minister for Law will present a set of measures to deal with this at the next Parliamentary sitting.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On top of the broad-based support to help businesses address the three "C"s, I will provide additional help to specific sectors that are most directly affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Sectors that rely on tourism and international travel have been hit the hardest.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The sharp drop in international visitors has impacted the whole tourism eco-sector, from our airport and airlines, to hotels and attractions and their tenants, to travel agents and bus companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The aviation sector sits at the core of this eco-system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke earlier about countries enacting border control measures to curb the spread of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Around the world, many airlines have responded with steep cuts to their capacity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many airlines unfortunately may not survive the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is the single biggest shock that air hubs and airlines around the world have ever experienced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is more than 40% of last year’s overall revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will have a profound impact on the global aviation sector for years to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Against this backdrop, governments around the world are taking steps to support their carriers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the US administration has indicated its intent to support both US airlines and aerospace manufacturers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: State support for the private sector where there are critical national interests at stake is not unprecedented.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During the Global Financial Crisis, the Americans and Europeans stepped in to support their key financial institutions and other companies in major sectors, to avoid wider contagion to the rest of their economies and preserve key economic assets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Air hubs and airlines with large domestic markets are under stress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our air hub, with only international traffic, faces an even sharper impact from widespread international border closures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Global connectivity is of fundamental importance to Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It links us to the rest of the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are connected by more than 100 airlines to some 380 cities in about 100 countries and territories worldwide.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Air connectivity connects us to families and friends studying, working, and living abroad.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It enables Singapore-based companies to access growth opportunities overseas, and catalyses investments and business location decisions by overseas companies here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The air hub supports other economic sectors, such as tourism, manufacturing and logistics, and anchors aerospace companies like Rolls Royce and Airbus here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Changi Air Hub is an important pillar of our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It makes us an ideal Global-Asia node, where companies all over the world can access opportunities in Asia and companies in Asia can access opportunities around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our aviation sector has significant linkages to the rest of our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If it collapses in a crisis, it will be very hard for the aviation industries to rebuild after the crisis is over, and the recovery of the rest of the economy will be impeded.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must, therefore, ensure that this temporary shock to our air hub does not become a permanent one.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will support our aviation sector to ride out the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help businesses whose activities are based principally in the aviation sector retain their local workers, I will provide an enhanced Jobs Support Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be paid in the same months as the main Jobs Support Scheme pay-outs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This enhancement will cost the Government more than $400 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also introduce a $350 million enhanced aviation support package to fund measures such as rebates on landing and parking charges, and rental relief for airlines, ground handlers and cargo agents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will also allow Singapore to retain a minimum level of connectivity to the world even during the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is critical to enable overseas Singaporeans to return home and keep our supply lines for essential goods open.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SIA Group sits at the heart of our aviation eco-system and anchors our position as an air hub.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2019, SIA Group accounted for over half of passenger traffic and cargo tonnage in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the main hub carrier, SIA links us to the rest of the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many foreign airlines chose to come to Changi because they can tap on SIA's connectivity to the rest of the region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A diminished SIA will undermine our air hub's ability to recover from the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Air travel would eventually resume when COVID-19 comes under control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Until then, SIA will need liquidity to tide over this outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this regard, SIA will benefit from the Enhanced Jobs Support Scheme and the Enhanced Aviation Support Package which will help reduce its operating expenditure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members will be aware that SIA requested a halt to trading of its securities this morning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have been informed that SIA is considering a corporate action, supported by Temasek Holdings and will be making an announcement in due course.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I welcome Temasek's decision to lend support to SIA.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SIA is an outstanding airline and a strategic asset for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through the Government's support for the aviation sector and, if necessary, more direct support measures, we will make sure that SIA is able to come through this in good shape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, this is about preserving the status of our air hub so that it can emerge stronger from this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Riding out this storm will require patience and adjustments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With resilience, I am sure our air hub will be able to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from the aviation sector, several other tourism-related industries, from hotels and attractions to travel agents and bus companies have had a difficult time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond sectors that depend directly on international travel, sectors that involve a high level of human interaction will take a hit from the recently-announced safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Food services is one such sector, with more Singaporeans avoiding crowds and choosing to eat at home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our taxi and private hire car or PHC drivers have seen their takings fall significantly, as more people work from home and as visitorship falls.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible taxi hirers and PHC drivers will continue to receive the Special Relief Fund payments of $300 per vehicle per month until end-September.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also extend support to the taxi and PHC operators.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help private bus owners, I will provide them with a one-year road tax rebate and a six-month waiver of parking charges at government-managed parking facilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the arts and culture sector, we will provide an additional $55 million support package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will save jobs and support upskilling and digitalisation of the sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will provide additional support to major companies and leading arts groups, which are integral to our vibrant arts scene.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help safeguard jobs and retain capabilities in our local arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will enhance the National Arts Council’s Capability Development Scheme for the Arts, to deepen skills and support the professional development of arts organisations and practitioners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we will step up digitalisation efforts, by building the sector's digital capabilities, and establishing more digital arts platforms which can reach out to new audiences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third thrust of the Resilience Budget is to build resilience in our economy and society, as we battle this downturn, and build capabilities for when the eventual recovery comes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us not face COVID-19 with fear and despair, but with a spirit of resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This means keeping our eyes on the future and staying the course, even in the face of hardship and adversity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will build economic resilience at all levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the national level, we will continue to invest in our long-term capabilities for growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak has reinforced the importance of investing in R&D to prepare for critical challenges – such as in managing pandemics and ensuring food security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has enabled Singapore to become one of the first countries to successfully develop COVID-19 test kits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An example is the Fortitude 2.0 kit developed by A*STAR and Tan Tock Seng Hospital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is currently used in nine local hospitals and has been sent to several countries including China, Myanmar and the Philippines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to make steady investments in R&D, under our masterplan for Research, Innovation and Enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will provide more details on this towards the end of the financial year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has also emphasised the importance of having resilient supplies of food and other essential items.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are building up our national stockpile of health supplies, including masks and hand sanitisers, so that we will continue to be well-stocked.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some may be concerned about the impact on our food supplies, arising from supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have in place a robust, multi-pronged strategy, to ensure that we continue to have a stable supply of safe food.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we did with water, we are strengthening our food resilience for the long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under our "30 by 30" vision, we aim to produce 30% of our nutritional needs by 2030, up from less than 10% today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the industry level, all firms have a part to play in building economic resilience, as we prepare for recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why we introduced the SG Together Enhancing Enterprise Resilience (STEER) programme, which supports industry-led initiatives to help companies tide over today’s economic uncertainties and build longer-term capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will now match $1 for every $2 raised by Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) or business groups for qualifying initiatives, doubling the earlier matching rate of $1 for $4.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage more TACs and industry groups to join us in helping the business community emerge stronger and better from this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses should continue to make use of this downtime to digitalise, restructure, and transform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, they can leverage the SMEs Go Digital Programme, the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) and the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will further enhance these programmes to give businesses a boost during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, I will enhance the SMEs Go Digital Programme to provide support for more digital solutions, from basic remote working tools, to more advanced systems.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, I will raise the maximum support levels for PSG and EDG to 80% and 90% respectively to spur transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support our workers to stay resilient, we will enhance our support for skills upgrading.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the individual level, we can all continue to grow and learn in this time of disruption.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SkillsFuture movement is a big part of this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the Unity Budget, I launched the Next Bound of SkillsFuture to further support our people in acquiring new skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SSG has worked with Institutes of Higher Learning and Continuing Education and Training Centres, to allow Singaporeans to make early use of the base $500 SkillsFuture Credit Top-up for their courses from 1 April 2020, ahead of the full implementation date in October.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope this will help many more workers, jobseekers, and self-employed persons make use of the downtime to learn, develop new skills and stay employable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I mentioned earlier that we are spending over a third of this Resilience Budget to save jobs, protect workers and support households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is ultimately about keeping our society strong.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is about giving us a sense that we are in this together, that we will look after those in need and trust in one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But building a strong society is not just about giving more social support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is also about fostering a culture of social responsibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will do what we can to encourage this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the COVID-19 situation develops, we may need to introduce a broader range of safe distancing measures to stop the transmission chain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Everyone must play their part to comply with these measures, for the sake of others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But it may sometimes be costly for employers and households to comply with these measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will provide help where appropriate to mitigate the impact and support responsible behaviour.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, we have provided support for the costs of quarantine accommodation, to mitigate the costs to individuals and families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The outbreak has also been a stark reminder of the need for good public hygiene.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources launched the SG Clean campaign in February to drive higher levels of personal and public hygiene, not just during the COVID-19 outbreak, but beyond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To make a real difference to public health outcomes, we will need the collective action of businesses and individuals alike.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are already offsetting the audit and certification fees for tourism, retail, and food services businesses participating in SG Clean.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also co-fund businesses to undertake professional cleaning of premises which have experienced a confirmed COVID-19 case.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MEWR will share more details in due course.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with the support that we are providing to workers and households, these will help to keep social bonds strong, encourage social responsibility and foster trust in our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To summarise, even as we deal with our immediate challenges, we must keep our sights on the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With our collective creativity and resilience, Singapore can emerge stronger from this, both as an economy and as a society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our reserves are our strategic asset, built up through the discipline and prudence of our people and political leaders, across generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our reserves serve as our bulwark against shocks and crises of an extraordinary nature.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For a nation with no oil, no gas, no gold, no diamonds, or natural resources of any kind, it is remarkable that we have built this up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our prudence and discipline in saving and growing our reserves give us the wherewithal to respond decisively when our nation faces extraordinary circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our founding fathers created a rigorous framework to ensure that such strategic assets are used only for the right purpose.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We amended the Constitution in 1991 to provide for an Elected President who is the custodian of our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under Article 148A of the Constitution, the President can withhold her assent to any Supply Bill if she is of the view that it is likely to draw on Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our principle is that each term of government must live within its means.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Any additional spending that the Government of the day proposes must be funded in a sustainable manner – recurrent expenditures should be funded from recurrent revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Past Reserves can be drawn down only in exceptional circumstances, under a two-key system, if the President, after consulting the Council of Presidential Advisers, agrees with the Government’s proposal to draw on the Past Reserves in exceptional circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Despite political pressure to dip into the reserves, the Government has scrupulously upheld the principle that Past Reserves are to be used only for exceptional circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During that period, the Government also sought the President’s concurrence to use $150 billion of Past Reserves to back the Deposit Guarantee Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I was in MAS at that time when we had to ask for this, and it took us a long time to deliberate on this before we even did that.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic, and the multiple threats it poses to our nation, is the sort of event that we had accumulated reserves for.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have saved up for a rainy day.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic is already a mighty storm, and is still growing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If over the years we had frittered the reserves away, on more immediate but less existential needs, big and small, as some in this House have pressed the Government to do, we would be in a much weaker position today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are experiencing a confluence of multiple external shocks – a pandemic that has triggered many nations to shut their borders, limit exports and halt economic activities in order to fight this pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The economic impact is magnified, as the global economy is already fragile and further weakened by a protracted US-China trade conflict and an oil price war.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, this is not a normal business cycle that we would have anticipated and dealt with using the revenues collected by each term of Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a "black swan" event that comes only once every few decades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In view of the exceptional circumstances, the Government has sought the President's in-principle support to use Past Reserves to fund part of the package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Before my Ministerial Statement, Members heard the President's message to Parliament, delivered on her behalf by the Speaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Unlike the Global Financial Crisis or the Asian Financial Crisis, where both the causes and solutions were economic and financial in nature, this crisis is far more complex, with additional medical, social and psychological dimensions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global economy is also more deeply intertwined with many complex inter-linkages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 situation is fluid and fast-moving, and nobody is quite sure how it will develop.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But because we have prepared ourselves well, Singapore has the resources to meet this crisis with confidence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will use our resources to get through this together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Once again, let me thank the President and Members of the Council of Presidential Advisers for your support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to monitor the situation closely and do more as and when we need to.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Should it become necessary, I am prepared to propose to the President further draws on Past Reserves to deal with the situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I trust that every Member of this House will deeply internalise the mission to be careful stewards of our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The situation remains highly fluid and uncertain, with significant risks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our fiscal position will be affected from both the revenue and expenditure sides.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With a weak GDP outlook, our revenues will be affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While revenues are coming down, our expenditure will be going up, to enable us to respond effectively to the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the past few years, we benefited from unexpected revenue upsides, such as exceptional Statutory Board Contributions from MAS and increased stamp duty collections.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We cannot hope to rely on a repeat of this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Instead, we must be prepared to bear the downsides when they happen.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Because we have been prudent and did not decide to spend all of the surplus that we collected, we are ready to meet such downsides.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can expect significant volatility in the economy and in financial markets in the near future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will need to continue to review our expenditure plans very carefully in this fluid situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must stay nimble and adapt our responses as new developments occur.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will adopt a nimble fiscal posture so that we can quickly channel the resources at hand to the most urgent and important needs of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All of us must remain prudent in the use of our resources.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Because of the urgency of the situation, we are providing significant help to many groups in this Budget, in a broad-based manner so that we can reach as many of those who need help as possible and as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that those who receive support will use the resources wisely and responsibly, or channel it to those who may need it more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we will not hesitate to take action against any abuse.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):   The COVID-19 pandemic is progressing aggressively, causing significant losses to the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the past few weeks, the number of confirmed cases worldwide has increased exponentially.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To avoid losing control of the situation, many countries have announced unprecedented measures to curb the spread of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These measures have battered the global economy and financial markets, disrupted supply chains and led to a slump in consumer demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a result, we have also been badly hit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pandemic is also a test of our society’s cohesiveness.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must be prepared psychologically and work together to overcome COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes the Supplementary Budget that was just announced today and the Budget announced in February.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Qualified Singaporeans will receive cash payout of $1,000 per month for nine months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will disburse these subsidies as soon as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have therefore introduced the SGUnited Traineeships, to provide opportunities for young Singaporeans to accumulate work experience in different industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, to help our enterprises, we will support viable enterprises to continue to operate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will provide more property tax rebates and rental rebates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly urge property owners to reduce rents to provide relief for tenants who may be facing cash flow problems.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For industries badly hit by COVID-19 such as the aviation and tourism industry, we will also provide targeted assistance to help them tide over this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pandemic may have serious impacts, it may also bring about new opportunities in the longer term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprises should make use of this lull period to upskill their workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans should also upgrade their skills and prepare for the economic recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we understand that many Singaporeans are worried that they will not be able to cope with living expenses for the next few months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will enhance the Care and Support Package introduced earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhanced package will be worth $4.6 billion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We do not know when this pandemic will end, nor the scope and scale of its impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, we hope to save jobs, help enterprises and secure our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are able to do so because we have our national reserves to serve as our bulwark against shocks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After serious considerations, we have decided to draw on our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are able to do this because of our fiscal discipline and we have been preparing for rainy days through the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, if we remain vigilant and calm, and continue to work together as one nation, Singapore can definitely overcome the difficulties, and emerge with confidence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At this point, I would like to thank our frontline workers, healthcare workers, public servants, enterprises, unions, community organizations and volunteers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Your selflessness and professionalism is critical in helping us keep the COVID-19 situation under control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to uphold the spirit of SG Together, to turn this crisis into opportunities, and emerge even stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, I will now conclude in English.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic is the most serious crisis we have faced in a generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has put all countries around the world to the test – on the medical, economic and social fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been able to respond boldly and decisively to the outbreak in Singapore because we have forged a cohesive, resilient society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The whole nation has come together in response.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our healthcare and frontline workers are working tirelessly to care for the infected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our cleaners are doing humble but heroic work to keep our environment clean.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Thousands of public officers are working round the clock to respond to the threat of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Private sector and corporations, too, have stepped forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Keppel has put together a $4.2 million package to support communities most affected by the COVID-19 outbreak.
