speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: It is, therefore, essential that companies and businesses relook their business models, train and upskill their workers and look to digitalisation as the new norm for doing business.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: It is, therefore, more crucial than ever for businesses to develop capabilities to be future-ready.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: If our businesses had been further along the digitalisation curve prior to the COVID-19 outbreak, the current transition to remote work arrangements and moving business operations into the online space would be less painful and probably better executed.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: The economy and business landscape after we emerge from this crisis will be vastly different.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: In the here-and-now, to limit physical interaction, we are faced with the reality of a leaner physical workforce and the necessity for many business operations and processes to take place in a virtual environment.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: At this point, we need to leap towards these solutions to accelerate the capability building process to be future-ready.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Companies have to realise with increasing urgency that digitalisation is no longer just a want or a good-to-have.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: It is now a necessity, and business owners must snap out of the haze of apathy and really use this opportunity for change.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Next, I move on to the final part of my speech – Singapore's strong labour tripartite partnership.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, I would like to focus on two aspects of this partnership.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: We are very fortunate that our current Government is efficient and one that takes a consultative attitude.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: However, it is also not by chance that most of our factories are able to continue running and that we are able to go about with our lives with relative normalcy despite this "perfect storm".

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: As a community, we have worked hard for this.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: However, from the US-China trade conflict to the civil unrests in Hong Kong and now COVID-19, employers have had to bravely plod through these overlapping hurricanes which have since merged into one perfect storm.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: The spirit of reciprocity also applies to employees.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Better understanding of policy leads to less resistance and people willing to go beyond the minimum standards that law mandates.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, it is in this difficult time that morale is not further beaten down by what can easily be perceived as draconian measures.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We focused on that and we improved MRT and bus services.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We also pushed hard for a car-lite Singapore, rolling out major extensions to the MRT network and cycling paths.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We also worked hard to enhance Singapore as an air and sea hub.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Last December, my family got me to take a short break.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: My third grandchild was born on my birthday in December the year before and the family gave us a joint birthday celebration in Melbourne.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: While there, I reflected with some satisfaction how everything was coming along nicely.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Tuas mega port, Terminal 5 (T5) and several MRT projects were on track.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Then, all of a sudden, hell broke loose!

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: How the world changed in four short months.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Here in Singapore, we are seeing community spread and we have to apply a circuit breaker.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As countries try to protect lives through isolating them, the global economy grinds to a standstill.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The impact on Changi air hub is severe.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Airlines, ground handlers, airport shops and restaurants have all experienced a sharp fall in business.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I met them often, face to face, at the airport, over the weeks.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As the virus grew into a global pandemic, I saw increasing fear in their eyes.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The last time I experienced this was during SARS.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For aviation, we will help the companies so that they can retain their workers.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They will get substantial cash grants to cover the bulk of their local workers' payroll.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We are providing other cost relief through generous rebates, deferments and rental relief.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The Changi community knows it is not business as usual – far from it.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The companies are reviewing their operations to reduce cash burn.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Right now, one terminal is enough to handle the current volume of demand.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We can close down one or two terminals.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: While full recovery this year is unlikely, partial recovery next year is probable.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We must be ready to lead and to ride the recovery when it happens.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With the suspension of T2 operations, we will reallocate airlines across the remaining terminals.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Singapore Airlines (SIA) will consolidate its operations in Terminal 3 (T3).

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will ensure sufficient capacity for all airlines to grow when passenger traffic recovers.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In managing this crisis, we are mindful that global connectivity is of fundamental importance to Singapore.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It links us to the rest of the world.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It defines us as a global city and indeed, as a people.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Domestically, the Changi air hub is crucial to Singapore's role as a business, manufacturing and research and development (R&D) hub.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: If it were to collapse, it will undermine our ability to recover from the crisis.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Many Singaporeans depend on Changi Airport for a living.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That is why we took swift action to support the air hub to prevent the loss of strategic capabilities and our hard-earned position as a reliable air hub.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Prompt action by Temasek to back SIA's fundraising efforts and the Government's Resilience Budget have been viewed positively by many industry analysts.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Their conclusion is that SIA "looks well positioned to emerge from the coronavirus crisis as an industry leader".

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Meanwhile, SIA, SilkAir, Scoot and their crew have not been sitting idle.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They are actively engaged in our national battle against COVID-19.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: First, they continue to mount around 40 return passenger flights a week to ASEAN capitals and the economic hubs in Asia, Australia, Europe and the US.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They take precautionary measures to protect the crew.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For short haul flights, the crew do not leave the plane during turnaround.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For long haul flights, the crew stay at airport hotels during the layover and do not leave their rooms.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: On board flights, the serving crew wear masks and minimise contact with passengers.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That was how we were able to evacuate two batches of Singaporeans from Wuhan in February.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: That was also how we flew our students back from the UK and the US last month.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Second, in addition to its passenger flights and freighter services, SIA is deploying some of its passenger aircraft to carry only cargo.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Together, these services fly in essential goods amidst the global supply disruptions, such as medical supplies, food and other useful cargoes.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Third, their crew are volunteering to help, using their skills in many useful ways.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I came across one WhatsApp text from an SIA stewardess: "I am a flight attendant.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Now that I no longer have flights to operate, I thought it would be best if I could render some kind of help to the community.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Apart from queue management, temperature taking and other tasks, I can also help the elderly and other individuals who require assistance." I find that a touching message!

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Apart from aviation, the pandemic has also affected taxi, Grab and Gojek drivers.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As one taxi driver put it starkly, "There's no work.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I cannot live like this." I met some of them when they came to apply for the Temporary Relief Fund.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Many have experienced SARS but unlike SARS, they know a speedy recovery is unlikely this time round.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Mr Lim Jit Poh chaired ComfortDelGro during SARS.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: He saw the hardship coming as soon as the outbreak worsened in February.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Meanwhile, we accept the fall in demand for buses and trains.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It means that Singaporeans are staying at home more and doing what they need to do around their immediate neighbourhood.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is not the time to use our public transport to get to the other side of Singapore for your favourite hawker dish.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With the circuit breaker measures, we can now enforce safe distancing on public transport.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: And we are deploying transport ambassadors to remind commuters of these measures.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: To tackle the pandemic, countries must work together.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It does not make sense for traditional food exporters to ban exports.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It only hurts their farmers as their harvests rot in the field.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It is critical to keep global supply chains intact so that goods can get to countries and the people who need them.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: From my office, I can see Pasir Panjang Terminal.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We had put in place precautionary measures to ensure a safe working environment for our staff and our crew.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With this, our port continues to service the world and at the same time, safeguard our essential supplies.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We thank the many countries that have worked with us to ensure that trade flows continue during this difficult time.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Working tirelessly behind the scenes to keep Singapore moving and connected are our transport workers – our train and bus captains, taxi and private hire car drivers, seafarers, shore-based staff, pilots, cabin crew, airport ground staff.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I am also heartened by how our transport operators, the National Trade Workers Union (NTWU) and LTA, had rallied together to stand by our bus captains from Malaysia when the MCO was suddenly imposed.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Our bus operators worked through the night, got the drivers checked into accommodation and updated their duty rosters to replace those drivers who stayed back in Johor.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: And the next day, our bus services functioned normally.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Our amazing One Transport family came together to support their colleagues in their hour of need and ensured the continuity of our public bus service.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Nobody knows how long the pandemic will last, but recover, we will.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It will, however, not be a simple return to status quo ante.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For instance, supply chain resilience will become even more important.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: So, expect more local production to improve resilience.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This will have implications for Singapore's transshipment hub.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As global trade flows shift, we must still secure and strengthen our role as a major node in global supply chains.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The efficiency and connectivity of our sea port and airport will become even more critical.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Just as 9/11 changed aviation security forever, expect COVID-19 to impact air travel and airport operations.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This will have implications for our T5 planning and timeline.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I strongly believe air travel growth will return, although a quick rebound is unlikely.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Fortunately, T5 was designed to be modular so that its construction can be scaled up or down as necessary.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Meanwhile, we have to revive air transport links.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This will be crucial to reviving the global economy and trade flows, and rebuilding people to people exchanges.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: When the situation improves, we will see how to bring the relevant stakeholders to work on sustainable recovery.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the International Maritime Organization (IMO) have a leading role to play and we will support them.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will need to develop new global rules and guidelines to take into account the lessons learnt from the pandemic.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We also have to think about how to enhance capability across all regions because the connectivity network is only as strong as its weakest link.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The transport sector plays a crucial role in the survival and prosperity of Singapore.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For me, during this crisis, I will focus on three areas: (a) keeping our air and sea ports operational so that we continue to play our pivotal role in the global supply chain.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Even in crisis mode, we must work to enhance our reputation as among the most reliable hubs in the world; (b) protecting the health of our transport workers and ensuring the safety of the commuters; and (c) enlisting the help of every Singaporean to get us through this difficult time to emerge stronger than before.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This will strengthen our social bonds as one people.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The coming months will be very challenging and hard for all of us.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But the world is not coming to an end.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With the circuit breaker in place, my wife and I cannot get near him.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: My daughters are not visiting us like before.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Fortunately, we have two grandkids staying with us.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Yesterday, when my wife was about to pick up some items from the neighbourhood sundry shop, I heard my granddaughter yelling out her instruction: “Remember to wear your mask; if there is a crowd, stand one metre apart; ask Auntie Frances to do the same!” Frances is our domestic helper.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But most importantly, as I go around my estate in Toa Payoh, I think we should also give a lot of thanks to our resilient Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The day before Singaporeans were informed to actually maintain social distancing, the day after when I passed by seeing Singaporeans actually maintaining the gap at hawker centres, highlighted how resilient our Singaporeans and citizens are.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And I think most importantly we need to thank our Singaporeans for being resilient and for riding through this fight against this COVID.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, once again, thank you, Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister Heng and team for rolling out the Resilience Budget.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Just about a month ago, we were debating about the annual Budget.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Since then, the COVID-19 situation around the world and in Singapore has seen some very rapid developments.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In spite of that, our Government has maintained a level-headed response to comprehensively manage the situation, winning the admiration of national bodies and citizens from around the world.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Now, in a highly reassuring move for all, a Supplementary Budget has been introduced to enhance help for businesses and individuals in this prolonged war against the COVID-19, and today we have the Solidarity Budget.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Besides saving jobs and healthcare help, the focus on resilience and making sure we emerge from this crisis stronger for Singapore is also key.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Since then, further details on the measures to support Singaporeans affected by COVID-19 has come out such as the Temporary Relief Fund, COVID-19 Support Grant, the Self Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) and Workfare Special Payment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These have been timely just as Singaporeans are increasingly being affected by the crisis.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have a few questions, clarifications and suggestions as a follow-up to the Supplementary Budget and hope the Deputy Prime Minister would consider them.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are for three segments, namely companies and workers, vulnerable residents and Singaporeans in general.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My first broad question is, given our unprecedented measures, what is the nature of this current crisis we are having now which is unprecedented and how different it is from past crises Singapore has faced.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Government has implemented an elevated set of safe distancing measures as a circuit breaker.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The negative impact on the economy and jobs will be significant.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some transactions like these can be deferred or shifted forward like property purchase or purchase of a washing machine or online laptop or clothing.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some transactions cannot be and will represent a permanent loss – a Michelin dining experience, yoga class or hotel stay.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some business services can be operated from home and still function despite a lockdown.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some businesses have already seen a sharp drop such as hotels, even before the additional measures.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, it is possible that non-essential services cover about a third of total employment more than their share of GDP.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The question to the Deputy Prime Minister is, the short-circuit measures may affect businesses and thus unemployment rates or jobs if it is prolonged and would have been even larger without any Government financial support.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is this going to be a deeper recession than even during the Asian Financial Crisis or the Global Financial Crisis?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And whether we need further financial measures to actually enhance or support the economy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Job Support Scheme (JSS) is a crucial part of the Budget, as I go on to my next question on workers, to help employees stay employed, and to help employers retain their trusted employees.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The question I have is, can we have this higher tier wage support extended to the retail sector beyond April.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But if we are still in a recession by the fourth quarter of the year, a third relief package and an extension of rental waiver will be necessary.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Government provide further waiver if the situation necessitates it?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I also note that JSS has been extended to cover nine months, up from three months previously.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In my Budget response, I shared my concerns on the duration of which eligible employers will receive the pay-out.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I am also pleased when the Deputy Prime Minister mentioned just now that enhancements will be brought forward to April, earlier, and it will be delivered as fast as possible.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But with the new enhancements what will be done to ensure the employees will get the grant short support in the shortest duration possible?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The other measure that the Deputy Prime Minister mentioned earlier was the Foreign Worker Levy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I am pleased that the foreign worker level will be waived in the month of April.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, we expect the COVID-19 situation to persist for for possibly over a year and these sectors are significant key node of the Singapore economy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Right now priority should be helping businesses stay afloat.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We cannot let them adversely be affected by creative destruction.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, will the Government consider extending the waiver beyond April if we manage to get out of the circuit-breaker period.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Next, if we step back, and take a more macro view of our measures to help the economy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In other countries facing major economic disruptions due to city or nationwide lockdowns, speculations are flying over whether governments would nationalise or bail out some of their key private services and businesses.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In our circumstance, we are blessed to have reserves and well managed sovereign institutions such as Temasek, GIC and Statutory Boards such as MAS.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, no matter how large the size of our reserves, it is still limited and we need to optimise its usage.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Broadly, my question is conceptually, how and when does the Singapore Government decide to bail out a particular company?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would it be based on the national security angle and the number of jobs they provide?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It would be useful to share the broader factors that are taken into consideration in a transparent manner.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Next for individuals and small businesses hit by the COVID-19 impact, there are a few issues I would like to suggest and seek clarification.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, in terms of relaxing macro-prudential measures temporarily to help small business and individuals.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The latest MAS and financial institutions support measures such as deferring of repayment for residential property loans and lower interest on personal unsecured credit is largely welcome.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, according to the statistics from MAS, housing and bridging loans have been declining since May 2019.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The concern is that under current crisis and with the above trend continuing, people may be resorting to alternative forms of credit, including the more expensive and higher interest rate loans from money lenders and even loan sharks.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The intention is to relax access to cheaper loans and credit from banks for sole proprietors and small SMEs, which often rely on personal credit and cash flow to keep their businesses running.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With self-employed workers losing their gigs, as well as job losses and wage cuts all round, many will see the TDSR curbing their eligibility for loans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The monetary policy transmission channel is broken from easier monetary policy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When you cannot borrow, it will be difficult for monetary policy to work.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Consumers cannot access credit because of TDSR and prudential measures.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Companies cannot access credit because banks will be wary of defaults – even with the enhanced risk co-sharing scheme that supports eligible SME loans and the other above support measures.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am also concerned that some parties and individuals may take advantage of the current crisis to make super normal borrowing rates, and I urge the Government to be on the watch for evidence of such behaviour.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Next, I have a question on CPF contribution rates.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Her employer said it is a cost-saving measure to help businesses.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Of course, I told her it was not, and to speak to me or MOM if her boss denies her full CPF payment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, this brings to mind that in times like this, some businesses may resort to illegal measures to cut their losses.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is fortunate that this resident sought clarification.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some others would have believed and accepted it, especially with so many jobs on the line now.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am sure any employer who resorts to cheating their employees out of their CPF will be duly punished.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But I hope the Government will consider the soft approach and help out companies with genuine difficulties.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The third segment I have and the final one is on building food, social and psychological resilience as we position ourselves for recovery.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One broad question I have the Deputy Prime Minister is how can Singapore citizens and the whole country emerge stronger once the dust has settled.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One example is how we can become stronger in terms of food resilience.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: COVID-19 has also emphasised the importance of having resilient supplies of food and other essential items.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Indeed, it is good to know that Singapore is building up our national stockpile of health supplies, including masks and hand sanitisers, so that we will continue to be well-stocked and we have in place a robust, multi-pronged strategy, to ensure that we continue to have a stable supply of safe food.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In these challenging times, the poor and vulnerable are the hardest hit.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Manpower too has become hard to come by due to COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the whole process can be streamlined so that eligible parties need not be put through a long wait for help.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Because we have an excellent healthcare system, a Government who cares for the citizens and great people who are going above and beyond to keep our country safe.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am proud to be Singaporean and this crisis makes me feel prouder and more patriotic than ever.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I support the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets and I pledge to do my best for my fellow citizens so that we can all get through this crisis together.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These challenges are fast evolving, not only in the world but also in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In many ways, we have managed the impact of the first wave of COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But the second wave has come upon us and the Government has taken more measures to combat the spread.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Protecting lives is of utmost importance and urgency.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But this can clash painfully with sustaining livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I have spoken to many on the ground – Chief Executive Officers (CEOs), workers from all walks of life and freelancers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The new circuit breaker measures, while protecting lives, will only make things harder for them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I am also personally reassured that the Government is prepared to do more if and when necessary.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They know that these circumstances are challenging, and they are willing to do their part.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: However, they want me to help them relay one key feedback.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They would like to see an increase in the speed of Government assistance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Government has pushed out a lot of budgetary help over the past weeks.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The key now is to put this help directly into the pockets of ordinary workers and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The economic impact of COVID-19, as many in this House have said, is unprecedented and the situation has escalated faster than any of us expected.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Through this, we must remain agile and adaptable in responding to the increasing challenges.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Over the last few days, I saw many queuing up for the Temporary Relief Fund – over 3,000 in my division.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: For many, it is the first time that they are applying for aid, not something they ever thought they would have to do.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They tell me they are more than willing to work to support their families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But now, many of them have little choice.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: And the worry in their voices was frankly heart-breaking.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: So, I am glad to hear Deputy Prime Minister say today that this money provided for in the different Budgets will be paid out quickly.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our financial muscle today in Singapore is not insignificant – thanks to the foresight of our founding leaders.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Government is rolling out other cash support for the months ahead, such as the COVID-19 Support Grant and the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme, or SIRS.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Though the support is generous, some freelancers and self-employed have told me they are worried.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I have also spoken to Deputy Prime Minister Heng and Mrs Josephine Teo, our Manpower Minister, to see how we can help this group of self-employed and freelancers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: NTUC will step up to administer the applications and appeals for SIRS.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will do our best in this aspect.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But I also hope more will apply for the NTUC Care Fund for COVID-19 in the interim.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: And we, in the Labour Movement, want to chip in and help out our fellow workers and put cash directly into workers' and freelancers' hands.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: More than cash, we must help Singaporeans with their jobs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Earning a decent wage is crucial for survival and paying bills.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Government is helping companies to stay liquid and keep their workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But again, if I may just reinforce my feedback, this help must be pushed out quickly, as the revenue has dried up for many companies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As Labour Chief, I have vested interests in companies' survival and success because our workers can only succeed when companies succeed and do well.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: NTUC, therefore, has been engaging CEOs to understand their concerns and see how we in NTUC and the Labour Movement can assist, whether it is about cutting costs to save jobs, accessing Government assistance or job matching their excess workers through our Job Security Council.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I also recently spoke to leaders in the local aviation and aerospace sectors to see how they are and see what we can do together.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Despite the aviation and aerospace sectors suffering huge losses, the CEOs are trying their best to keep their workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This means they can earn some income and, at the same time, help in our national COVID-19 efforts.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Also, despite these difficult times, the CEOs are keeping an eye on the future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They are making use of Government support to send their workers for training so that when the upturn eventually comes, our air sectors will be poised and ready for those new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I hope other employers do their part too, because their actions will greatly impact how Singapore emerges from this crisis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Companies must keep their workers employed and make use of the support to send workers for training.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In whatever ways NTUC can help, we want to do so.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: (In Mandarin):   	This year's Budget was first boosted and further enhanced.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It shows the Government's resolute determination to help our people and businesses tide over these difficult times.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In my conversations with residents, workers, union leaders and employers, they all said that this Budget can help them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: However, they hope that the measures will be implemented earlier – relief and subsidies be disbursed sooner.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As the Chinese proverb says, “distant water cannot help to put out a fire close at hand”.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In NTUC, we have also stepped up our efforts to help employers and workers understand the various schemes introduced by the Government and, more importantly, help them benefit from the schemes as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The income of self-employed persons was greatly impacted by the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I have discussed this with Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat and Manpower Minister Josephine Teo.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In these difficult times, I believe that if we stay united, with concerted efforts to overcome all challenges, we will be able to ride this out together and move towards a brighter future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: She thanked me profusely for all the different assistance given to her, whether Government or NTUC.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But in this conversation, what caught my attention was the story she told about her daughter.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: She told me her daughter had just returned from overseas.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Her daughter saw the big difference between Singapore's way of dealing with COVID-19 through a whole-of-nation approach in tackling the crisis versus what she experienced overseas.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: She saw the help that was given to her mother.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: She saw how Singaporeans came together to help one another.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: She says now she realised what it means to be Singaporean and that she is proud to be Singaporean – coming from a 20-something year old who, I believe, has matured tremendously over the last four months.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: COVID-19 is one of the biggest challenges we have faced to date.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Let us show who we are, that we are a resilient nation, that we respond to facts, we trust our Government and importantly, we have compassion for our neighbours.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have rice, canned food, toilet paper, cooking oil, instant noodles.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Yes, prices of certain items have gone up in recent weeks due to higher demand worldwide, increases in production costs, increases in shipping/freight charges and so on.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But be assured that we will continue to do our best to moderate these price increases and make it affordable to all.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This price guarantee could not be more timely under the current situation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Ordinarily, I would not have made such a promotional statement.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But these are not ordinary times and we are not an ordinary people.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In good times, some critics here call us stingy.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We are a House known for discipline, fiscal prudence, saving for rainy days.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At NTUC Enterprise, we too have to marshal our capital resources to ensure our entities – from NTUC Income, to Mercatus, to the FairPrice Group, to NTUC First Campus, to our NTUC Learning Hub, to our NTUC Health – that we are able to withstand the shocks and disruptions caused to our businesses.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have a strong local core and close to 80% of our team are Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have Malaysian colleagues who form slightly over half of our non-local workforce.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have staff from other nationalities as well and, as what NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng just said, every worker matters.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Every one of my colleagues plays a part to keep our many essential services running smoothly – our childcare centres, our nursing homes, our senior care centres, our food courts, our malls, our supermarkets, our online platforms and so on.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And in a different but equally important function, our NTUC Learning Hub is pivoting towards being a digital learning hub and they have been busy working closely with employers and unions to train thousands of workers, digital where possible, so that when our economy recovers, workers, both local and foreign, and companies will be all ready from the word go.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We are inter-connected and we are interdependent – manpower, skills, supply lines.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Our teams have been working as part of our diversification strategy to ensure our supply chains remain strong.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have been working on this for many years and we are proud to support local produce and local companies.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The things we do to support this philosophy – giving off-take contracts to local producers, holding local fairs such as the Annual Tasty Singapore Fair to promote local produce and products by local firms, our a manpower policy that employs as many Singaporeans as possible.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, while we think and plan global, we act, we support and we grow local.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There are also more older workers in our NTUC group, especially at the FairPrice group.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The demographics of our workforce and our policies are skewed towards mature staff.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am quite a few years more than 50 years old.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We also have a large pool of permanent part-timers which suits their lifestyle.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If there ever has been any doubt about the resilience of older, mature workers, the past few months have laid these to rest.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am proud and I am glad that our mature workforce came through very well during this period.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They have been very calm, steady, resilient and working tireless.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And they work well with our younger team members and so together, the team becomes stronger.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The young with energy, creativity and stamina; the older with experience, patience and acumen.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I see parallels with how our 4G leaders are coming up and showing their leadership mettle whilst being supported by the senior, more experienced leaders.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Again, together, we have a better team at the helm to take us through this global crisis.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Turning to our Government leadership – they have stayed calm, they have listened to feedback, they have been bold, thinking out of the box, thinking measures for both short and long term, and they have been decisive.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: During such times, there were, I am sure, many difficult and tough decisions to make and, for sure, some unpopular ones.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But I know the Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister, the Cabinet and most certainly, the Ministerial task force, they have all been guided by their true north – what is good for the country and our people.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If I can draw a parallel, a difficult and unpopular decision that I had to make as the group CEO of FairPrice was the one that concerned the imposition of purchasing restrictions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: No one likes to be told that there are some things money cannot buy.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But at end of the day, I was guided by my true north, which is to ensure as many people can have access to their food supplies for the key categories.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And yes, in this case, there are some things money cannot buy – fairness, a sense that we are in this together and a trust that we are doing the right thing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We can only take these decisions if we have supportive and understanding stakeholders – in my case, my board of directors, the public, the staff, my business partners, customers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In the case of the Government, this would be the Cabinet, residents, citizens and tripartite partners comprising employers, unions and the Government.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If there is no trust, none of this can be done.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Yes, we all need to tighten our belts, grit our teeth and learn to adapt.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As they say in Hokkien – no fish, shrimp also can.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And if need be, can we make do with porridge, with salted fish or vegetables?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As a Hokkien – can I make do with porridge?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Porridge with salted vegetables or salted fish – I am fine with anything.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Over the last two months, our supermarket staff in the frontline have been working hard, serving customers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They too are tired, they too are anxious, but they have to maintain a professional front, facing all kinds of customers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: A big majority is very understanding and polite, but there are some who do not make the effort to be civil or reasonable.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There is this very small group of people who turn into terrible versions of themselves when confronted with crises.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Just this morning, during our priority shopping hour for Pioneer Generation members, for pregnant women, for people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Again, we will have one or two of these people who will make a lot of noise.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What you do not see are also the staff serving behind, in the "backline" – as my chairman Bobby Chin describes them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They are working hard to secure our supplies and making more deliveries.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Indeed, I am extremely grateful to all our staff, frontline and backline, as well as our business partners and the public for their understanding and support.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For sure, there are some areas we could have done better, some where we took a wrong step, but learn we did and we strive to be better going forward.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Likewise, I am sure our Government and our leaders probably had such experiences too, but hey, we all have perfect vision after the event.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Having said that, my team and I have also received numerous notes, cards of appreciation – from the public, from customers, unions, business leaders, school teachers, school children.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We are in this together and this is what is required for us to overcome the crisis.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Over this period, we have had to press the button and call on many friends for help.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And when the button is pressed, our colleagues from the headquarters as well as staff across the group all responded and helped out – anytime, over the weekends – doing replenishment, picking, packing and what have you.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: From our leadership team to the administrative staff, from our board of directors to our union leaders.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We even had many members from the public and former colleagues stepping forward to call me and say, hey, if we needed them, just call them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I see this manifested and being played out throughout all parts of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Public and private businesses rallying and appreciating our healthcare workers, our security and immigration officers, our cleaners, our workers that keep our transport systems running and others such as the many volunteers who helped make the distribution of face masks and sanitisers for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There are many things that money can buy.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We do not make light of money because we know it buys a lot.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It helps us to pay for the salaries of workers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It helps us to save jobs, to help pay for the healthcare of the sick, to offset the living expenses and so on.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It will set us up to be better and stronger.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But we know, better than most, what money cannot buy.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I was listening very carefully to Mr Seah when he described what he had in warehouse.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think we are very assured except that I noticed he did not mention toilet paper.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Like many in this Chamber, I have received a tsunami of feedback.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: With that in mind, I would like to make a few points.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: One, at this critical stage, we must enforce safe distancing vigorously and our people must urge one another on, to do so.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It needs people to walk around to transmit, to spread.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, we must find a way to persuade one another that staying at home saves lives.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We must also be mindful that no amount of Government spending is sufficient to save our livelihoods if we lose the fight against the virus.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Two, we must create more short-term jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Then-US President Roosevelt introduced the Work Progress Administration (WPA) to create jobs for Americans, as part of the New Deal.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: WPA projects were designed to be manpower intensive, which means that the wages formed the vast majority of the project cost.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: There is already a fair number of unemployed professionals and management talent out there.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Some of them are too qualified to take on many of the new temporary jobs out there.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We can sign them up for short contracts, perhaps six to 12 months.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: To save time, the Government can outsource the management and hiring of these people to the private sector HR companies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The Government does not need to match their private sector pay.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Even $2,000 or $3,000 a month will suffice.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I believe many Singaporeans want to actively contribute to Singapore, rather than to wait on the sidelines for the economy to recover.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Their private sector experience make them ideal to contribute to the Government's transformation, to help the Government build even stronger bridges to the private and the public sector.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We can create a real and lasting advantage for Singapore and emerge stronger.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And if the pilot succeeds and if structural unemployment emerges, we can scale this up in perhaps three to six months' time.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Three, we can explore more ways to help our tertiary education students gain relevant skills.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The current situation is very tough for our current and future graduates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: While we can create short-term internships and training for some, others want to continue developing skills in critical demand.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Even amidst the challenges, there are still some skillsets that are very much in demand: AI, data-science, programming and electrical engineering.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that MOE can challenge our Universities to create opportunities for our students to gain these skillsets in the shortest time, at the lowest cost.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Naturally, it will be difficult to scale up the faculty strength quickly.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: One way is to consider the Emeritus model, which partners with Ivy League universities to offer online programmes from specialist certificates to masters programmes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: These courses now cost around US$3,500 to US$5,000 a year.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps you can consider subsidies to make this more affordable and more immediate to our tertiary students.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Also, perhaps you can consider getting our Polytechnics and Universities to temporarily relax criteria to shift majors, do double-degree or do a master’s degree, so that mechanical or civil engineers can switch or double in electrical engineering, data science or computer science.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Some of our Universities are already allowing for such flexibilities but it would be ideal if more can be done.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We can also consider a quick and temporary expansion of our SkillsFuture effort.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In this downturn, there is a fair number of private sector trainers or professionals with skillsets that provide valuable training, but are currently not certified to teach SkillsFuture courses.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The Government can consider partnering with a few reputable training providers, who can bring in these talents on board to train other Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Four, we should gather Singapore's leading minds to path-find the road ahead.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: If the pandemic does not globally peak by the middle of this year, the impact to the world could be truly profound.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The world is moving in a non-linear way.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It can comprise of our most brilliant and experienced experts, leaders and scientists.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We can apply scenario planning, develop multi-disciplinary insights, to decipher how the world could unfold and, therefore, provide advice and perspective to our Government and national leaders.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Some of the issues they can consider include how will the world order change?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: What is the monetary effect of a prolonged and massive debt-raising by developed countries?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: How will our industry structure change after this?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Can we benefit from the likely decoupling of the global supply chain?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Are there things we can proactively do to mitigate the downsides, for example, through localising the workforce of certain industries to deal with rising structural unemployment?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, will COVID-19 make it more difficult for the world to meet the challenges of climate change?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And therefore, must we accelerate our efforts or even do more to forestall or mitigate climate change?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For micro-SME owners, because they practise the concept of "leaders eat last", some take limited salary and get the bulk of their income through directors' fees.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Many of these micro-SME leaders have less than five employees and, therefore, actually, they are both workers and shareholders at the same time.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Of course, the job support amount must follow similar salary caps as per the other workers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore can and must come together to meet the challenges and emerge stronger.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This must and this will be Singapore's finest moment.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: With that, I stand in full support of all three Budgets.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I notice that the Member "arrowed" the Senior Ministers when they happen not to be in the Chamber.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have three points to make on the Resilience Budget.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, sufficiency of the Budget to fight and contain the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The bulk of this amount was earmarked for MOH.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The number of infected persons have gone up; the number of persons under quarantine and Stay-Home Notices (SHNs) are higher; contact tracing is vastly expanded; the costs of quarantining persons have gone up with the usage of hotels and other accommodation; equipment costs have also gone up.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My question is: have we put aside sufficient money to back our frontline agencies?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They – I am sure all Members of the House would agree – need our full support and should be as fully resourced as possible.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The next point is on helping the charity sector.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is a point that was alluded to by the hon Member of Parliament Mr Saktiandi Supaat just now.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Since the COVID-19 outbreak, it has been tough-going for charitable organisations including the mid-level and smaller Institutions of Public Character (IPCs).

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I personally spoke to CEOs of two VWOS which are IPCs supporting children from displaced families as well as the aged sick respectively.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is to be expected with the rapid contraction of our economy.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The VWOs, I am told, may be forced to dip into their reserves which are not as deep.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I respectfully disagree, however, with the hon Member Mr Saktiandi that more support should be given by the Government for these charities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I think the correct approach would be for us to deal with the root issue and scale up our efforts to reach out to the "haves" in our society – the grant-makers and donors – and get them to donate more to plug the gap.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng mentioned in both his Ministerial Statements that individuals, the private sector and corporations have stepped forward.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He suggested donations to be made to, inter alia, the Giving.sg platform.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the same vein, we should consider how to better match needs of smaller-scale VWOs with the interests and contributions from potential donors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Yesterday, I learned from a CEO of an SME that EnterpriseSG officers called him to check whether his employees who had to stand down owing to the contracting business, may be deployed in other companies that are less affected by the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We could adopt a similar approach and get a Government agency to help match VWOs with pressing needs with grant-makers or donors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I wish to share the content of a resident's email that was sent to me over the weekend.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He said and I quote, "Do you think we, Singaporeans, will be able to help by volunteering and donating part of our CPF monies to aid the Government and Singaporeans in this COVID-19 situation?" He wanted to donate part of his CPF monies!

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He is heartlander who wishes to be counted in helping the less fortunate during this crisis.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: When I read his email, it reminded me of what our President Mdm Halimah stated in her address that was read out in Parliament in 26 March 2020.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She said and I quote, "In these worst of times, I am heartened to see the best of Singaporeans." I heard another example in Mr Vikram Nair's speech just now about a shopkeeper in his constituency, distributing essential food items to needy families.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We have here an opportunity to mobilise even more fellow Singaporeans to join the clarion call sounded by our President to work together as one people and support one another in this journey.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In his Ministerial Statement delivered on 26 March 2020, Deputy Prime Minister Heng stated as follows: "While we attend to the immediate and urgent tasks, we will set outsides on the long term so that Singapore comes out of this crisis stronger as a nation." I applaud Deputy Prime Minister Heng and the Government for bringing focus to the need to build resilience to face the next challenge.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Almost a generation ago, we started building up our capability in R&D.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As a result, as Deputy Prime Minister mentioned, our country developed COVID-19 test kits quickly and the kits were sent to other countries.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is a source of huge pride for fellow Singaporeans that our little red dot is helping in a big way the global effort to contain the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Equally, we need to plant seeds of resilience now so that we, when the next crisis comes, which is in words of President Halimah, "inevitable", the next generation of Singaporeans can benefit from these long-term measures and deal effectively with – in the words of Deputy Prime Minister – the next generational crisis.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One, strengthening the Singapore Core in important operational jobs and two, engaging Singaporeans on the importance of food security.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is because a significant number of them are Malaysians.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Second, Deputy Prime Minister specifically highlighted locally, the food resilience point in his Budget as an area to strengthen.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There were at least two separate occasions during the COVID-19 outbreak when supermarkets were inundated with residents wanting to buy essential food items for fear that they will dry up.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We need to address this issue once and for all.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If Singaporeans are assured we have sufficient food through what is grown within our stockpile and outside resources, hopefully, we will be able to avoid runs on supermarkets in the future.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, I suggest we need to aim even higher over a long-term period.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I do not have sufficient information to suggest a target but I can already see potential for entrepreneurism and harnessing of technology in this arena.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The hon Member Mr Ang Wei Neng made the same point.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What is equally important is to ingrain in our people the trade-offs involved.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Our people must support local agricultural companies, which must provide good value propositions; and at the same time, our people must accept that there will be higher costs associated with this.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: So, this is an opportunity for our Government, particularly MEWR, to gain the support of people not just to achieve but exceed the 30 by 30 vision.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Moving on to the Solidarity Budget, I have one point to make.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is in relation to the enhancing of Temporary Bridging Loans for SMEs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am glad to hear the Deputy Prime Minister announce plans to strengthen this aspect.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Hitherto, there was some level of scepticism from some businesses on this issue.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One businessmen shared with me the potential effect that he feared once the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Bill is passed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He said that he is a landlord and he services a mortgage through the rent from the tenant.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Now, if he is not allowed to collect rent, then he would have to take out a bridging loan.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the end, he fears that he, as a landlord, would take a hit, the tenants will obviously be in a difficult position as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In a situation that affects the entire world like a pandemic, the world must get its act together before we, however resilient we may be, because we are very open nation, can return to normalcy.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Henry Kwek shared his musings on the global dynamics.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Ordinarily, this would be hard for small nations like Singapore to influence.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But we saw Singapore contribute to these efforts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Prime Minister Lee and Minister for Foreign Affairs Dr Vivian Balakrishnan gave important interviews that resonated worldwide.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I do not think that it is going to help us solve the problem sooner." It is both in our national interest as well as the world's, for these two giants to work together.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Singapore uniquely was able to make this call.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is a true friend of both countries.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I respectfully suggest that the words of Prime Minister Lee and Minister Vivian resonated better because of our exceptional people.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The vast majority of fellow Singaporeans including hon Members in Opposition fully back the Government in its plans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The fact that we back our Government has nothing to do with us being a paternalistic society; a label that foreign media has used.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: That assertion is an insult to right-thinking Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In fact, it is illogical because in almost a next breath, there is an acknowledgement that the plans we put in place here are good ones.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The backing of our people is because of the trust carefully developed over the decades.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng spoke about it earlier today.
