speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is manifested in the way the Government conducted itself through the crisis, taking its duties with utmost seriousness, being completely honest, forthright and transparent and unafraid to explain the tough measures needed to save our people's lives and livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Inevitably, there will be charlatans making false and spurious allegations and suggestions as to how they would handle such issues with knowledge gained from hindsight.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Their purpose is to drive a wedge between the Government and our people and erode the trust between them.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Such acts should be robustly rejected by fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng predicted that we would ride through the storm and emerge even stronger.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have no doubt that he is correct, so long as we all remain united.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I do not recall being in Chamber with so few Members on an important occasion of a Budget Debate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2009, when the world was reeling from the shock of the Global Financial Crisis, I was a Labour Member of Parliament on the backbench.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Just days before Chinese New Year, nearly 700 workers were retrenched by a textile manufacturing company.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I felt for the workers, including the union leaders who had become my friends.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Miraculously, by July, there were green shoots, the first time that phrase got thrown about, and the economy started on this rather strange V-shaped recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, COVID-19 certainly appears to me to be more cruel than SARS and even the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: No one can, at this point, seriously imagine a V-shaped recovery any time soon, if at all.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: After all, entire cities and nations have had to make drastic changes to the way people live.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last Friday, the Prime Minister spoke on the COVID-19 situation in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To protect all of us, we had to make the difficult decision to implement a circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The temporary closure of most workplaces, except for essential services and key economic sectors, takes effect tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many are asking – how will we get through the next one month?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But one thing we can be sure of is that we will get through this together.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will stand in solidarity with workers as well as businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Businesses providing essential services are still allowed to operate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For workers in non-essential businesses, those who can telecommute should do so.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Their employers should pay them appropriately, instead of treating this period as no-pay leave.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To Ms Jessica Tan's question, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will say more about how MOM will help businesses enable employees to work from home.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For those workers who are unable to work remotely, the enhanced Job Support Scheme should still help to fund the majority of their wages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We know employers are making many adjustments, but they should also do their part.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the generous Job Support Scheme funding, employers should aim to pass the Government support to their workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We urge them to communicate clearly to their employees on work and pay arrangements for the next few weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also ensure that vulnerable worker segments, such as self-employed persons and lower wage workers, receive sufficient support.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister has announced, we will broaden the coverage for the SEP Income Relief Scheme or SIRS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, we will include SEPs who earn a small income as employees, in addition to their main livelihood, which is self-employment, up to $2,300 per month, in terms of their earned employment income, which is the current Workfare income ceiling.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Two thousand and three hundred dollars is the current Workfare income ceiling.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will include most condominiums outside prime areas.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is no need for eligible SEPs to apply.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those aged 37 and above who declared a positive net trade income, will be automatically notified and receive their first payout in end of May.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For the rest of the SEPs that narrowly missed qualifying for SIRS, they can appeal and we will consider their cases.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To take care of appeals, I have reached out to Secretary-General of NTUC Brother Ng Chee Meng and the Labour Movement has established links with some groups of SEPs and is already administering the SEP Training Support Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Tomorrow, Minister of State Zaqy will share how we have enhanced the Workfare Special Payment (WSP) to strengthen support for our low-wage workers, many of whom Members of Parliament noted are critical to the provision of essential services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The evolving COVID-19 situation also brought about uncertainty to those looking for employment in this difficult job market.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I can completely understand that many are anxious.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In spite of the tremendous difficulties, the Government will actively facilitate the matching of jobseekers to businesses who still have immediate vacancies during this period, be it for a new job or to land a second job to supplement their income.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I had previously highlighted the SGUnited Jobs Initiative, which will create about 10,000 jobs over the next one year in both the public and private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The first SGUnited Jobs initiative Virtual Career Fair is currently on-going with 5,800 vacancies available and 5,500 applicants.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am quietly relieved that we have gotten good interest from employers and we will keep building up the pool of jobs that are immediately available.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as we go online, WSG's Careers Connect and NTUC's e2i centres will continue to provide face-to-face service to jobseekers who are in urgent need – of course, with appropriate safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our tripartite partners are also facilitating SGUnited Jobs at the company level.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through their networks, they bring together employers with complementary manpower needs – some have excess workers, some still have shortages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Adapt and Grow programmes will continue as far as possible, so people can get back into jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One particular group that weighs on my mind are recent graduates and graduating cohorts from the ITEs, from Polytechnics, from Universities and other educational institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a very tough time to be entering the job market and I recognise their worries as well as those of their parents.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I think Members will agree with me – we must find a way to help these young Singaporeans get started in their careers and not let COVID-19 derail them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we are making a big effort to mobilise employers to support the SGUnited Traineeships programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In normal years, most graduating students in Singapore can find a job within six months.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But in this climate, many employers are hesitant to take on any jobseeker, let alone one with no relevant experience.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It helps graduating students, as well as recent graduates, gain valuable work experience and develop professionally.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, if you look at their resumes, one year down the road, we hope not see this gaping hole, which they cannot articulate to prospective employers what happened, although everyone would understand, but still it is time lost.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More are coming on board and we are working hard on it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also support businesses to resume operations after this circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must hold on to the hope, that this is "pause", not "stop".

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM had earlier announced that SMEs will have three additional months to make the levy payments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government has further decided to waive levies due in April to provide extra relief.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, we will provide a one-off rebate to employers, based on past levies paid.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In view of the levy waiver and rebate, employers of foreign work permit and S Pass holders will no longer receive the daily allowance paid to employers of quarantined workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This supersedes the Government's earlier statement regarding the daily quarantine allowance.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have asked my colleagues to get the levy rebate out to the businesses as soon as possible and I am glad to say that it can be done as early as 21 April 2020, which is two weeks from now.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We need the employers to also sign up quickly, we will provide the details, but, in about two weeks, the levy rebate will come.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even before the payment is made, Members of Parliament have called for more.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: My commitment is that we will keep monitoring and reviewing the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This may go on for a while, so let us stay nimble and also sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: During this period, there are also many firms in need of manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I urge them to leverage on the SGUnited Jobs and SGUnited Traineeships to provide opportunities for our locals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can also tap on the existing pool of foreign workers already in Singapore, especially those that currently do not have work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The SBF's Manpower Connect will help businesses manage their manpower needs and tap on local and foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some people have asked and will continue to ask why we are providing support for businesses that hire foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will significantly impact all businesses with contractual and financial obligations, regardless of whether they employ locals or foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are providing some support, to ensure that firms with foreign workers can also restart operations and do right by their foreign workers during this period.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This does not change the fact that supporting local workers remains our top priority.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The schemes I mentioned fully demonstrate this commitment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But at such a time, we must stand united with all workers, every worker matters and not draw too many lines.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sharing pain should also mean sharing the relief.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, I appeal to businesses to use this levy rebate wisely.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is to help retain your essential workforce, so that your businesses can restart or scale up again once it is possible to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We expect you to look after not only your local workers but also your foreign workers and to take care of their upkeep during this circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Please demonstrate our solidarity with all our workers, both local and foreign.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Remember how they have helped you and your business in good times.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Do not forsake them in bad times and take care especially, of vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For now, the dark clouds cast by COVID-19 seem determined to stay.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But I am still hopeful, not because I have a crystal ball to tell me that all will be well soon.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If there is one thing I can say with confidence, it is this.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: On a global scale, we have seen extraordinary measures and steps taken by governments and citizens in managing and tackling this extraordinary calamity.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In my speech, I would like to make some proposals for the Government's consideration so that effort of strengthening our nation's unity and resilience can be more encompassing and more inclusive.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I am heartened by the steps taken by the MSF in exercising flexibility in rendering ComCare assistance.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, there are many households that have more than one immediate family staying together under one roof.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: For example, a couple with young children could be staying with their elderly parents along with another unmarried sibling.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Hence, there will be possibility of two main breadwinners or family heads within the same household being affected by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: By not limiting assistance to just one per household.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It will surely benefit and lighten the burden of such deserving cases.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The duration will be longer in a situation, whereby an applicant for some reason is unable to furnish a complete list of relevant documents.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Currently, the KiFAS or Kindergarten Financial Assistance Scheme is only available to students from low-income families while schooling in PCF kindergartens well as kindergartens administered by MOE's anchors operators.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In the past, I have made calls in this Chamber for KiPAS to be extended to all needy students who attend pre-school education centres run by Voluntary Welfare Organisations (VWOs) and faith-based entities such as churches and mosques.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Similarly, I would also like to suggest the same exceptions for MOE's Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This Scheme should also be made available to students who are attending non-public schools or education institutions which are not stipulated under MOE's list of qualified schools.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I would also like both MOE and MSF to consider extending the Assistance Schemes to another group of students who are Singaporean Permanent Residents with either one parent being a Singapore and even more so for single-parent families.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: On this note, I would like to suggest the same exception that I have mentioned earlier to cover the NEU PC Plus programme administered by the Infocomm Media Authority (IMDA).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The PC Plus programme offers low-income household with the students or persons with disability the opportunity to own a brand new computer as well as have Internet connection at an affordable price.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I believe we will not want to have a situation of Singaporean students who are unable to continue the school lessons because their homes do not have a computer or Internet connection.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: So, I am glad to see the following statement on IMDA's website: "Together with industry and community partners, IMDA has adjusted the NEU PC Plus programme to accelerate the provisioning of the PC bundle to eligible beneficiaries, which allow them to own online, to carry out activities such as e-learning amid the COVID-19 situation." IMDA acknowledges the current pressing needs and has made the necessary adjustments to ensure continuity and non-disruption of lessons to students.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Nonetheless, I would like IMDA to consider furthering their commendable efforts by allowing more than one PC to per household, which is the current practice.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Imagine a low-income family with more than two school-going children but only one PC at home, it will be challenging for these students to do their online lessons as prescribed by their schools.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: He shared that there are discussions among private hire car drivers on various social media platforms to request both HDB and URA to allow extension of the grace period from 10 minutes to maybe half an hour for gantry parking across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Reason cited was lesser point-to-point bookings will result in longer waiting times.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Hence, private hire drivers can have some savings whilst parking at designated parking areas rather than illegally on roadsides or restricted areas that in turn could pose a risk to other road users.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I hope MND can look into this particular request.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: My final point is on exercising leniency and flexibility in the payment of fines.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I would like to call upon the various Government agencies to consider allowing deferment of such payments or alternatively to allow instalment payments.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Nonetheless, appellants need to provide proof that are they are financially affected by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This will indeed lessen the difficulties faced by the individuals, businesses or any other entities who have been issued with fines while trying to cope with their financial struggles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: To conclude, Sir, as I mentioned in the opening part of my speech extraordinary efforts are being made worldwide to ensure that this pandemic will not result in extraordinary damage to human lives.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I am heartened by this move and strong emphasis on our vibrant arts scene in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that the arts groups and artists can tap on the Resilience Budget to build capabilities, to be self-sustained and well prepared for the future season to come.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: They can explore options such as upskill and upscale digital capabilities, such as online marketing and programming to share, spread and sell arts works across the boundary.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The funding can be maximised to help arts companies pick up necessary competencies in digital content strategy, search engine optimisation, online syndication and licensing.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: One, to digitalise arts activities and roll out a Digital Arts Festival so that this platform could be the outlet for quality arts performances.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For example, IMDA‘s Stay Healthy, Go Digital campaign encourages Singaporeans to “buy online, pay online and learn online”.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Inter-agencies efforts, for example, the National Arts Council (NAC) and IMDA could work together to stage a “SG United” Arts Festival online.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: And we hope to engage artists and arts groups in the making of the public campaign video to battle the COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Three, the Government could consider working with Giving.sg platform to encourage audience to give more donations for the arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The platform could configure a page for the arts community as a whole, on top of the current organisation feature.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, the refund from recent cancellations of arts concerts and activities could be donated to the particular arts group, or to the arts community as a whole.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This could be tapped on as a potential form of cultural influence and soft power.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that there are existing portals, such as MusicSG and Hear65, but often they struggle with maintaining audienceship and readership.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I hope more support could be given to these platforms.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In times of crisis, many countries will cut arts funding first.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: From this, we can see that the Government attaches great importance to the arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that the arts groups and artists can make good use of the funds and turn this crisis into opportunities, be more creative and use digital technology to make miracles.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, individuals should also upgrade and learn, and be prepared for the future as early as possible, so that when the time is ripe, they can realise their full potentials.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: IMDA can consider expanding the “Stay Healthy and Go Digital” campaign and promote the arts online.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: By doing this, different local arts activities can be broadcast online, and citizens can enjoy arts and spiritual inspiration.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We can bring physical activities online and create a Digital Arts Festival, so that this platform can be an outlet for quality arts performances to boost morale during this difficult period.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This would include commissioning new works, recording new audio or video productions.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: These support packages could help arts workers weather the storm and enable them to attract audiences back to theatres and shows with better arts works, to pay back to the society after this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Third, the Government can also work together with Giving.sg to promote arts giving.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We should encourage audiences to donate ticket refunds from the cancelled events to art groups to help them tide over this difficult period so that they can produce better quality programmes in the future.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Fourth, we could create a portal Arts.sg to bring all performances, recordings, arts courses and lectures together, and tap on larger platforms, such as SG United, to broadcast, so that appreciating and learning arts can become the people's inspiration and hope during this outbreak.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This could be packaged as Singapore Arts, and serve as a potential form of cultural influence and soft power for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I believe, Sir, as long as our arts groups work together, we can definitely ride out this difficult period.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: We are living in a world filled with anxiety now.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Anxiety about our livelihood, our health, our loved ones and even our future.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Life as we know it has been disrupted and changed in unimaginable ways by the onset of the coronavirus outbreak.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The livelihoods of many people have disappeared almost overnight as draconian measures are imposed on society to curb the spread of the virus and borders remain closed.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: No one knows when we will see the light at the end of this tunnel.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I am sure we are all driving blind in the dark at times, hoping that some, if not all of the targeted measures introduced over the course of this pandemic will work somehow.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: While these targeted measures are meant to slowly choke off the spread of the virus, they are also slowly killing the man in the street trying to make ends meet, working in the malls, cafés, coffee shops, and retail outlets, or driving taxis, private hire vehicles – and the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The world is certainly closing in for the man in the street with each successive round of heightened measures introduced the past few weeks.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I was at a coffee shop in Hougang when the news broke about the "no dining in" measure for eateries.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I could feel a sense of despair hanging in the air there.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I could sense the anxiety of the stall owners and coffee shop helpers as we spoke.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Two workers were very worried for they know their jobs are on the line.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: They know there would be no plates to collect and dishes to wash come Tuesday morning.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: You could tell by the look in their eyes they were worried about what is to come – the bills to pay and the living expenses.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The urgency and quantum of this Supplementary Budget probably sums up the gravity of the situation we are in right now.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: By dipping into the reserves, we are probably hoping to ride out this storm.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: We certainly need to buy some time for things to get better down the road, for nature to take its course and hopefully for a vaccine to be developed soon to end this misery.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But by doing so, we need to ensure the use of our reserves must achieve its intended purpose.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, the use of our reserves must save jobs, first and foremost.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: They should not be used to rescue corporate executives of large companies, who did little or no planning to save for a rainy day, and will continue to receive fat salaries while their companies bleed.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Next, I am in support of the measure to save jobs and the livelihoods of many self-employed Singaporeans in the Supplementary Budget.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: One particular group of Singaporeans I wish to highlight is those who are asked or encouraged to go on no pay leave for obvious reasons.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: My colleague, Ms Sylvia Lim, has highlighted some of these workers earlier.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Would they be receiving any help as well as there are bills to pay and mouths to feed?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: These workers would include retail staff, childcare centre cooks, coffee shop helpers, office cleaners and the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Other groups of Singaporeans that need help include those who are listed as directors or owners of their companies but they are actually one-man-operated entities – that is, self-employed.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I have a resident who runs an employment agency all by himself.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: There are also Singaporeans who are freelancers and they do not have receipts or CPF contributions to prove their livelihood status.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some may have only filed their income tax returns.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Where would such Singaporeans go to seek help for cash support?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I note the additional enhancement to the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme as announced by the Deputy Prime Minister earlier, and I hope the above workers would all be covered.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I hope the Minister can clarify on this matter.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Next, with the closure of non-essential workplaces and schools, I would expect utilities' usage for households to spike with Singaporeans working from home via telecommuting and students moving to full home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Affected Singaporeans struggling in this crisis will be unduly burdened by such overheads.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some help measures will only come in May or later, but many affected Singaporeans were already struggling to make ends meet since February.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I appreciate the Ministry for working at breakneck speed to roll out these measures.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COVID-19 is an unprecedented challenge that we face in this generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Within the short span of three months, many societies worldwide, in Europe, America, the Middle East and closer to home, in Southeast Asia, are seeing widespread transmissions, overwhelmed healthcare systems, soaring death rates and economic recession.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We all know the gravity of the situation – only the second time that we are dipping into our past reserves since Independence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we had experience with SARS 17 years ago, the world today is a much different place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are even more connected to the world than ever before.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have seen how the virus can spread like wild fire all over the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must do everything that we can to fight this virus on all fronts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Those who succumb to the virus could be a parent, a sibling, a friend, a neighbour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When we heard of community transmission in more countries and through large-scale religious gatherings, we took swift and decisive measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore suspended all religious services regardless of faith as part of a comprehensive set of safe distancing measures in order to reduce the risk of spreading the virus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is a huge sacrifice for all religious communities here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we all knew it had to be done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The fight against COVID-19 and coping with its socio-economic impact requires the support of everyone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By galvanising the strengths of these organisations, we will create new and stronger partnerships to provide better support for the community in areas such as employment and up-skilling, families and students, and the religious sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also strengthen the resilience of the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thus, I would like to speak on what we can do together as a community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This can be summed up in three Ps, namely, the first P – preserving our religious life; secondly, having a progressive religious leadership; and thirdly, persevering together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COVID-19 has disrupted our daily lives as well as our religious lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Muslims, many of our social norms are highly interpersonal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In fact, we believe that our merit is multiplied when we congregate to pray in a mosque.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We meet regularly in homes for religious gatherings like kenduri or doa selamat to offer prayers to family members who have passed on and strengthen our family bonds as we gather.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All these, we were told is part of our faith and our culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is therefore difficult to forgo such norms, but we understand and accept that safe distancing measures and the suspension of religious services are critical in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Changing our norms to protect ourselves and those around us does not make us any less of a Muslim or diminish our cultural identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Not being able to perform Friday prayers during our COVID-19 battle does not mean losing our faith or religious way of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the Mufti said, "  doing their bit to keep everyone safe is, in and of itself, one of the noblest things that we can do as Muslims" and also that "our togetherness and sense of community must remain strong in our hearts even as we have to keep physically apart".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am heartened to see that the community, the asatizah and the mosque leaders have rallied behind the religious leadership on the very difficult decision to close our mosques.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I also see people practising what has now been termed affectionately as "Salam Mufti" as an alternative to shaking hands with one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These actions are important as they reduce the risk of community spread.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am sure that many people are anxious to know when our mosques will reopen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Certainly, mosques hold a special place in the hearts of the Muslim community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we cannot be sure how soon the COVID-19 situation will improve, we must do the necessary to curb COVID-19 infections in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is to protect not just ourselves but also our loved ones, especially our seniors who are the most vulnerable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is the morally responsible and right thing to do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In fact, religious programmes over Warna 94.2FM, which were originally scheduled for Ramadan, have been brought forward for the benefit of seniors in the community who might not be as internet savvy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I commend our asatizah for stepping up to this new mode of religious guidance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope younger family members can also assist and ensure that this online religious content reach our older generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I also hope that the community benefits from the daytime infotainment programmes in the Malay media that help to reiterate how we can all help to stay safe and curb the spread of COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our Fatwa Committee, chaired by Mufti, has paved the way for how we can and must continue to adapt in the practice of our religion to the context and challenges that we face.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are indeed fortunate to have religious and community leaders who are open and progressive, can provide clear guidance to help the community address immediate challenges, and can rally and unite the community in times of crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A progressive religious leadership is also one that is able to grapple with increasingly complex issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, our asatizah are also working with medical professionals to develop religiously and medically sound advice for our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Working Group members have helped to communicate the scientific and religious reasons for precautionary measures we need to take in our mosques and our social interactions, such as at weddings, and how we can all protect ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, Dr Norhisham Main of Ng Teng Fong General Hospital appeared alongside Mufti in an online talk show to explain the closing of mosques from the medical perspective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Working Group is also actively discussing plans for Ramadan and how Ramadan can continue to be spiritually engaging for the community while we continue to observe safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will share more of these plans in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This collaboration between our asatizah and the medical professionals provides more holistic guidance for our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   COVID-19 has disrupted our daily as well as religious lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, changing our social norms to protect ourselves and the people around us does not make us any less of a Muslim or diminish our cultural identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Similarly, our inability to perform Friday prayers during our COVID-19 battle does not mean that we have lost our faith or our religious way of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the Mufti said, the Muslim community doing their bit to keep everyone safe is, in and of itself, one of the noblest thing that we can do as Muslims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: He also said that our togetherness and sense of community must remain strong in our hearts even though we must keep apart.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our asatizah’s progressive approach has helped us examine religious traditions critically and apply them in today’s circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Because of this, we were able to move decisively while others were still deliberating the way forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Given the crisis will be long-drawn, I urge all our asatizah to rally together in continued efforts to strengthen the resilience and confidence of the community through the challenges ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will help the community cope with this challenging period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More details will be shared by the Taskforce when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We acknowledge that it will take some time for us to overcome COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But, as one people, we must be ready to make adjustments to all facets of life, including our religious life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must persevere, so that we can emerge stronger after this crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The livelihoods of many Singaporeans have been affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, ensuring asatizah remain relevant and earn an income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will work with mosques and the Islamic Education Centres and Providers (IECP) to intensify efforts to ensure that asatizah remain relevant during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Asatizah must continue to play a critical role in guiding the community through Islamic education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To do this, mosques will conduct more online programmes and support home-based learning for aLIVE madrasahs and other Islamic learning classes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will also develop a toolkit to help IECPs move their learning online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am glad to see that some home-based Quran teachers are already having lessons via teleconference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These efforts will ensure asatizah continue to conduct their lessons, and draw an income during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, strengthening upskilling of our asatizah and preparing them for beyond the crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We encourage asatizah to tap on the various schemes, such as the SkillsFuture Credit as well as the enhanced Self-Employed Persons (SEP) Training Support Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This effort to upskill our asatizah is tied to the launch of the Career Map and Competency Framework (CCF) which I talked about during the Committee of Supply Debates last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The CCF was recommended by COFA and will provide an overarching framework to raise the professionalism of the asatizah sector and create more career pathways and opportunities for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will provide more details later this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many asatizah depend on direct contributions from their students or followers for their income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will work with relevant agencies to help asatizah affected by the downturn tap on schemes in the Resilience Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Muis will also reach out to asatizah through its partners, such as Pergas and IECPs, to raise awareness of these schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will guide the asatizah through the application process and facilitate any appeals from asatizah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, I encourage the community to continue their support for our asatizah and mosques.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our mosques are heavily dependent on donations from the community and, with the closure of mosques, the income of mosques is surely affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As such, MUIS is developing a platform to make it easier for the community to make online donations to the mosques, including those who would like to donate on a regular basis, such as through PayLah and GIRO.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The system is expected to be launched before Ramadan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As I urge the community to play its part to continue to support our mosques, I am also glad to share that MUIS will take the lead to support mosques in the following ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am heartened to see that some segments of the community have already stepped up to support our asatizah during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS) started the Gracious Package, a fund that provides some supplementary financial support for asatizah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During this period, eligible asatizah may receive a one-off payment of up to $400, and up to $300 per month, for the next six months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS and the SGTeguhBersatu Taskforce will work closely with these MMOs to ensure that our asatizah receive the support they require during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to the support for asatizah, our madrasahs will also do more to support students and ensure learning can be carried out smoothly even with the safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Like national schools, from Wednesday, our madrasahs will also transit to home-based learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will work with madrasahs to lend devices to madrasah students who may not have personal devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: If necessary, students may still come to the madrasahs if their parents are working in essential services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will also extend the application window for the Progress Fund Madrasah Assistance Scheme (PROMAS) to support madrasah students who may require financial assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our community will have to be psychologically prepared that they may not be able to partake in community breaking of fast at mosques or perform the nightly terawih congregational prayers at the mosques as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For many Muslims, Ramadan is not just a time to reflect and grow spiritually, but also to show care and compassion to all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must remember these values as we safeguard our loved ones and our countrymen from the virus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Let us be serious in implementing the precautionary measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A good number of locally transmitted cases could have been avoided if people had been more socially responsible by avoiding gatherings and crowds and staying at home when unwell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Adjust our daily routine, such as avoiding going to the market on weekends and going when it is not crowded instead and eat at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Wear a mask and see a doctor if we are unwell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our community must be part of the solution, not the problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is what we must do as a Community of Success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): This COVID-19 episode is an important opportunity for us reaffirm our fundamental values as a community and apply them to contemporary challenges, adapt and emerge stronger, both as a community and as a nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It takes a whole-of-community effort to overcome the challenges we face today.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: The saying goes that a week is a long time in politics.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: COVID-19 has shown us that a week is an eternity in a pandemic.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: As the coronavirus continues to rage through countries worldwide, it leaves a trail of destruction – claiming lives, industries, businesses and, of course, jobs.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: The Resilience and Solidarity Budgets are therefore most welcome indeed and will be a tremendous source of encouragement to the many who have been adversely affected.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I have, nevertheless, solicited feedback from people across multiple industry sectors to offer suggestions on how these extraordinary provisions can be further refined.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Some of the ideas I raise may come across as unorthodox but may have merits so I air them here in the spirit of collective innovation.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: These suggestions pertain to three aspects – generating work, stimulating spending and supporting SMEs.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Like many other people, my calendar has become blissfully clear with many events postponed indefinitely, or cancelled entirely.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: While the Government has introduced many schemes to provide industries with cash flow during this critical period, another approach may be to generate actual work so that industries can still chug along.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: For example, training programmes, workshops and conferences should still proceed by migrating online, thereby allowing event organisers and trainers to maintain their business, while gaining valuable experience in digitalisation.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: If the Government Ministries proceed with their original calendar of events in the coming months, training programmes and outreach campaigns, it sends a strong signal that it is business as usual, and supporting industries will also respond with creative online provisions.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: These events can still involve the production of conference materials that can be delivered to attendees, thereby also generating demand for additional services.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: If our Government Ministries and agencies continue to commission work rather than take a "wait and see" approach, the private sector will also follow its lead and this will create opportunities for smaller businesses to earn some revenue.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Another suggestion pertains to paying for work already done.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Many Government contracts have been halted with work done half way by contractors.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Contractually, payments may not be due but it would be a positive gesture for the Government to see if they can pay for work already completed or reimbursement for expenses incurred by contractors.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: As individual departments within Ministries may not have the discretion to make such decisions independently, some high level directive on this front would be a helpful signalling effect.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: The next suggestion relates to stimulating spending by consumers.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: With the recent lull in consumer spending and understandable dip in consumer confidence, retailers are, obviously, bleeding.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: The Government’s efforts to help with daily expenses in the form of one-off cash payouts and expenses for families will certainly help to ease families’ consumption needs.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Should the effects of the ongoing crisis persist for longer, more vouchers can be issued at a later juncture.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: While this is a somewhat unorthodox suggestion, the Government is in fact no stranger to vouchers as it has previously gifted past and present National Servicemen with S$100 NS50 vouchers as part of the NS50 Recognition Package.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: These NS50 vouchers could be used at more than 6,000 participating outlets and services, including major grocery stores and dining chains and indeed boosted revenue for these participating companies.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Moving on to supporting SMEs, feedback from these businesses suggests that cash flow is their biggest issue.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I would, therefore, like to echo Labour Chief Ng Chee Meng's call for the aid to come sooner.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: For the SMEs that still can generate some revenue even during the pandemic, they are now faced with unanticipated expenses.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Those that involve interfacing with customers such as F&B establishments are now finding that masks, sanitisers and disposable ware are a rapidly ballooning expense and need help to keep the costs of such items low.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, Government grant audit systems need to adapt to the digital environment as well.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: While training sessions are now encouraged to shift online, contractors now need to provide and record a full eight hours of online interaction.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: However, this does not take into account the fact that online training is more effective when it adopts a mixture of approaches such as flipped learning or blended learning.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: A mere replication of face-to face training will not work well in digital learning.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Or in this case, how many Singaporeans does it take to reset a circuit breaker?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: When we were first in this House no 18 February, the lights were still on, perhaps, flickering a little bit, but nothing to be too worried about.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Deputy Prime Minister Heng, at that time, introduced the Unity Budget, much like a new starter installed into a flickering light.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But we also had plans to quickly move towards LED lighting and solar panelling, to be better prepared for the future.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Yet, almost soon after, we had a power trip.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It turned on the emergency lighting so that Singaporeans would not stumble.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Soon after, we realised that the emergency lights only worked indoors.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And to get help, we needed to venture out a little further.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must not, however, overload our circuit, even though we hope to reset it as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: During this period, we must bite the bullet and adhere to the circuit breaker rules.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We need to make sure that our collective actions add up.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Just like a trip in the system, we all need to switch off before resetting the circuits, or risk tripping or worst still, shorting the entire circuit.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, every time we leave our house during this month for purposes beyond what is essential, we are literally tripping the system again.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: That would put the flash light to naught, as a catastrophic failure or ground fault would blow up the circuit, and would cost us exponentially – in economic as well as human costs.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, the answer is, it takes all Singaporeans to reset the circuits.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It takes all of us so that the drawdown from our reserves will be worthwhile, so that we do not end up bankrupting ourselves because of irresponsible actions that individuals may take.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The next point I would like to make a something that I am glad that Deputy Prime Minister Heng touched on.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And that is the long-term mental health impact of this crisis.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The scale of COVID-19 is unprecedented and our three Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets are also unprecedented to address the impact of this virus on lives and livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With the circuit breaker announced, a mother remarked, "Before schools close, my kids had a 1% chance of contracting COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Now, we have home-based learning starting Wednesday, and us working from home, I have a 99% chance of either going crazy or suffering a stroke." But on a more serious note, many of the little comforts that we took for granted in our daily lives will not be possible in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Habits like going to our favourite coffee shop; for our elders, going down for a chat; mingling, having a beer the end of the day.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Even spiritual comforts like going to our religious institutions have not been possible for some time.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Today is the beginning of Holy Week for Christians.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is the climax of the Christian year, but yet our churches are closed.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And this creates a major impact on the mental health of people who see these little things as comfort in their week, in their daily lives.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On Friday, I shared on my social media, a correspondence that I had with a friend who works as a frontline doctor.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: He told me that he had never at his age considered the need to look at will, to plan ahead for his young family.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: He was worried because he said that being on the frontline, he could see daily, the number of cases that were coming in.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: He could also see the patients who are not getting better or perhaps getting worse before they could get better.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: He could see his co-workers under pressure as well, having spent month after month working to combat this virus.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For him and many of the healthcare workers.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To be watching as people grow in numbers, as the infection numbers go up, as pressures on them grow, as the number of deaths may unfortunately increase, despite the best of their efforts.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is something that we have to be conscious about.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And I told him that I really hope that that will that he wrote, and perhaps, that many other healthcare professionals have decided to do so, would not be put to use anytime soon, that they would have a long and healthy life ahead of them; and he would be able to spend many more happy years with his wife as well as his young daughter.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Tthey never expected to be in this situation, to feel a sense of loss to feel that there is nothing for them to look forward to daily or worrying about how they are going to feed their families.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And for many of them, they had never planned for this this rainy day.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It will have an economic toll over the long term.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It will have a toll on family life over the long term as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, once again, let me thank all the healthcare workers and all frontline personnel for the hard work they have done so far to keep Singapore safe for all of us.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to thank all Singaporeans for working together, failing which, we would not be here today.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is with a heavy yet grateful heart that I rise to support this Supplementary Resilience and Solidarity Budget.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It has only been a few weeks since we concluded the Debate on our annual Budget Statement.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the short period since, the COVID-19 crisis has escalated and I had been hoping that the worst is over.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Around the world, hundreds of thousands of people have been infected and tens of thousands have died.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is an unprecedented global health, financial and social crisis.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The world, as we knew it, has changed drastically.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Here in Singapore, in our day-to-day lives, while there have been some changes to our routines, we have not yet experienced the magnitude of the impact many other countries have.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hopefully, we will be able to continue to buy time with these supportive measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: No one knows how long or how deep the crisis will be.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad that Deputy Prime Minister Heng has given all of us the assurance that additional measures or the extension of announced measures will be considered should the crisis be prolonged.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding these uncertainties, let us strive to have our businesses to resume activities and recover as quickly as possible with all the latest additional measures in place and implemented successfully.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More businesses would collapse if sales remain stagnant or decline further.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must do what we can to minimise and slow the potential domino effect.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I applaud the schemes to support our businesses but the implementation would perhaps need some Government intervention.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, according to some stallholders and tenants, their landlords have not reduced rents for them despite these extraordinary circumstances.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The new legislation to ensure that landlords pass on property tax rebates in full to their tenants would help businesses to a certain degree.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the other hand, some landlords complain that stallholders and tenants have delayed paying their rents or that they have lost rentals due to rising vacancies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Yet, they have to continue to meet their mortgage payments to the banks and finance companies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I suppose everyone has his difficulties and plight and the root of the problem is revenue loss and the resulting cashflow problems.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We would need to continue to encourage enterprises and investments and I urge the Government, its agencies and various private sector firms which may have put some projects on hold, to proceed to award contracts and carry out their plans, all of which will help to stimulate our economy and create jobs.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the meantime, we must all do our part to boost the level of hygiene in our public areas.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must heed the advice not only during this trying period but also beyond and adopt such hygienic practices as our way of life to reduce the spread of diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: From the correct handwashing technique to utilising and disposing of tissues properly, new norms for social interactions and use of public facilities, how will the Government ensure compliance?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What will be done to enhance the hygiene at the hawker centres and public toilets?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How do we encourage more tray returns and get food handlers and stall holders to wear hair caps and spit-guards?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, how will the Government work with property owners to ensure cleanliness, especially for food and retail establishments, hawker centres, coffeeshops and public areas?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These efforts will require quickly stepping up the professionalisation of the cleaning sector with training and certification.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The crisis also highlights how dependent we are on foreign workers to maintain a clean Singapore and how we need to expedite the adoption of technology to overcome the problem of limited manpower resources.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The COVID-19 crisis has also brought to the fore the urgency of ramping up our own food supply as part of a set of measures to enhance our food security.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Supply chains have been disrupted and are under stress due to lockdowns and the impact of the virus on logistics staff and workers around the world.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Government share how much the impact has affected our food supply?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can we attract more Singaporeans to this sector and what are the challenges faced by our local farms?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How are we tapping on new techniques and technology to overcome our local constraints?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   	Many countries around the world are currently in a state of emergency, imposing border controls, no-fly rules and local movement controls.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Because of the extreme panic, the financial sector is also abnormal.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Stocks and bonds, and even gold, were sold, leading to the collapse of many companies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The collapse in oil prices has made the global economy worse.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While we cannot predict how long the crisis will last, we need to remain positive, prepare for the global recovery and stay ahead of the competition.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must pay attention to the dynamics of our environment.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We are facing a turning point in history.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The way the world works will change dramatically.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We also need to work with countries around the world to fight the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even the Palestinian Islamic Resistance Movement (Hamas), which controls the Gaza Strip, has joined forces with Israel to fight the outbreak.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I wish to express gratitude for the hard work put in by Prime Minister Lee, Deputy Prime Minister Heng, the Inter-Ministerial COVID-19 task force and our civil and public servants who have worked tirelessly to manage the COVID-19 situation and put in place the necessary support and assistance for Singaporeans during this difficult period.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am heartened and moved by the extent of assistance provided in the Resilience Budget and now the Solidarity Budget – for employees, employers, business owners, the self-employed, job-seekers, the unemployed, and low-income and middle income families, among other specific segments of our society.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As the various assistance schemes and initiatives are being rolled out, Singaporeans will need to stay resilient and innovative in keeping their heads above water as the challenges imposed by the COVID-19 outbreak will continue to plague us for many more months ahead.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my speech, I wish to speak on three matters which residents have raised with me.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One, plight of the self-employed and future of the gig economy; two, employment opportunities for job-seekers and school leavers; and three, fees and loans payment.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, on the plight of the self-employed and future of the gig economy.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will certainly help SEPs during this difficult period.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While the current SIRS scheme is useful, we should never rule out the possibility of other possible crises from happening in the future and which may put one's income-earning potential at risk once more, which is particularly more likely for SEPs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, my concern is what happens after the nine months.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will our SEPs be able to find a more permanent form of employment that will provide them with a more stable income in future?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can we encourage greater participation in the SEP Training Support Scheme and other employment assistance schemes, such as Career Trial or Attach-and-Train?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can a more targeted employment assistance be rendered to SEPs to help them secure a more permanent and stable form of employment for the future?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My other concern is regarding businesses that are severely affected because of the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It will be very difficult for business owners to recoup losses incurred during this period, and they may decide to scale down their operations considerably and cut costs eventually.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
