text: One of the ways in which they may decide to scale down their operations and cut costs, would be to let go of permanent hires and outsource work to freelancers or those doing gig work.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This may lead to a growth of the gig economy, which may be acceptable during healthy economic growth.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But during periods of crises, such as now, we will once again have income insecurity among the freelancers and those doing gig work.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What more can we do to help them have better income security despite periods of crises?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Two, on employment opportunities for job-seekers and school leavers.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am reassured that the Government is looking to help job-seekers, in particular, first-time job-seekers just entering the job market.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is a very challenging time to be looking for employment, especially when you do not have sufficient work experience.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even among my students in the University, some have shared their difficulty in securing a more permanent employment because of the current economic uncertainty.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Those particularly affected are in the hospitality and tourism as well as design sectors.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While the SG United Traineeship programme will be able to provide our young people with opportunities to gain invaluable work experience, to enhance their employability and eventually land a relatively secure job, our students do question whether the few years they spent in a specific programme preparing for a job in an industry which is not able to provide employment for them has been a futile effort.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that under the SG United Traineeship programme, recent University, Polytechnic and ITE graduates who are looking to gain employment in an industry that is different from the one they have been trained in, will be given recognition for their academic training and qualification as well as related work experience, and can be accorded some form of recognition for these when they are granted employment in a different sector thereafter.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It helps to ease the financial burden for new graduates who are facing difficulty in securing employment during this period.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, what about late payment charges for other fees, such as telco and utilities, where consumption is likely to increase as more Singaporeans work from home?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can they also be waived for residents for a period of six months or so?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can the childcare or student care fees already paid during this period be redirected to pay for the later months when childcare or student care services are in full operations again?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At this juncture, Mr Deputy Speaker, please allow me to speak in Malay.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   The COVID-19 outbreak has transformed our lives.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most of us did not expect the advent of this pandemic and the resulting changes.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It has impacted our income, jobs and businesses within a very short period of time.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many were also unprepared to deal with the challenges that came along with it.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that the self-employed or freelancers can make use of this opportunity to upgrade their skills and gain relevant knowledge and experience, which will help to improve their chance of getting permanent jobs in the future.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that our community can make use of this time and available opportunities to enhance their skills, knowledge and experience, and plan their career wisely.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is a Malay idiom that advises one to “do any job that is available first until something better comes along”.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English) Mr Deputy Speaker, the COVID-19 outbreak has changed many things and thwarted many plans that we had.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In response, the Government has pulled out the stops and introduced extensive and generous assistance packages, schemes and initiatives to help Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak has changed many things, but it is also an opportunity for us to make some much-needed changes ourselves.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the words of Thomas Carlyle, "Permanence, perseverance and persistence in spite of all obstacles, discouragements and impossibilities: It is this that, in all things, distinguishes the strong from the weak", and I am confident we will emerge from this crisis even stronger as a nation.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For many of us, these first three months of 2020 have felt like a "horror suspense" movie that keeps us anxious and on the edge till the end.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Except, we are not watching this movie – we are living it, and we still do not know when is the end and how it would end.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Many people – some I know and some I do not – have reached out for help as their lives are turned upside down.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: An acquaintance almost killed himself last Monday because he has lost all his gigs as an event emcee.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: A single mother of a young boy, who lives with an elderly mother, has had her salary cut by 50%.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Many migrant workers struggle to pay for their daily essentials because there is no more overtime pay to make.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, the crisis illuminates long-term cracks that we must address decisively for a good and strong rebound as a nation.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Every crisis is an opportunity to observe the cracks, rectify the causes and become more prepared for the future.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: First, mental health of our people in this crisis and, second, low-income households who will bear the brunt of the crisis.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But I do not think we are doing enough.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Pandemics can trigger new psychiatric symptoms even in the healthy.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Safe distancing, constant fear and anxiety, the loss of loved ones, job losses, industrial failures will wear down our national psyche.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Our senior citizens are left to battle loneliness as community activities cease.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: A Straits Times report yesterday confirmed that some living with mental illnesses have suffered a relapse or that their conditions have worsened.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I also worry for our office-holders and civil servants who bear the weight of spearheading the fight.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I read the recent news of the German State Minister’s suicide over COVID-related stress with alarm and sadness.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Now, more than ever, we must prioritise mental health support.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, a mental health disaster is starting in Wuhan just as the Coronavirus crisis is easing.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Prime Minister Lee has said that it might take several years for COVID-19 to run its course.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For us, the psychological toll has barely started.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This proposal has been raised by mental health experts themselves.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: A Budget should also be set aside without delay to implement public health experts’ recommendations on mental health to avert a further public health crisis.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I urge the Government to broadcast through all its publicity channels, practical advice on maintaining mental well-being in various COVID-related situations.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The NHS Inform in Scotland dedicates an entire section of their website to this.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I hope it will be strategically designed and implemented to continue beyond this crisis.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I also repeat my call made at the COS that the Government consider allowing the first mental healthcare consultation for all Singaporeans to be free so as to incentivise help-seeking.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We must enable quality mental healthcare and subsidise fees for individuals whose mental health has suffered due to COVID-19, especially for lower income households.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: More resources must also be funnelled to organisations, such as Samaritans of Singapore, AWARE and Silver Ribbon, whose free counselling services are likely to become strained in the days to come.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Last but not least, I urge the Public Services Division to provide the necessary mental health support for all our civil servants and healthcare workers through this intense period.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I do not underestimate the imminent cash flow struggle that many Singaporeans face – my own friends and family are treading water.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But lower income families will suffer more than most.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Adam (not his real name) is a hotel cleaner in his 50s.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Because of the crisis, he has had no work since 25 March.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond Social Services has reported that their members who are disproportionately engaged in low-paid and precarious forms of work have suffered a sharp drop in household income, or lost their jobs altogether.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Even in good times, he took home about $1,600 each month.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: One thousand four hundred dollars went to his wife for groceries and household expenses.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: That amount is not always enough for them and their four young children.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Such want is normal in parts of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Household expenses for the average Singaporean household in the lowest income quintile have consistently exceeded income for the last 10 years.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Twenty-seven thousand of the poorest households in Singapore have, on average, $246 in savings per household member.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Our low-wage workers have always been insecure, and this insecurity will be exacerbated in an economic crisis.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, the measures announced are not enough to bail out a low-income household that loses its income, especially for those with several dependants.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, I welcome the change to a longer period of assistance of at least six months from the usual one to four months for ComCare Short to Medium Term Assistance.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Angie (not her real name) is a widow in her 60s who is unfit to work.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For one year, she received ComCare Financial Assistance in short tranches and had to apply for renewal at the end of each tranche whilst waiting up to a month for a reply without financial support.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For two whole months, she could not afford food, bus fare or essential medical treatment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: If processing times are challenging in normal times, they will reach breaking point at crunch time.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I am relieved that we are exercising flexibility and finally allowing for online applications from this week onwards.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to getting help to those who need it fast, we must reduce the administrative load on our Social Service Agencies (SSAs) so that they can focus in supporting Singaporeans affected.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Given these priorities, we may have to trade off the luxury of deep-diving every case to test its deservedness.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For applicants, this also cuts out the need to apply in-person and prove their suffering over and over again.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: With that, I would like to make two recommendations.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Second, make help unconditional and reduce the amount of evidence required to prove to MSF that the applicant is struggling.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, MSF officers could be given the power to investigate end-users whom they suspect are abusing the system.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: More immediate relief can also come in the form of HDB rental waivers till the end of 2020 as well as further rebates to S&CC fees.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Food security is another big concern, Mr Deputy Speaker, despite the best efforts from charities.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For Singaporeans in the lowest income quintile, 49% of income is spent on food.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, F&B businesses are suffering and the Resilience Budget may be insufficient to prevent the industry from going under.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, just as the Government galvanised a multi-sectoral effort with the hotels to accommodate returning Singaporeans for their 14-day self-isolation, I urge the Government to work with the F&B sector and food delivery companies to provide food to all families like Adam's and Angie's for the period of this crisis as a national response, not a fragmented approach like it is now.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: It ensures absolute food security for our lower income households and frees up household liquidity whilst supporting our local F&B businesses and self-employed delivery riders.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The very nature of frontline work like Adam's entails a higher risk of COVID-19 infection.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Adam and his family share 20 square metres of living space in a 1-room rental flat.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: If he is infected through work or job search, his family will not be spared.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Their home opens into an enclosed corridor, along which several other families live.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Infection risk is simply a logical consequence of overcrowding.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Such crowded living conditions create a ripe environment for infection which in turn could spread to the wider community.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The World Health Organization strongly recommends that national strategies be developed and implemented to prevent and reduce household crowding.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Our vulnerable families should be housed in flats with features to protect public health such as ventilated corridors, rooms to enable distancing and separate elevators serving different floors.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I wish to record my deep concern regarding the isolation of 20,000 of our migrant workers in these cramped facilities.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This must not become the "Diamond Princess" on our shores.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Alternative and more favourable living arrangements in spaces freed up from the circuit breaker measures must be urgently considered to avoid a large-scale tragedy of infected cases and mortality.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We must re-home our most vulnerable in conducive spaces.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We may not be able to do that for all during this crisis but we can do it in time for the next, and our people will be more resilient for it. "All of us are only as strong as our weakest link", said Prime Minister Lee at the Extraordinary Virtual G20 Leaders' Summit.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, unity is strength, yet inequality is our weakest link in this fight against COVID-19 and to our future as a strong, united Singapore.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The short-term measures announced in the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets are essential.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Our reserves are meant exactly for times like these.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Before I conclude, I want to thank every healthcare worker, civil servant, social worker, community practitioner, volunteer and everyone who has worked tirelessly and selflessly to support fellow Singaporeans and residents affected by COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But please do take care of your mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: You must not pour from an empty cup, because the work you do is important for us, for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This amount has increased even more with the announcement of the Solidarity Budget today.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Today, I would like to touch on three concerns arising from the people around me during this situation.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: On 3 April, it was announced that to enhance safe distancing measures, Singaporeans were encouraged to stay at home and to generally avoid leaving the house.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: At supermarkets, it is not uncommon to find people stocking up on their food supplies despite the Government's message that there will be ample supplies.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Given the surge in demand, online grocery companies are also facing difficulties in fulfilling orders.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Some have resorted to placing limits on the number of items and weight in order to cope with the demand.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Taxi and private car hire drivers are allowed to make home deliveries to meet increased demand.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, even with such measures in place, these companies are often very stretched and are not able to cater to more customers when their delivery slots are full.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: With more Singaporeans encouraged to stay at home, we need to find ways to increase grocery deliveries in order to take the pressure off physical supermarket outlets.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: When Singaporeans know that delivery slots and essential items on online supermarket platforms are available and not difficult to secure, they will be more assured, hence, alleviating the crowds at physical supermarket locations.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, it will keep more Singaporeans home and safe.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The second one is with regards to public transport social distancing during school dismissal hours.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: With the new measures enforced, schools and Institutes of Higher Learning will be conducting full home-based learning from 8 April onwards.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, when home-based learning stops, we can consider staggering school hours even more, just like how we encourage the staggering of office hours to deal with peak hour traffic on public transports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, public transport is packed with students from different schools during their commute in the morning and when school ends.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This has resulted in large crowds in the trains and buses during such periods, contrary to the concept of social distancing, which the Government has been advocating.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: While it may not be feasible to enforce social distancing on trains, the Government can consider staggering school hours even more to reduce the number of students traveling on public transport at the same time.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, I would like to share my thoughts on sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sports has the ability to transcend boundaries and provide immeasurable benefits to one's well-being.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sport Singapore's core purpose is to inspire the Singapore spirit and transform Singapore through sports and they have done well thus far.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Behind the scenes, there are many sports enterprises which contribute to the success of Singapore as a vibrant sporting hub.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, sports-related activities tend to bring in a large number of participants and spectators from around the world, boosting tourism figures.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I have heard from many sports enterprises about the issues they are facing with their businesses in this period.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: These include sporting event companies, mega gyms, clubs and even social clubs.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: These companies have been affected since the outbreak of the pandemic in January 2020.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: And with every new measure being implemented to help flatten the curve, it has been harder for these companies to continue operations given the drop in number of patrons and students of such establishments.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, many of them face a huge loss of revenue and to manage their bottom line, cost cutting measures were taken in order for them to stay afloat.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Rent and manpower-related issues are the largest component of expenses.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Some enterprises received rent relief from their landlords.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, dealing with manpower-related expenses such as salary has been more tricky.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In some instances, salaries have been cut in order to minimise the number of layoffs.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Since 24 March, where the advisory was to suspend all children and youth-centric sports programmes, most companies are facing zero revenues.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: When the circuit breaker measures were announced, it was seen that there would be mandatory closures of many sporting establishments on 7 April.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: These SMEs which are considered "non-essential services" will face a larger strain on their finances.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: After the circuit breaker, if the regulatory measures in the sports sector still remain the same as before the circuit breaker, many companies in this affected sector will still be facing a high loss of revenue, and in some cases, no revenue given that recovery will be a protracted process in light of these disruptions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I rise in support of the Supplementary Budgets.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The Resilience and Solidarity Budgets are a very significant addition to this year's Budget.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Earlier in February, Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced the Unity Budget that included $6.4 billion worth of measures to cope with COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I am grateful that the Government swiftly and significantly increased the amount of help given.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Most of the concerns that residents raised to me at the beginning were addressed in the landmark Resilience Budget and now the Solidarity Budget as well.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Cash flow was a key concern for families and businesses I encountered.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: At my weekly Meet-the-People Session two weeks ago, I recall meeting several self-employed residents whose incomes were drastically reduced because of COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: One such case was a man who is the sole breadwinner of his young family, working as a Grab driver.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: His wife is medically certified unfit for work.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: His children are very young, with the youngest being only five months old.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: He had to take a break earlier in the year after being hit by a car – it was a hit-and-run incident – and upon returning to work, he received few assignments as a result of COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Most often, he had no cash to take home.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: That night, he told me his children had been hungry for the entire day and were waiting for him to bring food home.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Of course, we immediately went to the 24-hour FairPrice nearby, and bought them groceries and milk powder to tide through the night.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I know families like the one I just described will benefit from these measures.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These enhanced measures, amongst others, such as the one-year waiver of Government fees and charges, and reprieve from loan repayments, will increase cash flow for them and over a more sustained period of time.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I must say that our Government and leaders have been very focused, single-mindedly, wholeheartedly, battling this COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And as we thought that we have gained grounds in battling down this COVID-19, I think, all of the sudden, we realise that there is a spike in the infection cases.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: It is almost as if we have been working so hard to keep our house in order but because of what is happening around us, around the world, we are seeing this spike of infection.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I can only imagine how demoralising it could be for our frontliners, for all the Government officials, the social workers, everyone, who have been involved in this fight.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And therefore, I must express my deepest appreciation and gratitude to all of you who have worked so hard.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And I feel that personally, when I see the measures being introduced, it is almost as if whenever we see a new problem appeared or a new gap that has emerged, immediately, our Government will find the resources to go and plug that gap and help Singaporeans to tide through.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I feel that this sincerity is something that we can see and I hope that all Singaporeans will be able to appreciate this.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is a very extraordinary time and we must continue to stand together to render our support.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Therefore, with all of these funds put aside to help Singaporeans, I think this is a very decisive move and a much needed one.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As we battle this unprecedented crisis, I am thankful that our past and present leaders have been judicious in managing our reserves, painstakingly saving up for "storms" like this and resisted siren calls in the past to spend our reserves.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Because of this, we can now confidently dip in to help Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: About two months have passed since we had our first COVID-19 case and the economic consequences are already dire.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We now have an extremely generous package to battle the virus.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But with the pandemic expected to last for up to a year or more, I wonder how many more packages we will need and how much more might we have to dip into our reserves for.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As much as I believe it is necessary for us to draw on our reserves to help Singapore and Singaporeans get through this storm, I wonder if this is also the beginning of a long slippery slope down.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Will we have enough to leave behind for our future generations?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: How do we moderate ourselves and is there a red line beyond which we shall not draw further from our reserves?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Essentially, how can we sustain help and at the same time, not deplete this pot of gold for our children and theirs?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In a crisis of this scale, Government's intervention is critical.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But we must also not diminish the power of individuals.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: All of us have the power to help and contribute towards a sustainable future for the next generation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Over the past months, we saw various ground up initiatives, such as sourcing and distributing masks and hand sanitisers to the elderly.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In recent weeks, we continue to see Singaporeans coming forth to offer ideas and support.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: A call for volunteers to help with form filling and crowd management saw many responded.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Similarly, we now have volunteers who have stepped forth to man the reusable mask collection centres.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Others took their own initiative to collate and circulate lists of useful official websites offering critical information during this period of information explosion.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This helps Singaporeans to get the right information from the right channel and in a most timely manner.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Because of these big-hearted Singaporeans who volunteered, we have been able to pool community resources, close gaps and do more for those who need help.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But the potential for individuals to play a part is more than this.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: If there is a silver lining to this crisis, it is the opportunity for us to show our solidarity, transform our capabilities and strengthen our resilience.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Most immediately, as we approach the "circuit breaker" starting tomorrow, we should all stay home and do whatever we must to encourage our family and friends to stay home.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Simply, if we do not cooperate and the spread worsens, this one month "breaker" and the pain that everyone must endure will be a wasted sacrifice.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We will then have to draw from our reserves further and leave even lesser for our future generations.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, care for yourself, care for others, stay home to show our solidarity with those on the frontline.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The hesitance is understandable as they are preoccupied with the immediate challenges and as they still harbour hopes that they can return to their jobs once this crisis "blows over".

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: However, I would urge that we keep the "big picture" in mind.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Even without this COVID-19, the advent of digital economy is certain.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, why not take this opportunity to get ourselves ready for that inevitable future?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Similarly, enterprises of all sizes can take this opportunity to transform.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As companies get hit by COVID-19, many realised that they were not ready to offer their services and products online.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Taking the enrichment education sector for example, I came across an informal survey by a fledgling platform company Beecraft.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Amongst those surveyed, they cited financial support being most important in helping them drive their digitalisation effort.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hon colleagues in this House will know of the many schemes that IMDA offers.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: With COVID-19, the imperative for digital transformation cannot be any clearer.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Just as it is an opportunity for the IMDA to step in and catalyse the transformation, I hope companies will take this opportunity to make use of the support available and up their own game.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is a period of great many adjustments.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Government is adjusting, so are businesses and people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We are heading into the "circuit breaker" for at least a month.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I am glad that our thoughtful Government made sure that essential services will continue so that life can go on.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But we also need to reduce the need for interactions and administrative load on some of our public agencies.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Based on case trends at our weekly Meet-the-People Sessions, mainly mine, could financial assistances, including ComCare and MediFund that are expiring during this "circuit breaker" period be automatically renewed for another month?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Could the social visit passes and long-term visit passes of Singaporeans' foreign family members that will be expiring in this period also be automatically renewed for another month?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In essence, could Government processes that typically see high public interface be adjusted so that Singaporeans in need may have peace of mind as we all hunker down during this period?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: (In Mandarin):   Amidst the COVID-19 outbreak, the global economy is tumbling drastically.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The series of packages are timely, for individuals, families, workers and businesses.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We can do so because our Government has been planning for rainy days over the years, allowing us to acquire this economic capability.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Our reserves are strategic assets accumulated over a long time.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Generations of Singapore leaders have been practising fiscal prudence to achieve sustainable economic growth.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Although faced with political pressure, the Government has been upholding the principle of tapping on reserves only during extraordinary times.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As the pandemic worsens and creates multiple external shocks, economic activities have also been affected.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: At this critical moment, the Government drew decisively on reserves to stimulate the economy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: However, the battle against COVID-19 will be long-drawn and the unprecedented fiscal expenditure has also caused some concerns.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: With the unexpected advent of COVID-19, we have seen many community organisations voluntarily make and distribute reusable masks for the elderly and the vulnerable.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We have also seen many Singaporeans express their sincere gratitude to frontline healthcare workers, encouraging them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This demonstrates the warmth in our society and is commendable.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Besides the Government, public agencies and communities, businesses and individuals should also play their part.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: During this period, we must first take care of our own health and stay at home.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is the best contribution you can make to the country now.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Ensuring our own health is the best we can do for our healthcare workers, allowing them to see the light at the end of the tunnel and take a breather.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Taking care of our health can also reduce the need to tap on our reserves.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is being accountable to our future generations.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Over the weekend, I took a walk in the hawker centre and talked to the residents.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Many of them were feeling a bit worried about the closing down of non-essential services, but they showed understanding nevertheless.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I think the more difficult the situation is, the more resilient Singaporeans should be.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is a chance to demonstrate our strength.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I believe as long as we are united and uphold our Singapore Spirit of solidarity, we will eventually beat this virus and emerge stronger.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: (In English): Over the weekend, I was at the hawker centres in MacPherson.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: If we can do this together, we can overcome and emerge stronger.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This was the point that I had wanted to bring up and appeal and I am happy for the adjustment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Resilience and Solidarity Budget demonstrates the Government's determination and resolve to minimise the impact of the COVID-19 crisis on jobs and the economy as best as it can.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At that age, Singaporeans would be planning for marriage or would be married with a child on the way or have at least a child to support.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some of their parents or in-laws might be retired and need their support too.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hence, allowing for auto-inclusion from 30 years old and above will greatly help to relieve the burden on affected families and also reduce the administrative workload on Government officers so that they can devote more resources to other urgent appeals.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, some unemployed residents hope to qualify for the COVID-19 Support Grant, which was targeted at employees who lost their jobs due to the contagion.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While they had not lost their jobs earlier due to COVID-19, the crisis has definitely made their ongoing job search much harder.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I feel that as long as they are actively looking for jobs, whether these are permanent or part-time positions or on fixed term contracts, or are still attending training, they should be also assisted under this Scheme.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   	The Resilience Package is to reduce the economic impact of the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) will help the self-employed to cope with the current difficulties.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Those who had lost their jobs even before the outbreak also appeal to the Government to accommodate them, so that they can receive the COVID-19 Support Grant, too.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): With stricter safe distancing measures and the greater vulnerability of our seniors, we would want our elderly to stay at home more.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we ensure that our needy seniors or seniors living alone can get the help they need?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How is the Government empowering VWOs to pool their resources to assist them, such as helping them to buy groceries or sending meals to them?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could we make better use of technology in this area?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I support the Resilience and Solidarity Budget and its measures to help our workers and the unemployed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There will be some who might fall through the cracks and need to be given special consideration in view of their particular circumstances.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I trust that our leaders would exercise due diligence and flexibility.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Allow me to begin my speech in Malay.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):   The COVID-19 crisis has evolved so rapidly and shaken us to the core.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This situation drove our Government to act swiftly and issue new regulations and legislation to contain the spread of this outbreak.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At the same time, the Government also coordinated support to assist those who are facing the fallout from this crisis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This began with the Unity Budget which was then supplemented with the Resilience Budget.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The Government also gave a commitment that there will be a sustained effort to help those facing difficulties due to the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The impact of this crisis is becoming clear and we can see many people from various job sectors being affected.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Within the Malay/Muslim community, those affected include Geylang Serai bazaar entrepreneurs and the asatizah.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Many Malay/Muslim workers, families and students also face challenges arising from this crisis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I think we need to have a targeted approach to assist the Malay/Muslim community and mobilise the resources within our community, like the Malay/Muslim bodies, to come up with holistic support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Therefore, I am heartened that the SGTeguhBersatu team was set up to ensure that the COVID-19 national assistance schemes will reach our community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am also glad to be involved in this task force.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I see opportunities for many of our community members to go to the ground and work hand-in-hand to help everyone ride through these difficult times.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For instance, one group that I am concerned with are the young people who are about to complete their studies and enter the workforce.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is likely that they will face difficulties getting suitable jobs with good pay.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Observers have said that the graduating Class of 2020 will be affected beyond the duration of this crisis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Their careers and income potential may be affected throughout their lifetime.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Therefore, there has to be sustained efforts to help them so that they can use this difficult period to continue upskilling and enhance their competitiveness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: These efforts can help new graduates gain employment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We must also ensure that young Malay/Muslims are aware of these available opportunities and make use of them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At the same time, I feel that Malay/Muslim bodies like MENDAKI and AMP can also play their part to strengthen support for these young people, perhaps through their available programmes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: MENDAKI, for instance, has the Future-Ready and mentoring programmes that can be enhanced to supplement the Government’s efforts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The Malay/Muslim community can be helped to seize available opportunities and can continue receiving support using the resources within our own community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: May these efforts help us overcome any challenges that come our way together and continue to contribute to the economic recovery and development of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In English): Just a few days ago, I met a resident seeking some assistance as he had lost his job in the midst of this COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He seemed disheartened but not defeated, and we spoke about the various support measures available.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He was the last resident I was meeting for the night and I heard a child’s voice as he walked out of my Branch.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: His wife and son were waiting for him outside.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I walked out too and saw a familiar face saying hello to me.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I had met the boy just a few weeks back when I sent some cupcakes over to his pre-school because we had cancelled the regular birthday celebrations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He was lively and happy, innocent and clearly oblivious to the challenges his parents were facing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It hit me how much things had changed since I last met the little boy, how fast things have become a lot more challenging in just a few weeks.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The issues his father is facing is not unique and I have met many residents in similar situations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At one point, especially before the announcement of the Resilience Budget, I was feeling rather helpless because people were really struggling and I was concerned if enough is being done to help them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Many felt that the measures were generous and gave much hope to different groups of people within the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, the challenges brought forth by COVID-19 is multi-faceted and the Government needs to also step in with various new legislation to make the system work.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It has become even more stark, in the past few days that the worst is not over.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Numbers of those infected by COVID-19 continue to rise and the Government has had to announce further measures, in particular the circuit breaker, to protect our people.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This will bring many things to a standstill and cause massive disruption to our routine affairs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Construction projects cannot proceed, cases in Court would have to be postponed and more businesses and more individuals will be affected further as non-essential services have to be shut down.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am therefore heartened that the Government has announced the Solidarity Budget to augment the existing support and, in particular, to address the side effects of the circuit breaker.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are so many aspects of life that would be affected especially in light of the recent measures, I would therefore like to ask how the Government plans to manage all the knock-on effects of the crisis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Would there be a coordinated effort to assess the challenges faced by the different sectors and come up with a recovery plan?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Are there lessons we could learn from the lockdown in other countries?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Further, it is apparent that more funds would have to be injected to continue to support businesses, individuals and families affected by the disruption.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am truly grateful for the stewardship of the Government as we navigate through these challenging, unchartered waters.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have always been so proud of being Singaporean but now more than ever, I am proud to be part of this great nation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It has been oft said that this is the crisis for this generation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We may not have to physically go to the battlefield and pick up weapons to fight the enemy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But we have our own burden to bear and we will do this together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: SGUnited is one of the taglines we have chosen to capture the spirit of togetherness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Let it not be mere lip service but an actual effort by all of us to do our part.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Let us not take advantage of each other and give indulgence to each other where possible.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We definitely have this compassion in us, as can be seen from the numerous ground-up initiatives by Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have heard of businesses and young people from different academic institutions banding together to put up a list of job and internship opportunities to help their peers who have had their overseas internships and studies cut short due to COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have seen Facebook posts from people personally offering to cook or give food to those who may be struggling during this period, so one would never go hungry.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The COVID-19 crisis has brought about carnage but, at the same time, also allowed for many good things to blossom.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This crisis is pushing us to do all the things we know we should have been doing but have resisted for so long.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some of us have championed flexible work arrangements and asked employers to allow for opportunities to work from home.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There was much inertia but now, we are pushed to look at digital solutions and make it happen.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For the longest time, we have wanted people to use their own containers to buy food from stalls or restaurants.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Now, we have been pushed to do so more pervasively as the "tabao" option will be a common feature.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Like many Singaporeans, I am anxious and overwhelmed with all that is happening.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, I am also hopeful as I have faith in the strength of this leadership and the compassion and resilience of the people.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Let us make the best of this crisis, learn the important lessons from the challenges that come our way and emerge stronger as a nation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I believe that all these additional budgetary measures will go a long way to assuring Singaporeans from all walks of life that the Government is doing its utmost best to help Singaporeans cope with the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the current situation, many Singaporeans whom I speak to appreciate the difficulties facing Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They urge the Government to persevere in finding a solution for the COVID-19 crisis and gave their assurance that they will work with the Government to break transmission.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In simple Chinese, they say " " I am confident that with the right political leadership and with strong support from our civil service, we will be able to overcome all challenges.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I acknowledge that many of the additional measures can only mitigate the financial struggles to hit Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Whatever the Government does, it will not and should not be seen as a measure to put Singaporeans back to the days before the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Nevertheless, I have two areas of concern which I wish to highlight for the Deputy Prime Minister's consideration.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many of my residents are affected and I speak for them.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This means that business owners who are directors and shareholders of the companies will get no help at all.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They are also not eligible for any financial support for the self-employed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many of them may be just small businessmen who own a small share in a company or a $1 share.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And they are also working as directors in the company.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: During this period, if their businesses are badly affected, surely, we can offer some help to these people by co-funding the wages of the working directors.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many self-employed persons who have done well in previous years have bought a property of higher value and they may now be reeling under the negative impact of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The fact that they have invested in their dream home, which is more expensive, does not mean that they will suffer less due to COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In fact, they may well be struggling even more to pay more in terms of their mortgage instalements.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For some of these self-employed persons (SEPs), this month, April, this month of suspension of activities mean they would have absolutely no income at all.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Besides tackling the medical crisis, governments around the world are rolling out emergency stimulus and support packages to keep their economies afloat.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These packages range from less than 1% of their GDPs to as high as 32%, for example, in the case of Germany.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Still, it is by any measure an enormous package and quite unprecedented for us.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On one hand, this massive injection of funds helps to boost confidence and goes some way in tackling the current and near-term economic challenges.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And as we enter today into the first day of this circuit breaker measure, our fight against COVID-19 here in Singapore enters a critical phase.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is reassuring to hear from Deputy Prime Minister Heng that the Government is able to and prepared to do even more in the future should the crisis drag on, as seen in the further measures just announced under the Solidarity Budget.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, on the other hand, we all know that our reserves are not unlimited and some had urged caution about dipping too deep into our national savings, although virtually all the people I have spoken to or I have interacted with over the past weeks have expressed appreciation for the various assistance schemes.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The worry is that no one knows how long this crisis will last and that we might need more funds further down the road.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the meantime, we must, of course, all do our part to minimise further spread of the disease and continue contributing to our community and economy in a socially responsible manner.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is of course good news to owners under financial pressure due to the impact from COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They can choose to defer just the principal amount or both the principal and interest payments.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand that it may be difficult for the banks and finance companies to consider waiving interest on the principal amounts.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Nonetheless, I hope MAS and the Government will consider persuading them to implement a reduced interest rate over this deferment period on those deferred amounts, or at least not to charge interest on the deferred principal amounts.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is probably in line with the fact that lending rates across the board are slowly reducing over the next few months.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This special deferment arrangement also, to my knowledge, does not currently extend to individuals with commercial or industrial property loans.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While owners are encouraged to discuss debt restructuring with their lenders, some guidelines for relief measures for this group would be helpful; and this way, the owners may, in turn, be able to extend arrangements for relief to their beleaguered tenants as well.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would also like to appeal for a little bit more assistance under the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I know that some new measures have just been announced under the Solidarity Budget.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But I would like consideration, perhaps, to be made for further help for SEPs who have more dependants.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would MOM consider taking into account the number of dependants supported by the SEPs?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: SEPs supporting young children, elderly or disabled family members would probably require additional financial assistance during this difficult time.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For SEPs who are also not auto-enrolled in the SIRS, I hope that the application and appeals process will be as expedient and as inclusive as possible.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would like to also bring up the special plight of private hire drivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the early days of the COVID crisis, there had been some calls in some quarters for those who had seen reduced employment, or been furloughed, to consider supplementing their income with private hire driving.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With this recent drastic reductions in social interaction and travel, many private hire drivers, along with regular taxi drivers, are facing severe constraints on their daily income.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Whilst taxi companies have announced rental rebates and waivers for their drivers, many private hire drivers are still bound to their rental agreements, and some who have taken private leases on their vehicles are also finding it difficult to service these loans.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think for the latter, the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Bill, which was just introduced, should address some of these concerns.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But I hope that he relevant agencies can work together to address these areas of urgent concern.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As to my final area of worry, with the anticipated reductions in disposable incomes, I would also like to ask if more help can be extended to lessen out-of-pocket expenses for essential medical services.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Despite very generous Government subsidies, many Singaporeans still need to pay a portion of their medical expenses.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During this trying period, more families’ finances will be stretched.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hence, could I ask whether the Government would consider a temporary, extended liberalisation of MediSave for both outpatient and inpatient essential medical treatments, and also for ILTC expenses?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Now, this would not entail any immediate further expenditures for the Government.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While these subsidies are generous, again, due to the high costs of certain drugs, the balance costs borne by patients and their families can still be fairly significant.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to seek clarifications regarding MediShield Life premiums.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: All of us are behind you and thank you for your hard work.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Regarding our battle against SARS in the early 2000s, I recall a quote from the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew who said that: "We were united as one people", this was during SARS, "to protect the health and safety of everyone.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The experience bonded us as one people regardless of race, language and religion".

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This COVID-19 crisis, terrible as it is, offers us another chance to emerge stronger as one nation and one people, and stronger we will be.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And I would like to conclude with my support for this Budget.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: No one alive has seen a global pandemic of this scale, and none can accurately predict how the global economy will look like after the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This is why the Government is taking extraordinary steps in the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets to inject some certainty, some confidence into the economy and our society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore is very fortunate that the prudence and hard work of our forefathers and past governments have left us with public reserves to help us through the current phase of the crisis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This illustrates how important it is for a country to maintain healthy financial reserves and a strong economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The reserves also allow the Government to act quickly and decisively to support the people and the economy, which may not be achievable otherwise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: However, none can predict how long the crisis is going to last or how much of our reserves we will deplete.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans cannot tide through this crisis by relying on our public reserves alone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The strength of Singapore must lie in the willingness of our people to make the necessary sacrifices to protect the weakest among us from the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Globally, unemployment claims have risen at rates far exceeding those during the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Initial jobless claims in the United States for the week ending 28 March 2020 were over 6.6 million – an increase of about 30 times over the average rate the year before.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The jobless data, moreover, do not account for reduced hours, cut allowances, reductions in commissions and no business for the self-employed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, there are many Singaporeans in immediate need, and many more to come.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But because many measures are means tested to avoid waste, there is a real risk that Singaporeans will fall through the gaps.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The rapidly evolving effects of the pandemic also mean that our schemes, carefully designed as they are, may be one step behind the needs of the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: That is why we must now consider shifting our approach from means testing and gatekeeping public support, to ensuring that all Singaporeans, on a universal basis, have some basic income necessary to provide for their families in the months ahead.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But more than that, I want to call on the public to make a sacrifice to finance this scheme through a temporary increase in personal income taxes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If we truly believe that we are only as strong as the weakest member of our society, we must be prepared to pay the price necessary to protect that fellow Singaporean.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I have worked together with Dr Ong Qiyan from the Social Service Research Centre at the National University of Singapore, to produce a concrete proposal on this Universal Basic Income Scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We call this scheme the Majulah Universal Basic Income Scheme, or MUBI, for reasons that I will explain shortly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The MUBI Scheme’s key objective is to give all Singaporean households the certainty that they will be able to pay for basic necessities during these uncertain times.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: MUBI achieves this by giving all Singaporeans weekly cash payments without means testing, calibrated at the amount necessary to cover an average households’ cash expenditure on food, utilities, and telecommunications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The payout period can be extended at additional cost if the COVID-19 pandemic continues to severely disrupt the economy past these 12 weeks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But to ensure that the most help goes to those most in need, the payouts can be recorded as personal income, which will be taxable in the Year of Assessment 2021.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, the scheme’s net benefit to each Singaporean will eventually depend on the recipient’s taxable income in 2020 and their tax rate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, the key feature of MUBI is that all Singaporeans will receive payouts for daily living expenses immediately.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The MUBI payment will be larger than their expected increase in taxes next year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The median taxpayer will also benefit on net if they have Singapore citizen dependants, as the full MUBI payout will be given to children and seniors, who are generally not taxed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Taxpayers who suffer a sharp drop in income due to COVID-19 will benefit because their taxes could drop below what they receive in MUBI payouts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For solidarity, high-income taxpayers will be asked to contribute to financing MUBI, unless they suffer a significant income loss due to COVID-19 or have many dependants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In that case, then the tax structure ensures they will not pay much.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We call this the Majulah Universal Basic Income scheme for descriptive and symbolic reasons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In essence, MUBI will advance income from the future, when the economy and jobs are expected to recover, to the present, when it is needed the most.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But MUBI will also be a symbol of how Singapore comes together to ensure that those hit hardest by the crisis are provided with vital benefits in this time of need.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Through the tax system, more fortunate Singaporeans, who retain their earning capacity during the COVID-19 pandemic, will help less fortunate Singaporeans who suffer reductions in earnings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Incomes and jobs will be volatile over the next few months.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: A family that is financially secure today may not be so next month.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Means testing, moreover, is often based on lagging indicators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It may be based on income tax records, housing annual value and it may not reflect present finances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The effects of the COVID-19 pandemic are unpredictable, so it will be difficult to identify today which sectors, which jobs, will be affected the most, even though we know many people in aviation, tourism, retail and F&B, have already been hard hit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The universal approach will provide some assurance to everyone that there would be some income regardless of their circumstances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This approach is also equitable because many of our affected sectors have already made sacrifices to ensure the safety of other Singaporeans during this crisis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The certainty of having weekly payments to help put food on the table also means that Singaporeans will never feel pressured to choose between feeding their families and protecting public health.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This will help Singaporeans follow public health advice, especially if that advice may hurt their livelihoods.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For example, some Singaporeans provide essential home-based personal services such as home repairs and air-conditioning servicing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Not all will be confident they can protect their health and that of their customers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: MUBI will allow such Singaporeans and many others like them, to decide, based on the risks at the time, to reduce or halt their services, instead of getting more business just to feed their family.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We need to preserve the time of policymakers and social service agencies to assist Singaporeans affected by the COVID-19 pandemic in other ways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: When social workers have to navigate through different assistance schemes to find what is the eligible set of aids for each client, this takes up time and energy which could be better used for counselling and supporting clients.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Our social workers also need time to respond to emerging issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Social isolation measures in many countries have triggered an increase in family conflicts and violence, which may well occur in Singapore during this circuit breaker period.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Other social problems that may worsen include the social isolation of elderly Singaporeans and care-giver stress syndrome, as many daycare, support and respite services have shut down.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These issues require not only timely interventions, but a social service sector with the bandwidth to proactively identify potential problems and implement prophylactic measures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, policy-maker attention and time is a scarce resource.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The potential flashpoints caused by the rapid development of the pandemic and measures other countries take to control it, require extensive coordination, leadership and creative thinking to develop the optimal response.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: MUBI saves policy-makers' time and bandwidth as it requires less inter-agency coordination and limits fine tuning of the policy to one dimension – the payment amount.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We focused MUBI on the daily living expenses that receive less support from existing Government schemes, namely food, utilities and telecommunications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: While food is an obvious necessity, utilities will also cost more now that people spend longer hours at home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Telecommunications is also necessary, as work and learning must now take place online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Telecommunications also helps people to stay in touch with family and Government agencies; and provides basic home entertainment, which helps keep people at home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We did not include housing and medical expenses as these are already supported by other Government schemes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We did include utilities despite U-SAVE support because the costs could rise sharply if people work more from home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We looked at four expenditure categories: one, food and non-alcoholic beverages; two, hawker centres, food courts, coffee shops, canteens, kiosks and street vendors; three, utilities and other fuels; and four, telecommunication services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: To ensure that we covered vulnerable groups such as the elderly, we also referred to the 2019 Minimum Income Standards study led by Dr Ng Kok Hoe of the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But I am asking those who are fortunate enough to retain their incomes, to pay more the next year, to support those who cannot survive today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: You will only pay for MUBI, on a net basis, if you kept a high income throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: First, MUBI is progressive and it helps lower income taxpayers more.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, they keep about $1,120 of the MUBI payout once all taxes are paid.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For the median taxpayer, MUBI really just helps to bring their income forward to cover any short-term problems due to COVID-19.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But, if they have dependents, it will help even more.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: A high-income taxpayer will pay more in taxes than they receive in MUBI benefits.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If you earn about $110,000 a year, you will help pay for one and a half other Singaporeans to receive their MUBI benefit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, MUBI helps support households with dependents better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Third, MUBI gives automatic insurance against unexpected drops in personal income.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: A taxpayer keeps more and more of the benefits, the more their income is hurt by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: While means testing can help target social protection benefits to those who need it the most, means testing can be complex, administratively costly, and it may deter recipients from seeking and receiving the necessary help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The severe economic impact of the COVID-19 crisis will stretch social safety nets throughout the world to the breaking point.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Our means testing systems will be an expensive distraction for social services agencies and policy-makers at a time when the very structure of our economy and society is under threat.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Means testing also runs the risk of letting Singaporeans fall through the gaps, or asking Singaporeans to make impossible choices between protecting public health and earning a living.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
