text: The next sector that has been deeply affected by the COVID-19 crisis is the tourism industry.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The tourism industry is not just a sector that is important in its own right but it supports many other sectors of our economy as well.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Tourists contribute to retail, food and beverage, events and conventions, and it	even helps attract investors as well as companies who want to set up their businesses in a place with a worldwide audience.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Tourism also helps build connections for potential trade partners in the future and boosts Singapore’s standing on the international stage.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As such, supporting the tourism industry which has been greatly affected by this unexpected crisis is important; and therefore I welcome the enhanced support for the tourism industry in the Resilience Budget.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, we should try to go further – so that the money is made more productive, we should require tourism hotspots to consider seriously how they can make their attractions more safe, from a hygiene point of view, as well as improve user friendliness for their visitors.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will help ensure Singapore will be one of the first destinations tourists would want to return to in the aftermath of the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The third area I want to talk about is the rental of commercial properties.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Commercial tenants have been deeply affected by the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Even before the closure of non-essential businesses, these tenants in malls have suffered from lower footfall as people were encouraged to stay at home.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Safe distancing was understandably implemented to prevent overcrowding in malls and minimise the spread of the virus.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This has had a huge impact on retail and F&B business.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have been told that some of these tenants that some of these tenants are unable to secure a $100 in revenue a day, a sum too little to cover rental for a day.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In some places, landlords have not been prompt to pass on the rebate saving to their tenants, adopting a wait-and-see approach.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In my speech on the Unity Budget I had suggested	that we make the landlords of commercial spaces	more accountable, and suggested that they be required to fill up a declaration to IRAS as to whether they had passed on the property rebates to the tenant and if so, how much in dollar terms.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Indeed,	the bludgeoning few weeks since I gave that speech have caused me to form the view that we should go even further.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such prescriptive legislation ensures the money spent from our Budget is indeed stretched.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The fourth area that I want to speak about is supply chains.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In our globally connected economy, supply chains are	interwoven across countries and, with cities and countries under lockdown, global supply chains have been affected.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Many businesses especially with smaller margins	may not have enough liquidity and cash to survive through months of low revenue due to the crisis.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such risk-sharing initiatives are commendable, for they incentivise the injection of liquidity in the market.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Nonetheless, as these	loans are	administered by individual financial institutions and banks, the process for	sourcing	and	the	exercise	of	comparing	rates	and fees across banks can be complicated and time-consuming especially for those who are unfamiliar with business loans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will shorten the time needed to source for a loan, obtain the loan and the time needed to receive the much-needed monies from the loan.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is crucial to shorten and simplify the process as much as possible during this COVID-19 crisis because some businesses may not have the weeks needed to wait for the monies to be credited into their accounts.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such expediency will help the risk-sharing initiative better achieve its aim – that of swift injection of liquidity and the prompt availability of credit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As Singapore was still in the midst of the recession described as "a watershed in our economic development”, President Mr Wee Kim Wee in his Address to Parliament said, I quote, “When the recession eventually ends, as it must, we would have made another great stride towards realising our vision of a nation of excellence.” What we are facing today is different from the past in terms of extent, magnitude and nature, but all Singaporeans must have to count on each other.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Indeed, many Singaporeans are counting on us in this House to express clear, methodical, honest, rational thinking as we shape and pass policy into law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We must deliver that for Singaporeans we were elected to serve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: All these facets make up the essence of solidarity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The names of the Budgets are such an accurate description of what we want to instill – unity, resilience, solidarity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Just last Friday, four days ago, Mabel, a constituent in Ulu Pandan spoke with me at Meet-People-Session (MPS).

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mabel is caring for a young special needs child in her family.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: She is also helping her adult daughter recover from a hospital stay, and on top of that she is caring for her own mother who is aged.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yet, Mabel continues to want to get re-employed notwithstanding the present situation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Three days ago on Saturday, I met Adeline, a young adult in the Ghim Moh Hawker Centre.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In just the last five days, I have met different Singaporeans in completely	unochestrated settings who have reflected and	expressed the magnanimous traits of Solidarity, Unity and Resilience.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Will there be some friction along the way?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But as long as we gravitate towards a national ethos of unity, resilience and solidarity, and have the physical fire power to deploy further financial measures, if needed, then we would have earned Singapore a steady ballast to weather this storm.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, Sir, spending our country’s reserves cannot, and must not, be taken lightly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We owe it to the generations who built up these reserves and the generations not yet born to ensure that every dollar should be stretched to maximise its benefit to the industry and the worker it seeks to help.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Integrity and the ethos of stewardship in that spending process will achieve for us the objectives of unity, resilience and solidarity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But I choose to believe that we, as a people, have the	mettle to accomplish such a task, and that the camaraderie	that it will entrench will define Singapore’s character – as a nation full of fight, determination and grit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And that is a future worthy of our struggle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Seeing us all spaced out, a reflection of the times that we are facing – to overcome a crisis that will define this generation, our generation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Having spent the last few weeks engaging employers, workers and ordinary citizens, we can see the anxiety shows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For those whom I have met whose livelihoods have been affected, I thank them for their calm and their willingness to work with us to get through this crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many hope for the best, some plan for the worst.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With three Budgets in the space of two months – the Unity, the Resilience and the Solidarity Budgets – the leadership, care and concern of this Government shows as it prepares Singapore for the best, the worst and everything else that comes in between.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For the Ministry of Manpower, our priorities are clear – to Save Jobs, to Protect Our Workers and to Support Their Livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In these difficult times, we are especially concerned for those who are more vulnerable – our low-wage workers, the self-employed persons (SEPs) and our foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I will first address our efforts for self-employed persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many SEPs have seen their livelihoods badly affected amidst this COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SIRS will provide cash assistance to SEPs most in need quickly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want the cash assistance to reach our SEPs fast.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, we used the Workfare criteria as a starting point, and further expanded the criteria to cover almost double the number of SEPs as Workfare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hence, there is no need for most eligible SEPs to apply.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Eligible SEPs aged 37 and above who declared a positive net trade income to IRAS or CPFB for 2018 will be automatically notified via letter and SMS in end May 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They will receive the first payout automatically in end May, followed by July and October this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We know that some SEPs who do not qualify automatically are worried.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, SEPs who are aged 21 to 36 in 2020, but otherwise meet the criteria; and SEPs whose spouses earn a high income but have many people at home to support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: My colleagues and I will try our best to consider the applications of those who did not qualify automatically, particularly those aged 21 to 36 in 2020 but otherwise meet the criteria.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also seriously consider the appeals of those who narrowly missed the eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am also glad that NTUC Secretary-General has offered to front the application and appeals of SIRS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM will work with NTUC to provide details on how to apply, and how those who do not meet the SIRS criteria can appeal very soon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During this downturn, we want SEPs who have spare capacity to train and upskill themselves for the coming upturn.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To support them, we announced a new SEP Training Support Scheme (STSS) during COS last month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SEPs who take up any SkillsFuture Series courses and other selected training programmes can receive an hourly training allowance of $7.50 that will help defray their daily expenses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This was for a period of three months, and is on top of the substantial course fees subsidies of up to 90%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There is no cap to how much training SEPs can sign up for.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, a self-employed private hire car or bus driver who spends 10 full days of training in a month can receive $800 of training allowance that month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Applications have already started since 1 April 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SEPs can refer to NTUC’s website for more details.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We encourage all SEPs to tap on this training support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many, such as our cleaners and security officers, are critical to the provision of essential services during this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At Budget 2020, we announced that low-wage workers on Workfare will receive a Workfare Special Payment (WSP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They would receive an additional 20% of their Workfare payout for work done in 2019, with a minimum payment of $100.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: CPF Board will pay eligible Workfare recipients two payouts of $1,500 earlier, in July and October this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Eligible recipients will be notified and paid automatically by the CPF Board.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Lower wage workers will continue to receive additional support through the enhanced Workfare Income Supplement (WIS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The	qualifying	income	ceiling	and	maximum	annual payouts have both gone up since January 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More workers can benefit from greater Workfare support of up to $4,000 a year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In his speech yesterday, Member Pritam Singh spoke about adopting "living wage".

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In times like these, no "minimum wage" or "living wage" system can help low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When there is no work, there is no salary, there is no minimum wage to talk about when firms are unable to pay for their low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, Workfare is the reason why the Government can calibrate the 20% additional wage top-up and the $3,000 special payment, or any other wage support needed for later, for our low-wage workers who are vulnerable and who need our support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This, on top of Jobs Support Scheme that we are providing to companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, we complement the approach with the Progressive Wage Model for our cleaners, our security officers and landscape workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Unlike minimum wage or living wage, we take a multi-layered approach to support our low-wage workers, and which is effective especially in these times of need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As the impact on our economy deepens, more firms may close.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Short-Term Relief Fund today provides financial help to low-wage workers whose employers are unable to pay them wages due to financial difficulties or business failure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While we look out for our local workers, it is just as important that we take good care of our foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some Members highlighted the media coverage that conditions in the S11 Dormitory @ Punggol were poor.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM last inspected the dormitory on 4 March 2020 and found that the dormitory was clean and the conditions were found to be satisfactory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We acknowledge the challenges at the start to prepare the living areas for isolation while quarantine was going on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We appreciate the workers’ patience and cooperation, and will continue to improve the conditions for the residents of the dormitories.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Workers that had close contact with the confirmed cases have already been separately quarantined.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOH has also set up medical posts on-site to assess and treat workers who are unwell.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They will be relocated and housed separately from their usual room-mates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is an unprecedented incident that the Government is managing, and MOM officers and our partner NGO, the Migrant Workers' Centre, have been working round-the-clock with the dormitory operators and our partners to prioritise the well-being of workers who remain healthy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This includes ensuring the timely supply of food and stepping up hygiene management, as a result of extended hours of stay by the workers in the dormitories.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Minister Iswaran, Member of Parliament Murali and I visited Westlite Papan dormitory last weekend to assure our foreign workers that these heightened measures of safe distancing are to protect everyone and that we will do our best to work with employers to take care of their welfare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I had also visited Sungei Tengah Lodge dormitory on the same evening as MOH announced that a COVID-19 cluster was found in the dormitory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Understandably, they were anxious to know what arrangements would be made to protect them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Top of their concerns was whether they would continue to get paid.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Second, what measures will the dorms put in place to ensure their safety and protection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They too have families at home who depend on their salaries here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I strongly urge employers to pass the Budget support to their workers and help us to keep them cared for and motivated during this period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our self-employed persons, lower-wage workers and foreign workers play an important role in our economy and in building our nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In this uncertain period, it is important that we provide them with greater certainty and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The MOM will help them overcome this difficult period so that we can all emerge stronger after this crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   Last Friday, the Prime Minister spoke on the COVID-19 situation in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We had to make the difficult decision to implement additional safe distancing measures for one month to act as a "circuit breaker”.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The temporary closure of most workplaces, except for essential services and key economic sectors, takes effect today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We stand in solidarity with businesses and workers and will get through this together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our top priority is to protect the livelihoods of our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The enhanced Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) will help businesses retain and pay their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the assurance of the enhanced JSS, we urge businesses to communicate clearly to their employees on their work and pay arrangements for the next few weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As I shared in my English speech earlier, we will ensure that all vulnerable worker segments, such as self-employed persons (SEPs) and lower-wage workers, receive extensive support to tide through this period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SEP Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) will provide direct cash assistance to SEPs with less means and lack family support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We expect SIRS to automatically benefit about 100,000 SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SIRS will go to those SEPs most in need and there is no need for most SEPs to apply.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also support SEPs in their training efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The new SEP Training Support Scheme (STSS) provides a training allowance for SEPs who take up SkillsFuture courses and other selected training programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The STSS has been extended till the end of the year, and the hourly training allowance increased from $7.50 to $10 per hour, with effect from 1 May 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The advantage is that the SEP can enhance his skills while getting an allowance, during the downtime in this current economic climate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Workfare Income Supplement has also been enhanced, with increases in qualifying income ceiling and maximum annual payouts since January 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also strengthened relief for those whose employers cannot pay their salaries because of financial difficulties or business failure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together with immediate financial assistance from the Temporary Relief Fund, COVID-19 Support Grant, as well as other support from the enhanced Care and Support Package such as grocery vouchers, service and conservancy charges rebates (S&CC), we will support our SEPs and lower wage workers through this crisis together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There are those amongst us who may have difficulties getting a job in this challenging job market due to the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government understands their situation and help will be provided for those looking for employment in this difficult job market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government will actively facilitate the matching of jobseekers to firms who have immediate vacancies during this period, be it for a new job, or a second job to supplement income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In these unusual times when safe distancing is key, job fairs would have to take on different forms too – through the use of virtual technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The first SGUnited Virtual Career Fair is currently ongoing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have gotten good interest from employers and will keep building up the pool of jobs with jobs that are immediately available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The M3 network is also playing its part.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through two virtual career fairs hosted last March and April, MENDAKI SENSE has already received over 700 job applications and are further facilitating job placements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They also recently launched a dedicated helpline to help those who require assistance in navigating the online portal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI SENSE will also help job-seekers find employment through the CariKerja app and will continue to share information on available jobs identified through multiple channels and various initiatives, including those under the SGUnited Jobs initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI SENSE and other self-help groups are also working with government agencies, such as EDB and ESG to link job-seekers up with companies looking to fill vacancies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Among our jobseekers, we are particularly concerned about our graduating cohorts from ITE, our polytechnics and universities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is a tough time to enter the job market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These traineeships will help our ITE, polytechnic and university graduates – they are all first-time jobseekers – to further develop their skills professionally and further boost their employability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To better help our workers, we will need to support companies to overcome the immediate challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Apart from very significant support through the JSS, the Government will also help with other business costs and ease cash flow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, MOM will waive the foreign worker levies in April, and will also provide a one-off rebate of levies paid.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SMEs will be given three additional months to make foreign worker levy payments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Lastly, the Government will help businesses with access to credit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Partners such as our trade associations and chambers, also play critical roles in helping our Malay businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce & Industry (SMCCI) has set up a task force to explore how its members can better leverage on measures from the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They have set up an emergency hotline for members seeking targeted assistance and will organize engagement sessions to gain a better understanding on members’ concerns and to see how best SMCCI can help its members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SMCCI will also support its members in their engagements with stakeholders and landlords.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to pay particular attention to our SEPs as well as lower wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For those looking for employment, we will help facilitate their efforts in seeking employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Businesses and workers alike can take this time to adapt – businesses to transform and Singaporeans to further improve our skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We carry a heavy burden, but we will all bear them together, and emerge stronger from this experience.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: One of the things we worked on with colleagues was pandemic preparation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Among other things, we helped prepare and vet agreements for public health stockpiling efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And in 2008, we worked with then Minister for Health Khaw Boon Wan on amendments to the Infectious Diseases Act to ensure we had the tools to implement important public health measures to protect people and save lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is a very extensive and wide-ranging provision, requiring people to stay home, closing places, restricting movement, prohibiting events and gatherings, to stem the transmission of disease.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Minister Khaw said in Parliament in 2008 that, "invoking such a provision has serious implications as it will cause major disruptions to the businesses and the daily lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such a decision will not be taken lightly." He also said very clearly to the House that public health measures are not the role of just the Government but really involve every person and the entire community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I remember discussing with my colleagues then, as we were working on the drafts, that if we ever had to implement extensive safe distancing, it would be at a very critical juncture, and that it would only work if everyone understood the gravity of the measure and played his or her part.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are measures we prepare for but wish we would never need to use.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But here we are today, drawing on many of these measures as part of a major circuit breaker to keep Singaporeans safe and to save lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since the start of the COVID-19 outbreak, we have seen the severe impact it has had on ordinary people's lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Public health measures to "flatten the curve" are necessary, but they impose a huge toll on people – loss of jobs and livelihoods, uncertainty, social isolation, fear, psychological distress.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is the public health fight of our lifetime and my colleagues at MSF, ECDA, NCSS and in the social sector have stepped up to play our part in this wide-ranging battle.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These included tapping on existing schemes such as ComCare and the Courage Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we have also had to quickly roll out new support schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Temporary Relief Fund for April started last Wednesday and the COVID-19 Support Grant will start from May.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are making adjustments along the way in response to feedback as well as operational and situational constraints.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We seek your patience and understanding as my colleagues at the frontline are doing the best they can to help Singaporeans and residents in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I also thank all who have stepped forward to volunteer and donate.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In this exceptional time, we are encouraged by your generosity, spirit and support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, visiting our Social Service Offices (SSOs) and Community Centres (CCs), I have come across colleagues and volunteers who have been personally hard-hit by this crisis but who continue to soldier on to serve others who need help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I received a message last night from a couple.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They described how all their jobs and assignments had been abruptly cancelled and have had no income for some time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But their only ask is, "Since we will have no work for the foreseeable future, we would like to see how we can take this time to do something meaningful using the skills that we have to connect people, helping them to ease their fear and loneliness.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to help but don't know how we can go about doing it." There are many others who have stepped forward – silent heroes who are making a positive difference during this crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The economic impact of COVID-19 is wide-ranging, affecting many beyond the low-income.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ten days ago, the Deputy Prime Minister launched the Resilience Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under this Budget, MSF has put up two new schemes to help lower and middle income households, who have lost their jobs or a significant proportion of their incomes because of the crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are doing our best to process them quickly, accurately, and responsibly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With the latest circuit breaker measures, we anticipate that more will need help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also need to implement greater safe distancing measures, at our SSOs and CCs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Yesterday, thanks to our partnership with GovTech, we launched an online application system.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Applicants only need to fill up a short form, and attach some form of proof of income or job loss, such as a letter of retrenchment or payslips.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Those who have absolutely no documentation, can make a legal declaration on the form.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Those who had applied for TRF earlier and had given us their consent to be assessed for the COVID-19 Support Grant, do not need to put in a separate application.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They do not need to visit the SSO again and the SSO will contact them if they require further information.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For self-employed persons, MOM will also be implementing the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) from May.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In parallel, we are also adjusting existing schemes and processes to accommodate the dynamic situation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have simplified our ComCare processes for lower income households who qualify.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They can submit supporting documents even via email.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: SSO officers work with grassroots volunteers to provide practical support, for example, to elderly residents who are quarantined and need help to purchase groceries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Silver Generation Office has arranged for meal deliveries for seniors who live alone and have mobility issues and communicated COVID-19 precautionary measures to help keep them safe.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For Singaporeans who are homeless or rough sleeping, our Partners Engaging and Empowering Rough Sleepers (PEERS) network continues its work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With 28 partner organisations, Government departments, religious and secular organisations and uniform groups, they have been reaching out regularly and stepped up measures during this process.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During the crisis, some of our Safe Sound Sleeping Places have gone 24/7 to enable homeless persons and rough sleepers who need help to stay in shelter during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have seen an outpouring of support from companies, unions, volunteer groups, grassroots and religious groups.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many have also stepped forward in their personal capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have disbursed grants to a frontline worker who contracted the disease.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also reached out to family members of the others who passed on due to the virus and will be disbursing the support to some of them by this week.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a community, we also want to enhance our support to our social service agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This Fund will channel private donations to Social Service Agencies or SSAs, that deliver critical services to vulnerable groups in our community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The additional support will help our SSAs maintain their operations, make technology investments to better serve their users, and emerge stronger through this period.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF and NCSS will share more details on this fund soon.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition to financial support, NCSS is also working closely with our SSAs to help them with business continuity and technology adoption, so that those providing critical services can continue to do so remotely during this time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For those who are better off, individuals and families who do not need this cash payment from the Solidarity Budget, and are considering donating them, you can do so to families that you know who are in need or to one of these funds or to donate it to charities through Giving.sg.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Younger Singaporeans may not have encountered a crisis of this magnitude, while older Singaporeans are reminded of tough times early on in our history.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our daily routines have been sharply curtailed and many have had their livelihoods threatened.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such stressors and tensions, if prolonged, can have wider repercussions on relationships, marriages, families and communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This hotline will be manned by Government psychologists, counsellors and other trained personnel.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we would like to make a call for more support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If you are a registered professional – a psychologist or counsellor or trained to provide counselling on marital and family issues, please join us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some SSAs have already come forward, stepped forward to offer their professional resources, to come under this National CARE hotline umbrella, and we are grateful to them for stepping forward.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Already this crisis has taught us invaluable lessons – shown us areas that we will continue to work on, long after COVID-19 is over.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will take a hard look at these areas and also position ourselves to seize opportunities when the thunderstorm starts to clear.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: How we organise ourselves and support one another, use technology to stay connected, stay healthy, keep isolated if needed, but not lonely.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I am encouraged by many who have gone beyond the call of duty, and looked beyond their own interests and difficulties to help others: colleagues in our pre-schools and social service agencies, and volunteers who, at short notice, helped us to roll out new schemes on the ground to help large numbers of people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is our strength as a society and people, and we will get through this together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This test will be our legacy to the generations after us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Singaporeans are now grappling with the economic impact of the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many are facing the grim realities of pay cuts, job losses and business downturn.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Amidst these uncertainties, many are worried and naturally will ask – how long will this last, and how will I provide for my family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I will also highlight specific help measures for the Malay/Muslim community to help them get through these uncertain times.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Allow me to continue my speech in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Speaker, the Government is concerned for those who are badly affected by the economic slowdown due to the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This one-off assistance of $500 will at least provide immediate relief to their families’ daily needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, recipients will also be given employment assistance or training support, or both, from the WSG or e2i.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am moved and proud to see the community come together to contribute to the Courage Fund to help those affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This fund supports healthcare workers and those in the frontline.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This fund is also given to lower income households that lost their income because their family member was infected by COVID-19, had to be quarantined, or received the Stay at Home Notice or Leave of Absence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Lower income households can now apply for help from the Courage Fund at the Social Service Offices (SSOs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Details of the various schemes under the Courage Fund can be found at the National Council of Social Services’ (NCSS) website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MSF has also stepped up assistance for the low income group who are directly affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Social Service Offices (SSOs) have reached out to more than 6,400 Singaporeans who are quarantined or given the Stay at Home Notice, who may need ComCare, or other kinds of assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The SSOs also partner the grassroots to purchase or deliver groceries to those undergoing quarantine or given stay at home notice, but do not have any family, friends or neighbours who can help them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MSF has also simplified the application process for ComCare assistance, for those undergoing quarantine or stay at home notice, who need assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, these applicants can submit their supporting documents electronically by email.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Aside from measures to help those directly affected by COVID-19, we have also enhanced support for other groups who apply for ComCare financial assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Those who are eligible to receive the ComCare Short to Medium-Term Assistance will receive help for a longer period of at least 6 months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is meant to stabilise the family's financial situation, while their family members look for jobs or retraining opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During these trying times, it is important that we do whatever that is necessary to not only protect ourselves, but also those around us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The community must adapt to new social norms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This includes avoiding crowds and mass gatherings in order to stop the spread of COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those who plan to tie the knot in the coming months, we know that you are disappointed and may have to make several adjustments to your plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Therefore, ROMM will give fee exemptions to couples who wish to change and re-register their solemnisation dates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Affected couples can contact ROMM if they wish to change their solemnisation date due to COVID -19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While we work hard to stop the spread of COVID-19, we must ensure that our children's education is not affected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is important especially to students from lower income families who may now feel more pressure due to their families’ financial problems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Students who were previously ineligible for MENDAKI's Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy (TTFS) or its interest-free Study Loan, can now re-apply, if there are any changes to their family's income due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MENDAKI will also contact students who are receiving 50% or 75% subsidy for them to reapply for a higher subsidy, if there are changes to their families' income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are also ITE students who had to work part time to support themselves, but lost their jobs due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For such students, MENDAKI will provide financial assistance for three months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They will receive a $10 allowance for each per school day to pay for their transport and meal costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will hopefully ease the pressure on these students so that they can focus their attention towards their studies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Apart from ITE students, MENDAKI will also provide this allowance to students from the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHL) who are mentors to ITE students in MENDAKI's Empowerment Programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One lesson we learnt from COVID-19 is how we need to take care of one another and stand united.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I was heartened to see many Malay/Muslims coming forward to support Singapore’s effort to deal with COVID-19 and help those in need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I was pleased that AMP has announced its Temporary Assistance Package 2.0 or TAP 2.0 that costs $100,000 to help workers whose family income was affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Despite the many challenges that COVID-19 crisis has inflicted on our country, it has also shown our people’s caring side, and when we are united, no Singaporean will be left behind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It affects our source of income, our daily lives, the way we practice our religion and how we socialise with one another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, it will not rob us of our fighting spirit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Each individual plays an important part in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In fact simple things like taking care of our personal hygiene and having social responsibility are defences to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Let us ignite this fighting spirit, help those who are affected and stand as one in the battle against COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In tough times, we demonstrate our mettle and sensitivity." The Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets are apt testimonials of that truth.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The past few weeks have been a time of deep reflection for me.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: As one of the relatively younger members of this House, I was in my early teens during the SARS outbreak.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: When H1N1 came to the fore, I was serving my National Service.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Despite the anxiety, life did not grind to a halt in those days.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We did not have aeroplanes parked on runways, lives disrupted and humanity coming to a standstill as we are seeing today around the world.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I believe I speak for my generation when I say that COVID-19 has been a sobering experience and a reality check.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The fragile nature of life has been made manifest once again.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Seismic shifts labelled mildly as "new norms", are being charted.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I believe it is not going to be "business as usual" when "normal service resumes".

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Frankly, it can no longer be business as usual and this shall form the crux of what I am about to say.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Allow me to begin by highlighting three groups of people who, I believe, deserve our nation's gratitude.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: First, like all Members in this House, I express my deepest appreciation to our front-line workers.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: These are our doctors and nurses who work tirelessly round the clock to treat our people.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: These are our civil servants, policemen and soldiers who do contact tracing, manning our borders and to ensure the smooth delivery of services in these trying times.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Next, I ask this House to remember the foreign workers in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: During this difficult time, these heroes have chosen to be away from their families in order to fulfil our critical manpower needs.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: When Malaysia instituted the MCO, they came on such short notice that they had barely had time to pack and say goodbye to their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Three weeks ago, I met a lady who shared with me that she was working as a cleaner in Singapore and she left her four-month-old infant with her sister to come to Singapore overnight and to be here.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And they are our cleaners and construction workers, delivery riders, security guards and people who provide essential services.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Without them, our city would quite literally grind to a halt.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, I extend my appreciation to the citizens who have stepped up to assist in times of crisis – from the individuals who help to ensure that our workers have shelter to our drivers who are committed to transport our healthcare staff to and from their workplace.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, one encouraging trend is individuals mobilising to express their appreciation for the people around them.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Just yesterday, I am aware that the students in SMU Law School as well as other student groups sent care packages to our frontliners.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Our nation has set the “gold standard” not only in how we have dealt with this crisis, but also in how we have treated our people.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: This effort is only possible because of the dedicated service, immense sacrifice and the resolute single-mindedness of our people.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Next, I would like to focus on my second theme of fear, which I sense is an undercurrent permeating our society.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In these tumultuous times, our fellow Singaporeans are going through tremendous stress.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: First, our workers are understandably concerned about their livelihood.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: With the partial lockdown or circuit breaker measures in place, the drastic reduction in demand worldwide, many businesses will have little to no revenue in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Next, I will speak about the fears expressed by our VWOs and their beneficiaries.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Our VWOs are an important component of our social safety net.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: They ensure that our fellow Singaporeans who have fallen on hard times are clothed, fed and generally able to begin rebuilding their lives.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Other VWOs make it a point to befriend our elderly, bring them for their medical appointments and generally care for their needs.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: With the current economic downturn, many have expressed their worry at not being able to continue servicing their beneficiaries.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I wish to ask this House how do we intend to ensure that this crucial component of our social safety net does not disappear simply because of this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: While this sickness will eventually pass, I worry that a massive loss of capacity in this sector would leave us with yet another crisis on our hands.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly – this is a very personal concern for me – I fear for that the mental health of our fellow Singaporeans in these difficult times.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: People silently suffering in abusive households, struggling with unemployment or financial distress are the hardest hit in these trying times.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We are in this fight against COVID-19 for the long haul and building up the mental well-being of our society is critical in enabling us to respond with resilience.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I wonder if more can be done to ensure no one suffers in silence, to ensure that it is not just the vocal minority that are heard, but the silent majority as well.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: If properly managed, I believe that we will emerge stronger as a nation.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We can either “Forget Everything And Run” or “Face Everything And Rise”.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore DNA is all about the latter.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: This leads me to my final point on Hope.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Here, I am hopeful because COVID-19 is not just a challenge.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The circumstances today offer a perfect opportunity to consider what a future Singapore will look like.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure Members of this House are no doubt aware of the impact which the global shutting of businesses has had on the world.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: While the extent of Singapore’s pollution is not as severe, these examples highlight the destructive impact on our environment.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: COVID-19 presents us an opportunity to re-imagine our nation.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I urge this House to consider the potential of an economy which will not harm our grandchildren.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The old norms of doing business have quite literally disappeared overnight.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Telecommuting and flexi-work arrangements are no longer exclusive to fancy tech companies.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, they are a necessity in this climate.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that this House will consider how we will institutionalise this practice when we reignite our economy.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, I hope that we will consider the way we value each other.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I began my speech by thanking our healthcare heros.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: However, I wish to make clear that simple platitudes, or even clapping at 8.00 pm, is not enough.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I feel that the current system should be re-balanced to raise the salaries of workers in sectors absolutely critical to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Ultimately, I hope that this crisis reminds all of us how important steward leadership is.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: From our Prime Minister, to the Multi-Ministry Task Force, to fellow Singaporeans have shown us the brand of leadership that Singapore can deliver and truly deserves.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: To steal a line from the Officer’s Creed: I hope that we will always serve with such honour and integrity.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: This fight is far from over and each of us must act responsibly and stand resolute in overcoming COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond this House, I thank fellow Singaporeans for supporting our frontline workers and the many thoughtful perspectives shared with me and my team.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The battle against COVID-19 is entering a critical phase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we begin a period of tough pre-emptive restrictions to break the transmission chain and to head off the possibility of the outbreak escalating.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our livelihoods and our economy will be disrupted for a while, but we have to do this for our health, and the well-being of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Members have told me how the last two months have felt like a year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The latest circuit breaker measures have dominated our discussions so much.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With that as a backdrop, I will round up the debate by sharing my thoughts on this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, the nature of this crisis, and how it differs from past crises faced by Singapore and the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, what we must do now, even as we speak, to stay united and stay resilient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, how our people and our nation, can emerge stronger when the storm passes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lastly, I will conclude with some reflections on the critical importance of good governance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked what is the nature of this current crisis that we are facing now and how different it is from the past crises which Singapore has faced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Almost everyone in this House described the current crisis as “unprecedented”.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, COVID-19 has been unparalleled in its spread and impact on the medical, economic, financial and other fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is astounding how a microscopic, single-stranded RNA virus, of less than 200 nanometres in diameter, has wreaked such devastation around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Medical experts are divided on how long this crisis will last.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some hope that the distribution of COVID-19 outbreaks are displaying seasonal patterns, and that warmer weather could suppress the virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Or new ways are found to enable the quick detection of infection, minimise its spread and effect.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Others have cautioned that the virus could be cyclical.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even if its spread was slowed in the next few months, it could return in the form of a stronger variant when temperatures fall in autumn in the Northern Hemisphere.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global scientific community is racing to find a vaccine.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must therefore do our utmost now – take our circuit breaker measures very seriously, and minimise physical contact among ourselves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the economic front, even the most skilful and experienced forecasters have had to repeatedly revise their economic forecasts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The reality is that no one really knows how badly economies will be hurt and how long they will take to recover.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I was serving as Principal Private Secretary (PPS) to then Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew during the Asian Financial Crisis in 1997 and learnt much about the root and nature of the crisis from the many discussions that Senior Minister Lee and also at that time Prime Minister Goh had with global experts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And during the Global Financial Crisis, I was the Managing Director of MAS, at the frontline of a very severe meltdown in global financial markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Global Financial Crisis was different from the Asian Financial Crisis, as it originated from the financial system of the most advanced economies – in the US and EU.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It was so severe, and the financial system so interconnected that it brought down century-old banks in the US and Europe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Both crises were severe but the root causes were largely financial mismanagement, which were then amplified through an interconnected financial plumbing and the real economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This time round, the problem is much more complex.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Almost every country’s most urgent priority is to slow the outbreak of the virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the Asian and Global Crises, airlines were still flying, and many activities continued.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The sharp fall in aggregate demand this time is severe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Financial markets and the global economy today are far more integrated and interdependent than they were a decade ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global supply chain is much more integrated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Action by one country to contain the outbreak disrupts the global supply chain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The effect of the outbreak is a sharp reduction in global aggregate demand and a widespread disruption to the global supply chain, and this is sending shock waves across the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Furthermore, the political consensus in many advanced economies is fraying, making decisive responses and coordinated action much harder.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Globally, the situation will get worse before it gets better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But do not get me wrong – I am not a pessimist.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is hope that as the crisis deepens, people around the world will find the need to come together and be single-minded about winning this battle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Ong Teng Koon indicated yesterday, this is a global crisis that demands global cooperation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that multilateral institutions – the WHO, IMF, World Bank, as well as the G20, have stepped up to coordinate and manage the multiple dimensions of this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The world must come together and do its utmost to avert catastrophic consequences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For Singapore, we have to contribute our views and do our part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are not be a superpower with immense resources, but we should support multilateral institutions in their mission, help build global consensus and do what we can to get through this crisis collectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is feeling the full effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As an open and globally connected economy, we are deeply impacted by global economic shocks and the effects of border closures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our aviation industry, for example, is entirely international.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Extensive border closures has effectively brought the whole aviation sector to a standstill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The circuit breaker measures that kick in today will have a severe impact across the whole economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Until an effective vaccine or treatment is developed, our policies can only seek to mitigate the fall-out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is difficult to predict when this crisis will be over.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This means that we have to plan for the worst and work towards the best.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I shall now turn to the Government's priorities in tackling this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have to keep the rate of infection and transmission low.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we fail in this, our healthcare system will be overwhelmed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If overwhelmed, we will lose more lives, not just from COVID-19, but from other treatable conditions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must do all we can to support our frontline healthcare workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the more stringent the measures we put in place to keep the number of cases down, the bigger the impact on our economy, as several of you have pointed out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The alternative of allowing the virus to spread widely enough so that community develop herd immunity will cost too many lives and much more destruction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So let us act decisively now, accept the pain, protect lives, so that we have the strength and vitality to recover faster and thrive in the long-term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The economy is hit on so many fronts that it is not possible to just restore the status quo.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Moreover, as the most open economy in the world, injecting funds cannot counter the extensive global supply and demand shocks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our economy, we build resilience by ensuring that viable businesses are not permanently damaged, but instead, are able to preserve their capabilities to recover.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We support businesses with costs, cash flow and credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also help affected workers bounce back and to make the best use of this downtime.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our society, we support our people by saving jobs, providing cash support and easing their cash flow needs, especially of the most vulnerable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Ong Teng Koon mentioned, we are seeking to ensure that all of us pull through this together and that we leave no one behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
