text: When many people are out of a job, there is a major cost to our individual lives and to society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For individuals, this means depriving them of the chance to gain experience and grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Josephine Teo set this out well, when she shared why we started the SGUnited Traineeship Scheme for first time job-seekers and students who are graduating from our ITEs, Polytechnics and Universities as well as those returning from overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For companies, if workers are laid off, it means they will become less competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some Members have also asked if we can do more to help, such as Ms Yip Pin Xiu, for the sports sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Rest assured that we will continue to monitor the situation closely and do more, as and when we need to, to save jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can save more jobs, if we have more resilient firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help viable firms stay resilient, we have provided support for their cashflow, cost and credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For this support to work well, it is crucial that all do their part and I am glad many have done so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the cash flow front, the Government can provide the support through schemes such as the Jobs Support Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, the Jobs Support Scheme will fail if firms take a short-term view, pocket the payouts in one month and retrench their workers the next month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge businesses to take a longer term view – retain and upskill your workers to accelerate your transformation for the future economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the same vein, the National Wages Council with the support of the tripartite partners, has called for firms to reduce non-wage costs and tap Government support, before resorting to retrenchments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng and his union leaders emphasised repeatedly – firms should cut costs to save jobs and not cut jobs to save costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Otherwise, firms would have to start from scratch in re-hiring and retraining and may not be able to seize opportunities once the economy recovers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Sylvia Lim asked how we ensure employers receiving JSS payouts continue to retain workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Conversely, employers who had already done so before the announcements can still bring their workers back onto the payroll.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As long as you pay your employees wages and make the necessary CPF contributions, you will receive the corresponding JSS payouts for the relevant months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOM and the tripartite partners have released an advisory yesterday to guide employers on salary and leave arrangements that takes into consideration the substantial support from JSS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation closely with our tripartite partners and take action where needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked if we can flow the assistance to firms even more quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Agencies like CPF Board and IRAS have redoubled their efforts, working through nights and weekends, to expedite the payouts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Public Service is also working towards making faster payments to businesses supplying goods and services to the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage businesses that are in better financial positions, to consider making similar gestures for their suppliers, many of which are SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By keeping your supply chain intact, your company will also benefit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the cost front, I am heartened to see some property owners passing on the 100% Property Tax Rebate fully to their tenants, by reducing rentals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some property owners, such as Mapletree Commercial Trust, have even gone further, by giving their tenants more than the Property Tax Rebate that they receive, to share the burden during this time of uncertainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some property owners commented that such an obligation penalises them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But this move does not make property owners worse-off – in fact it staves off rental terminations and keeps their premises rented out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With a Property Tax Rebate of up to 100%, property owners pay less or even no property tax for the year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Property owners should pass the full tax savings on to their tenants, as the Property Tax Rebate is intended to benefit the tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Chef Willin Low put it, "Landlords and tenants need each other, like a garden and its plants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When times are good, the garden flourishes with flowers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is now time for landlords to help tenants so we can wait together for the sunshine to come again." With this move, I trust that all property owners will do your part, support your tenants and give additional help to tenants who need it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government is leading by example, by giving a rental waiver of up to three months for Government-owned properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the credit front, I enhanced financing support for enterprises in our Resilience Budget and introduced further enhancements yesterday to manage the uncertainty in April, as part of the Solidarity Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that MAS, together with financial institutions, has introduced a package of measures to help SMEs with temporary cash flow difficulties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a concern raised by a number of Members, including Mr Murali Pillai, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Ms Foo Mee Har and Prof Lim Sun Sun.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke about these measures in my Ministerial Statement yesterday.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad to see the industry step up and come together to support their customers through this difficult time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge businesses to use this support on the 3Cs – Cash, Cost and Credit, to keep things going, while they do a stock-take and make adjustments for what could be a prolonged downturn ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also urge businesses to use the support wisely and responsibly, even as we provide many forms of help in a broad-based manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Resilience Budget also focuses on building resilience in our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The best form of support is continued employment, both in the immediate and long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But if your livelihood is affected, we are here to help you through difficult times, to bounce back when conditions improve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For employees, beyond subsidising wages through the Jobs Support Scheme, we have also provided direct help for workers' training and upskilling, by enhancing course fee subsidies and absentee payroll.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For those who lose their jobs, we have stepped up our efforts to help workers find new jobs especially where there are emerging trends, such as through the SGUnited Jobs initiative, which Minister Josephine Teo spoke about yesterday.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For those who experience hardship, we also provide strong social support through new schemes such as the Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-19 Support Grant, as well as through existing schemes like ComCare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For self-employed persons, we will provide direct cash assistance through the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme, or SIRS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In implementing this new scheme, we have heard many suggestions such as that from Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Dennis Tan, to improve its auto-inclusion criteria.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also encourage all self-employed persons to make full use of the SEP Training Support Scheme to train and upskill, during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several Members like Mr Png Eng Huat, Mr Pritam Singh and Assoc Prof Walter Theseira have asked for the Government to relook our approach for support for our low-wage workers, especially during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our union Members of Parliament too, have been consistently championing the needs of our low-wage workers and actively working with the Government to uplift them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the right approach, because we need a combination of policies which work together, to shift the entire landscape of support for workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Progressive Wage Model and Workfare, which then-Labour Chief Lim Swee Say is a strong proponent of, have uplifted low-wage workers while keeping unemployment low.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every worker is assured that he can earn more wages through skills upgrading.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We continue to believe strongly in that, and have strengthened our SkillsFuture and Next Bound of SkillsFuture movements to allow for this continual progression.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have also heard Mr Henry Kwek's suggestions on sharpening this effort.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also ensure that our workers are treated fairly by their employers, through the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is made possible by the strong tripartite partnership, that can be a "viable flexible companion to the rigidity of law", as mentioned by Mr Douglas Foo.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This model has worked well for our society thus far, and has laid the foundation for good outcomes and trust between the Government, firms and workers over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In supporting our economy, we have sought to provide holistic, integrated support, while keeping an eye on the long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond subsidising wages, we gave firms the resources to re-engineer their business operations, digitalise, retrain workers and even temporarily redeploy workers in their downtime.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is so that they can emerge stronger once the economy recovers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SATS, Changi Airport's biggest ground handling and airline catering operator, is one good example.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I visited Changi Airport last week, I met several SATS employees who will be redeployed to the public and healthcare sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of them is Ms Neo Xin Yin, a Customer Service Agent, who will become an SG Clean Ambassador with the National Environment Agency.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Duty Manager Mr Yazid Izkhairol will be deployed to a public hospital as a care concierge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is our attempt at "making the perfect match", as called for by Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Christopher de Souza and Mr Henry Kwek, who also raised the idea of short-term job creation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The firm is also pushing ahead with R&D to improve its operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It uses an advanced 3D camera system to scan the dimensions and contents of incoming cargo, before optimising and packing them using a robotic arm system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is being piloted at Changi Airfreight Terminal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The aviation sector, including Singapore Airlines, is one of the hardest hit sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan spoke on the strategic value of the aviation centre to our position as a Global-Asia Node.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Despite being hit so hard, it has found strength, retained staff and pressed on with training and innovation, and volunteered to help others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Resilience Budget also provides support to increasing resilience in our supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last Wednesday, I visited Apollo Aquaculture Group and Max Koi Farm, saw what they had achieved and learnt about their plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In my Ministerial Statement on the Resilience Budget, I spoke about our efforts to deal with the immediate challenges, by having a robust, multi-pronged strategy to ensure a stable supply of safe food and essential items.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been working on this for years and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Masagos will provide details later this week.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank Mr Seah Kian Peng and his staff of the NTUC group, who have been working hard to keep shelves stocked.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is how we support a resilient society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Additional support is available through the Self-Help Groups and Community Development Councils.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Louis Ng and Mr Faisal Manap have requested to provide more cash in hand for different groups of Singaporeans and their families to tide through this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, we will already be providing more than what the Members have proposed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is from the Solidarity Payment, Care and Support Package and PAssion card top-up in cash.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the interim, those who require urgent help with basic living expenses can apply for cash assistance of $500 under the Temporary Relief Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MSF and HDB are also exercising greater flexibility under ComCare and for mortgage repayments respectively to provide stronger support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible self-employed persons will receive $9,000 over the same period under SIRS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I share Ms Foo Mee Har’s concern that some Singaporean families may have non-citizen members.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They currently do not benefit from the cash payouts under the Care and Support Package, but are supporting the family in different ways, through this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also extend this to LTVP+ holders, who are spouses of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With this set of schemes, we balance between targeting our support for those who need it more and flowing support quickly to large groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is not an easy balance and we will do our best to calibrate this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That said, I fully support the spirit of Assoc Prof Walter Theseira’s suggestion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Those who have more, should support those who have less.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such solidarity is especially needed in these difficult times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement, some of our support have to be broad-based, so that we can flow the support to our people quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage those who do not need the cash payouts to share it with those who need it more, by donating to Giving.sg or the Community Chest’s Courage Fund, or to directly share it with others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Pritam Singh noted that the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets have features of the New Deal in the US, and went on to ask if we can provide continued support beyond nine months, even after the pandemic subsides.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He made a comparison to the “New Deal”, and asked if we should have a "living wage" for our essential services workers, including cleaners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Singh himself pointed out, the "New Deal took more than six years and secured the US as a welfare state with a strong federal government and a perennial national debt problem".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He went on to say, "the comparison with the New Deal is nonetheless thought provoking".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While the New Deal was meant to bring the United States out of the Great Depression, its ideas have now polarised American society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We still see this schism today – between liberals who support it for its comprehensive relief and reform programmes, and conservatives who oppose it for being hostile to business and growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The United Kingdom went through a similar phase, with their government swinging between the left and right of the political spectrum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I was a student in the United Kingdom in the early 1980s, when Mrs Margaret Thatcher rode to electoral victory when ordinary Britons got fed up with the "Winter of Discontent" in 1978-1979 where there were widespread strikes in the public sector, including the NHS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a first-year student of Economics, we had to study economic history, and wrote essays on why the Industrial Revolution started in England.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, I had to do macroeconomics and wrote essays on why the British economy was then de-industrialising, and how economic growth was important for the welfare of workers, and did papers on sociology on class warfare in Britain then.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is important that in any policy making, we pay attention to the subtle but significant changes in the tone of society, in the attitudes of people and in relationships which will take years to show and which are not easy to reverse.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let me caution that in making good public policy, we should be rigorous and clear-headed and not rely on some ideological short-cuts or labels, without thinking deeply about interactions and longer term effects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our little red dot, we must have the courage and wisdom to do what is right for us – and not rely on simple ideology or fad or fashion of the day.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Focus on our people’s well-being, and design systems and support around that core purpose.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For this Government, it has never been a question of whether we “want to spend”.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Rather, it is a question of “how do we make the best use of resources to achieve the best outcome for our people”.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I said in my Round-up speech 39 days ago – and some Members might have forgotten – let me repeat: “There must be a role for the Government to redistribute resources, in the right way, so that everyone shares in the fruits of progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One way is to do this through schemes that enhance the capability of our people – through investments in education, health and the provision of housing, as well as schemes to mitigate inequality, like Workfare and Silver Support." I also said, "It is not just how much we spend, but how well we spend".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I showed various charts showing the outcomes we achieved, in comparison with other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we stay adaptable, we can keep adjusting our social security system according to the needs of the day.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the recent wave of digitalisation has brought great rewards to the innovators, but also put pressures on employment and wages for older workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have responded with social support schemes like the Workfare Income Supplement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help our people tide through immediate challenges in this crisis, we have been adaptable and introduced schemes like SIRS and the COVID-19 Support Grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let me urge all Members in this House to remain rigorous and clear-headed, and to focus on outcomes for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us commit to making sure that what we do are fiscally sustainable, not just in this term or next term of government, but for our future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to work hard at this and continue to look at improvements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And in the same vein, how artists could self-sustain and be well-prepared for the future, as mentioned by Mr Terence Ho.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Grace Fu has also shared more on what the Government will do to support this community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the spirit of SG Together, I am glad that many are stepping up to help others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The mayors and their five CDCs have stepped up local assistance schemes to support the heartlands and partnering local merchants to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These efforts bring warmth and direct assistance to those who need it most.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our charities, IPCs, and Self-Help Groups, have also come forward spontaneously to support Singaporeans in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened to see that The Community Foundation of Singapore has launched the Sayang Sayang Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fund aims to boost the morale of frontline healthcare workers with transport vouchers and some cash support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our schools transition to home-based learning as part of the circuit breaker measures, the Sayang Sayang Fund will also provide disadvantaged students with support for their meals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are many other heartwarming examples of individuals stepping forward, such as that of the provision shop giving out free rice to the needy, mentioned by Mr Vikram Nair.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singaporeans have also been helping one another, from distributing hand sanitisers, masks, and even meals, to those who need it more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some even offered their homes to Malaysian workers who were affected by the Movement Control Order.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans are also taking care of the seniors amongst us, a group that Ms Joan Pereira raised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Alice stays in a mature estate where there are many senior residents who have mobility issues, and these seniors faced trouble collecting their masks and hand sanitisers during the collection exercise in February.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Alice helped the residents with their collection and delivered to their homes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Alice also took the opportunity to chat with these residents and checked that they are doing fine during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are spontaneous acts of community support and I hope that they will inspire more to do the same.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the social cohesion and resilience that we must have.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on the nature of the crisis and how we must build resilience in our economy and our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several Members, like Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Douglas Foo, have raised this and asked how we can position ourselves better for recovery and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And Mr Mohamad Irshad had just spoken of hope.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, COVID-19 will re-shape our world and amplify the global structural shifts already underway.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With these shifts come risks as well as opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will accelerate structural shifts in the global supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Global and regional businesses will place a higher premium on locations that offer stability, reliability and effective governance in how they had managed this pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, trust will command a higher premium than ever.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has also accelerated digitalisation and the adoption of technology in our daily lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many more firms, workers and consumers have had the opportunity to embrace new models of remote working, online learning, telemedicine and e-commerce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will not automatically switch back to their previous habits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are in a good position to make the most of these opportunities in a post-COVID world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To do so, we will redouble our efforts to position Singapore as a Global-Asia Node of Technology, Innovation and Enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that even during this period, companies have continued to engage Singapore on new projects and the development of new capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also press on with our Smart Nation and R&D efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we will prepare our people for this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also continue to press on with business transformation and upskilling of our workers, even during this downtime, in fact, especially, during this downtime.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Douglas Foo, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling and Ms Tin Pei Ling stressed, businesses need to take the opportunity to transform now, as the post-COVID-19 landscape will be vastly different.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, Mr Douglas Foo astutely pointed out that had our businesses been further along the digitalisation curve prior to the outbreak, the transition to remote work arrangements and moving operations online would have been less painful and better executed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling has shared what we are doing to support firms with flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 fight still has a long way to go, and things will get tougher; it will get worse before they improve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But one way or another, eventually it will pass – not next week, not next month, but perhaps within a year or two.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Dr Lim Wee Kiak put it, it is an invisible threat, but it is not invincible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The question we should ask ourselves even now is when that day comes, what sort of world will it be and how ready Singapore will be to march forward again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should think ahead on how we can deepen economic and social resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I earlier announced that I would set up an Emerging Stronger Task Force under the ambit of the Future Economy Council, to help our economy bounce back from the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Desmond Lee and Mr Tan Chong Meng, Group CEO of PSA International, will co-chair this task force, to review how Singapore will stay economically resilient and build new sources of dynamism in a post-COVID world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This task force will report to the Future Economy Council and I hope that this can speak to Ms Rahayu Mahzam’s call for a coordinated effort to recover from the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Together Movement, led by Ministers Indranee Rajah and Desmond Lee, has been seeking to tap on the creative energies and commitment of Singaporeans, and friends of Singapore, to shape a better future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has reinforced the importance of social and psychological resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As President Halimah pointed out at the start of this session, the worst of times can bring out the best in our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How we respond to it, how our nation comes together, will show much about our values as a people and the principles we hold dear.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ministers Indranee and Desmond will mobilise Singaporeans to explore how we can deepen our social fabric and partnerships between Government and people in Singapore, and between Singaporeans and people around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be a whole-of-nation effort, which will take our collective energies and ideas to do well.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To do so, as I have mentioned before, we will have a series of national challenges across different domains to encourage ground-up participation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of the first challenges we will have is the "Singapore Together Stay Home for Singapore Challenge".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am asking all of us to be a part of it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These four weeks of circuit breaking will feel unusual and unnatural.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The challenge is to help ourselves and others stay home, and do so purposefully and positively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we stay home, how might we thrive, by staying healthy and learning?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How might we connect with our loved ones and the community?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be a time for reflection, to learn something new, bond with loved ones, to show care and support for one another, and do something active and constructive for the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are existing resources available to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, you can tap on online resources from the National Library Board and the National Heritage Board to learn new things and connect with your loved ones.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some Singaporeans will also be emotionally affected or distressed in this period, as pointed out by Mr Alex Yam, Mr Mohamed Irshad and Ms Anthea Ong.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If you need additional help, you can get help from various platforms, such as the National Care Hotline, or from our community partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are putting together some resources, and Ministers Desmond and Indranee will speak more about them soon.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are entering uncharted waters in the fight against the COVID-19 outbreak and we cannot predict with precision how long this will be.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But at this point, let me share some personal reflections with Members on what we need to pull through.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I presented the Unity Budget to this Chamber on 18 February.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Thirty-seven days later, on 26 March, I presented the Resilience Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The three Budgets make up our largest Budget in any one financial year, in dollar amount and as a percentage of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Ms Tin Pei Ling observed, this deficit alone is half of our total spending in the preceding financial year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We had to seek the President’s approval to draw on our past reserves, not once, but twice.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Once again, I thank the President for her deep understanding of the nature of this crisis, and for her support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank the Chairman and members of the Council of Presidential Advisers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Finance Minister, I am extremely grateful that we have been able to tap on the deep financial reserves – our current and past reserves which have been so carefully built up, invested and managed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has allowed us to respond to the crisis without having to borrow and without burdening our future generations with repayment obligations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But just exactly how deep are our reserves?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Pritam Singh has asked this question time and again in this House.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members would know that our reserves comprise assets invested by MAS, GIC and Temasek.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MAS and Temasek publish the size of the funds they invest.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small country without any natural resources and highly dependent on imports, our reserves are vital to our overall economic and financial stability and our well-being.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This move calmed our depositors and we did not have a single bank run during that very difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Having our reserves therefore played a key role in helping us emerge stronger from that crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It gives us the wherewithal to resolutely defend the Singapore dollar against speculative attacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This contributes to a stable Singapore dollar, which in turn bolsters the confidence of investor and citizens.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our reserves are thus no different from SAF's arsenal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No country’s armed forces will ever tell you exactly how much ammunition and weaponry they really have.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To do so is to betray valuable intelligence to potential adversaries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is obviously not a wise defence strategy and likewise should not be adopted for our financial reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: What Members should focus on are the policies and programmes, especially those which may require the use of reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Debate the merits of these programmes, including the expenditure required for them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But let us be clear – it is neither in the interest of Singapore or Singaporeans to repeatedly ask about the size of our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are in the middle of a storm and I am very disappointed that Mr Pritam Singh has used this occasion to raise this question again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Pritam Singh also asked how we will ensure sustainable finances in the next term of government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He suggested that we review our usage of past reserves in view of the longer term impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many have urged us, year after year, to spend more of our reserves to fund our growing expenditure, suggesting that we do not need to save so much or to ever raise taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But like Mr Liang Eng Hwa said, we kept the discipline and stuck to our principle of using the returns from our reserves in a prudent manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We do not view the reserves as a piggy bank to be broken at will, to provide the Government with a convenient source of additional revenue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We avoided running deficits in good years and consistently saved.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we had succumbed to the political pressure to spend more of our reserves in good years, we would not have had the war chest to deal with critical moments, such as now; and to do even more, if necessary, even in the next term of government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the aftermath of the COVID-19 outbreak will be with us for a long time and we will need to deal with it on a sustainable basis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we must make plans – and we are – at this hour, let us all focus our minds fully on making the best use of this very unprecedented Budget to build social and economic resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And if there is a need, we have the institution of the Government and the Elected President to decide on how best to use our resources to manage a crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, indeed, this crisis has reaffirmed the value of our key institutions and the key tenets of our prudent fiscal policy – to spend prudently, invest wisely and plan consistently for the long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond our financial reserves, I am grateful that we have been able to tap on the deep reserves of strength and resourcefulness of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Without the strength, resourcefulness, trust of our people, all the right measures will not be worth the dollar tag on them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But with these, our combined strength is worth so much more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our healthcare workers, Home Team officers, cleaners and many other unsung heroes have carried out their duties with commitment and courage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have to stay alert and careful while working long hours and over weekends.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is very moving that our people recognise this and pour out strong support for them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singaporeans have made videos and written letters of appreciation to spur our frontline workers – students and staff from Yew Tee Primary School, who made personalised cards and a video to show support and appreciation for the frontline staff of various hospitals and our Police officers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Just last week, applause rang across our heartlands at 8.00 pm on 30 March as Singaporeans came together to give those on the frontline a round of applause as part of our "Clap for #SGUnited" campaign.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This applause was also for everyone who has been helping to keep Singapore safe during this tough time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, our national stock of resilience is made up of all our individual stocks of resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, the long-drawn fight against the virus will be won by us standing together as one united people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Cases are creeping up and, as Mr Vikram Nair put it, we must each do our part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is absolutely serious – a matter of life and death.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has been an extremely hectic period for me, Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister Indranee Rajah, and all my Cabinet colleagues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am grateful to my staff in MOF, many of them young or with young families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have been working tirelessly for almost 10 weeks now – from Pongal, to Valentine's Day, to Chinese New Year, and over many weekends.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is the first time that MOF officers have had to prepare three Budgets within 48 days.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I know people like to call us at MOF bean-counters because we are always counting the costs and benefits of things.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We weigh up our reserves of strength, measure out the right actions to help our people and businesses, pace ourselves to go the distance and save for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We count to protect our people and our home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I could not have asked for a better team.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And I thank their families for their understanding.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: You should be very proud of your loved ones who are giving their everything in the Public Service.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank Members of the House who bring their honesty and resilience not only into this Chamber but also into our fight on all fronts against COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am especially heartened that fellow Singaporeans and Members of Parliament show strong values and commitment to our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After I announced the Resilience Budget, Ms Tan wrote to me, saying that she is touched that we are tapping into the reserves built up by earlier generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She then went on to urge that we must work to put back what we are going to use so that future generations have emergency funds for the next crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members such as Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Ms Tin Pei Ling have also come forward to urge us not to spend in an unbridled fashion from the reserves, even in today's situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, as we draw down on our reserves to tackle this generational crisis of unprecedented scale, we must uphold our responsibility to steward our reserves properly in our time for the benefit of our future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yesterday, Minister Khaw Boon Wan shared the story of his Primary 2 granddaughter who have been urging his wife and their helper to put on masks and to observe safe distancing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And less than 24 hours ago, when I was here in this Chamber delivering the Solidarity Budget, a young mother was at home watching it live together with her daughter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The mother later wrote to me saying that, afterwards, her daughter asked her, "Will Singapore become bankrupt?" I was surprised and glad that her daughter and Minister Khaw's granddaughter could understand such values at such a young age.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As adults, let us uphold our values and not let our children and future generations down.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is precisely for them that my team and I are determined to exercise fiscal discipline and prudence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The mother who wrote to me asked for an answer for her daughter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Spanish Flu occurred in 1918 and COVID-19, in 2019.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A hundred years from now, should there be another unprecedented crisis, will Singapore have the wherewithal to tackle it?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It depends critically on the values of our people, and I am grateful to Singaporeans like Ms Tan for reminding us all of our responsibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):   To deal with the COVID-19 outbreak, we announced three Budgets within a short span of two months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The purpose is to protect enterprises, protect jobs and secure our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is the gravest challenge for our generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The healthcare, economic and social fronts are interacting in complex ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is very hard to predict what is going to happen.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As such, we have introduced decisive and wide-ranging measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Because the outbreak is still evolving, we will make adjustments along the way, based on public feedback and as the situation develops.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has fiscal surplus and we also have the reserves to back us up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Here, I would like to express my gratitude to the President.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our reserves are like the trees planted by our ancestors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will do its best, but I hope that everyone will also do his part, mutually support each other to overcome this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the past two months, our healthcare workers, the Home Team and frontline workers have been working tirelessly around the clock to fight this virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We would like to thank them for their hard work and contributions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We keep emphasising these because these are important means to curb the spread of the virus and protect our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we unwittingly get infected and subsequently infect our family members and friends, causing them to lose their health or even life, then we will be left with only deep regrets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is relentless but there is warmth in society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Various charitable organisations, IPCs, self-help groups and volunteers have all extended a helping hand to people in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the ongoing outbreak, I hope that more Singaporeans can step forward and show that we care.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have built deep mutual trust between our leaders and the people over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: People trust the current Government, allowing us to implement measures to ensure their safety.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that Singaporeans will continue to work with the Government and strengthen the Singapore Spirit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to work on areas, such as research and development (R&D), economic transformation, skills training and improving social cohesion to prepare for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our pioneers have encountered many turbulences during nation building.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have toiled together to overcome various challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Similarly, this current crisis will have a profound impact on our generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So long as we stay united, protect our health, jobs, enterprises, livelihoods and secure our future, we will overcome this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When our children and grandchildren look back on this moment, they will see how this generation has stood United, Resilient, and in Solidarity to overcome this crisis together and emerged stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): I will now conclude in English.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have managed to weather this crisis so far because of our world-class healthcare system, our strong finances, our administrative capacity, our strong tripartite partnership and most importantly, our exceptional people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These require long-term planning, deliberate investment, stewardship of resources and careful build-up of capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is only possible because of the values that this Government and our people have upheld across generations, which has allowed us to fight the crisis from a position of strength.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are the values of discipline, prudence and long-term thinking.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The journey ahead to the end of this crisis will likely still be long and uncertain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But my team and I will continue to stay vigilant and partner Singaporeans and people around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Difficult decisions will need to be made during this period and so, we will do so with Singaporeans' interests at heart.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us stand united, resilient and in solidarity.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I just have a quick follow-up on the point he made about the reserves and why Singaporeans, including myself, keep asking questions in this House about those numbers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think, at the start, I have to make a point which is, the Opposition in this House is also is a steward.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We are also a steward of the reserves and the expenditure priorities of the Government because these things are something all of us have to take ownership of.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But we seek these numbers because when the Government introduces policies where reserves have to be employed, the question we have to ask ourselves is, is it enough or is it too much also, because that is a relevant question too.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think these are the reasons why some of these numbers, some of these issues keep coming up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Certainly not to make life difficult for the Ministry of Finance and its team in this moment.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I understand the Deputy Prime Minister has made the allusion to the SAF and you do not reveal your deep capabilities but I am pretty sure that we can nuance that position.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Two Budgets ago, I brought a Business Times article and showed it to the House; some Singaporeans were wondering whether you could look at some part of the reserves which could be used to improve conditions for Singaporeans, improve the livelihood of Singaporeans while there could be another component which may have to remain secret.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I recall Mr Singh asking, "Why not spend more?" This was debated in the House when the spending rules came about earlier on and when we increased the spending by including Temasek into the overall framework.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, Mr Singh can just check the number that we have been spending from NIRC over the years, and that would tell him how much we are spending.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Singh also alluded to whether there are proper checks and balances.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And certainly much better than the debts that have been incurred in so many other countries.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, let us do this carefully, Mr Singh.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, could I ask whether we can introduce a COVID-19 related childcare leave, specifically only for those workers who are in the essential work and the key economic sectors?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I also had a question about the foreign workers living in the dorms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am just wondering whether we can do the swab test, especially for those who have lived in close proximity to those who were infected.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think many are very worried that they are infected at this point.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And as I said, this Budget has been prepared in a record time.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, there will be details that the different Ministries will announce later and this will be sorted out by the different Ministries.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: This question is for the Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I just want to seek clarity on whether these two groups of Self-employed Person qualify for the COVID-19 Support Grant or SIRS.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Those SEPs who are not on the Workfare radar, who do not contribute to their CPF, but they do file their income tax returns.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The second group is SEP who are not on Workfare CPF or income tax radar, but they do have documented proof of their livelihood status.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And last but not least is there a contact point for these people to make an appeal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As the Deputy Prime Minister said, the Budget has been set up in record time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, there will be details that will be forthcoming and the good thing is that NTUC has volunteered to look into appeals and manage the appeals administration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, the email address and contact details hotline will be provided soon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the meantime, just hang on there and we will give you more details once ready.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The arts charities can also apply to the schemes under the Arts and Cultural Resilience Package including the Capability Development Scheme for the arts and the Digital Presentation Grant for the arts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They may also avail themselves of broad-based measures to support charities in general.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, they can apply for the VWOs-Charities Capability Fund (VCF) and obtain funding support of up to 80% to attend training courses and engage external consultants to improve key governance and management areas.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In view of the challenges presented by COVID-19, we recently expanded the VCF scope to include funding for online training courses, audio and video-conferencing tools and enhanced the funding quantum for charities who outsource their payroll, finance and accounting functions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There is no need for these charities to seek extension separately.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, Mr Louis Ng asked about the management of dorms and whether more can be done to test workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That includes taking steps to move out workers in some of these dorms to other areas so that we can better manage them, ensure compliance with all the safe-distancing measures within the dorms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And yes, it also includes stepping up of tests of workers in these dorms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, to Mr Louis Ng's specific question, we will be doing more to test the workers there as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Leon Perera also asked about the mask distribution exercise.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: He mentioned that the last time we did a surgical mask distribution exercise, he had asked whether it could be done through the mail and I had explained that we preferred for people to pick up at collection points because not everyone would need the masks and we wanted to conserve the masks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And so he said since this is now reusable masks, why not do it through mail rather than have people collect the masks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I would again like to clarify the task force did consider the different ways in which we can put out the masks to Singaporeans as quickly as possible and also safely.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When we changed and updated the guidance for masks, our priority was to ensure that the reusable masks could be released to Singaporeans quickly and safely.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If we were to do it through the mail system, actually it would have taken quite some time – maybe up to a week or more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we have a system in place through the collection points where people can come down to collect and we can put in place on the procedures for fast, efficient and safe collection.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So immediately upon the update of the guidance on mask on Friday, on Sunday the collection points were all activated nationwide.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: From experience, or look at what has happened so far.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The time they took to pick up the masks was very quick.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we again appreciate SAF, the PA and all our many volunteers who have been activated, who have stepped forward to enable this collection exercise to be done promptly and safely.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I appreciate it is technical and there is a lot of things going on at the same time, but I did raise a question for the Deputy Prime Minister in my speech.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, even though I asked the Deputy Prime Minister for a prescribed interest rate, given that there is so much help by the Government, I would just like to ask Deputy Prime Minister if you cannot give me a number, do you have the expectation given all this help that the bank should now be able to provide a much lower interest rate to help SMEs to tide over and not let them have unnecessary debt burden when they recover.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As to what the banks would do, as I have announced, the MAS has been getting the financial system together to provide a whole range of support including a Singapore dollar facility and the conditions for using the facility.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, this will take some time for them to sort it out.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But I believe that, as I said before, if we are in this together and it is in the interest of the banks to provide support for their lenders just as in the interest of landlords to provide the support.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: While at the same time, of course, adhering to the risk management that they have always been practising.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But this is an extraordinary time and I believe that this will be worked out between the banks, MAS and the borrowers.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I have a question and I do not know whether it should go to the Deputy Prime Minister, Minister Lawrence Wong or Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I mentioned that in my speech about my concerns for the rental flat communities in terms of the overcrowding, especially given how we have been alerted to the danger of infection with overcrowding in the clusters that we found in dormitories.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you are not sick, then it is all right, I mean, if you live together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But as so long as you start feeling unwell, even if it is a cough, sore throat, then you do not continue to interact even with your own family members; immediately go and see a doctor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And then, at that stage, you should self-isolate even from your own family members and take necessary precautions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If all the family members are feeling all right, then it is fine.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not as though they have to minimise interactions amongst themselves.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As a family, I am sure you will still be coming into contact.
